# Changelog

All notable changes to vike_trader_rust are recorded here.
Format loosely follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/); versioning is
[SemVer](https://semver.org/) — pre-1.0, a minor bump may include breaking changes.

Per-release notes are also auto-generated on GitHub (the PRs merged since the previous tag)
by `.github/workflows/release.yml`; this file is the curated human summary. Cut a release with
`just release-prep <X.Y.Z>` in the last candidate PR, then `just release <X.Y.Z>` (`docs/ops/release.md`).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.1.98] - 2026-10-31

### Changed

- **`vike-cli secrets set` drops ONE leading byte-order mark (U+FEFF) from a value read on stdin (`vike-cli`).** Windows PowerShell 5.1 on a UTF-8 console puts the mark in front of piped bytes, so a key piped from the PC (`just studio`, the builder-key carry) used to be stored with the mark inside it and then never matched the key it was meant to equal. A second or an interior mark stays, a value that is only the mark is empty and refused as before, and no message echoes the value.
- **A deposit no longer needs a human: under the default `quarantine` the reconcile pass adopts a venue cash INCREASE beyond the tolerance by itself, once, when nothing else is held for that account, its book is flat and the previous pass held the same figure (`vike-exec`, `vike-core`, `vike-tradehub`; owner ruling 2026-10-31, "who all the time will click manual?"; Option B of the decision record `docs/decisions/0179-a-pure-increase-of-free-balance-is-adopted-by-reconcile-under-quarantine.md`, which the owner ratified on 2026-10-31; offline-proved only: a deposit cannot be provoked on a demo account here).** Until now a deposit after the first sync was only held as a `BalanceDrift` until an operator ran `trade recon confirm`, and sizing and the margin check judged the smaller equity meanwhile. Now `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/reconcile.rs`'s `adopt_a_pure_balance_increase` folds the same cash adoption a confirm sends, announced ONCE at WARN (`cash reconcile ABSORBED an unexplained balance move`, with the amount) and once in the node's recent events (`absorbed +<amount> unexplained ... adopted as a deposit`). **A deposit lands one pass after it is first seen:** the first pass only holds it as a `BalanceDrift` row and the next, on exactly the same venue figure, adopts it and the row goes, so a funding payment or a closing fill that this node folds a moment after the venue credited it is never booked twice (review finding 1). **It waits for a flat book:** no open position and no working order, because cash a position causes (an IBKR short's proceeds, a perp figure with unrealized PnL) cannot be told from a deposit without a per-venue statement of what the figure means (review finding 2); a deposit that arrives beside an open position waits until the book is flat or an operator confirms the row. **It adopts only when the account has no position divergence and no `MissingFill`, `MissingTerminal`, `UnknownOrder` or `JournalDivergence`, raised by the pass or still held** (a position closed on the venue by someone else at a profit raises the cash too, and adopting it beside the phantom position would book the profit twice; this guard is wider than the record's, which named the position kinds only), and adopts it on the first pass where none stands. A DECREASE (a withdrawal, a liquidation) is held as before, the tolerance is not widened, and `hybrid`, `synthesize` and `external-quarantine` hold a deposit as before. The policy carries a new serde-default flag (`ReconPolicy::adopt_balance_increase`, set by the `quarantine` word alone and skipped from the journal when false), so the journal format stays as it is and a journal written before this rule replays as held; a restart's first pass is the ordinary first sync and does not announce the deposit again. Cold path only (the reconcile cadence): nothing on the per-message hop moved. The start line for `quarantine` now says so instead of "nothing auto-folds". Residuals (an external close the position fetch did not show, a transfer from an account you do not control) are the new row of `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`.
- **The four hub keys (the tradehub and datahub OBSERVE and CONTROL keys) are read from the `hub_key` table of the SQLite settings database and from no environment variable, in every client (`vike-cli`, `vike-desktop`, `vike-app-core`, the thin container, `vike-config`; decision 0111's verdict 5 amended in place, the owner's ruling of 2026-10-31: every key lives only as a row of the settings database).** `vike-cli trade`, `mcp` and `report` (the tradehub pair, CONTROL places orders) and every datahub-facing `vike-cli` arm used to read `VIKE_TRADEHUB_OBSERVE_KEY` / `VIKE_TRADEHUB_CONTROL_KEY` / `VIKE_DATAHUB_OBSERVE_KEY` / `VIKE_DATAHUB_CONTROL_KEY` from the process environment BEFORE the table; the desktop filled a missing observe key from the environment and resolved the datahub observe key from a variable named by the backend record (any name) before the table. All three rungs are deleted with no fallback and no migration, and the four names are `vike_config::REMOVED_ENV` rows: a process that still carries one refuses to start, names the `hub_key` table and never echoes the value. ⚠ **Who has to change something:** anyone who exported a hub key (a shell profile, an agent's MCP `env` block, a unit file, a `docker run -e`) must file it as a row instead (`vike-cli backend connect <host> --manual` on a client, `vike-cli secrets copy-hub-keys --from-settings-dir <DIR>` between projects) and remove the export; the thin-client container is now started with a mounted settings directory (`-v <project>:/project -e VIKE_SETTINGS_DIR=/project/settings`, `docs/ops/tradehub-container.md`) and `docker run -e VIKE_TRADEHUB_OBSERVE_KEY=...` is refused. The container's VNC password (`VIKE_THIN_VNC_PASSWORD`, stored with `x11vnc -storepasswd`, which put the password on argv and into a file) is removed rather than patched: publish the port to loopback only (`-p 127.0.0.1:6080:6080`) and reach it over an SSH tunnel; a stale variable is refused by the entrypoint. Studio's backtest key and the pager and Telegram values are not part of this change.

- **The Studio strategy builder's key lives only in the SQLite settings database, never in a file or a variable (`vike-strategy-builder`, `vike-studio`, `vike-desktop`, `vike-venues`, `vike-config`; decision 0083's question 2, answered by the owner on 2026-10-31: "all in the SQLite, not files").** It is a deployment row named `VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY`, filed with `vike-cli secrets set VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY` (the value on stdin, or `--from-env VAR`, never on the command line; journaled without the value) on each machine that uses it. The builder service reads it from its own box's store at start, one scoped read; the desktop's Studio reads it from the PC's own store through the credential map the desktop already loads. Nothing reads the key FILE (`settings/strategy-builder.key`, the shipped unit's `LoadCredential=` source) or the key VARIABLES (`VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY` as a variable, `VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY_FILE`) any more, and there is no fallback and no migration code: a missing key makes the service refuse to start and Studio's Build refuse before it dials, each naming the row and the one command. `just studio` no longer reads the key over ssh or hands it to the GUI (Studio's backtest key still travels that way); the container entrypoint asks the store for the row and skips the builder, loudly, when it is missing; the container image smoke files its throwaway key through the image's own `vike-cli`. ⚠ A box that runs the builder needs three steps in this order: file the key into its store, install a builder unit that lets the daemon see its database file (the shipped unit's jail hides `settings/`, and the unit still loads the old key file), then deploy; a builder started from this release under the shipped unit refuses to start, which fails the deploy's health check and rolls the release back.
- **The Studio strategy builder's key lives only in the SQLite settings database, never in a file or a variable (`vike-strategy-builder`, `vike-studio`, `vike-desktop`, `vike-venues`, `vike-config`; decision 0083's question 2, answered by the owner on 2026-10-31: "all in the SQLite, not files").** It is a deployment row named `VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY`, filed with `vike-cli secrets set VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY` (the value on stdin, or `--from-env VAR`, never on the command line; journaled without the value) on each machine that uses it. The builder service reads it from its own box's store at start, one scoped read; the desktop's Studio reads it from the PC's own store through the credential map the desktop already loads. Nothing reads the key FILE (`settings/strategy-builder.key`, the shipped unit's `LoadCredential=` source) or the key VARIABLES (`VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY` as a variable, `VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY_FILE`) any more, and there is no fallback and no migration code: a missing key makes the service refuse to start and Studio's Build refuse before it dials, each naming the row and the one command. `just studio` no longer reads the key over ssh or hands it to the GUI (Studio's backtest key still travels that way); the container entrypoint asks the store for the row and skips the builder, loudly, when it is missing; the container image smoke files its throwaway key through the image's own `vike-cli`. ⚠ The tracked builder unit (`deploy/vike-strategy-builder.service`) adds ONE line, a read-only bind of the settings database FILE into the unit's jail, and nothing else: it still carries the old `LoadCredential=` and key-file lines for one release, so it serves BOTH binaries and a failed deploy that rolls the binary back does not crash-loop the builder (the new binary ignores the file variable, the old one reads only it). The cost is plain: a strategy's `build.rs` runs as the same user and can now read every credential row in that file, and no narrower bind exists without a second file. A box that runs the builder needs three steps in this order: file the key into its store, install the tracked unit (a root-owned install; nothing is restarted), then deploy; a builder from this release under the PREVIOUS unit refuses to start, which fails the deploy's health check and rolls the release back. The two old lines and the old key file go one release later.
- **Studio's backtest key (the datahub CONTROL key Studio's Run signs with) lives only in the SQLite settings database of the PC, never in a variable: `just studio` files it as a row on a pipe (`vike-studio`, `vike-desktop`, `vike-venues`, `vike-config`; decision 0083's question 1, amended in place after the owner's ruling of 2026-10-31: "all in the SQLite, not files").** It is a deployment row named `VIKE_STUDIO_BACKTEST_KEY` (the name of the variable it replaces), admitted to `vike-cli secrets set` like the builder's; the desktop's Studio reads it from the credential map it already loads (`backtest_key_from_credentials`, the one resolver, still behind the opaque `BacktestKey`, one signing site and the data-plane refusal). It is NOT the platform `VIKE_DATAHUB_CONTROL_KEY` hub key, so no datahub dial and no `vike-cli datahub` verb on the PC asks for it. `scripts/studio.ps1` no longer reads the key into a variable or puts it in the GUI's environment: one line pipes the box's `vike-cli datahub control-key` (over ssh, unchanged: it still refuses a terminal) into this PC's `vike-cli secrets set VIKE_STUDIO_BACKTEST_KEY`, refreshed on every start so a rotation reaches the PC on its next launch, and the pipe runs under a byte-order-mark-free console input encoding (Windows PowerShell 5.1 on a UTF-8 console otherwise stores a mark inside the key). The variable is read by nothing and has no fallback; Studio's Run without the row is refused by a keyed backtesthub with a sentence naming the row and the command. ⚠ The PC needs a `vike-cli` built from this tree (an older one refuses the name) and the project's settings database to exist; the key now persists in that database file until `vike-cli secrets delete` removes it, where it used to exist only in the GUI's process for a session.

- **The silent-series pager's three values, the Databento key, the cTrader authorize tool's grant and the IBKR Client Portal login's second-factor code no longer pass through an environment variable or a file (`vike-datahub`, `vike-backfill`, `vike-ctrader`, `vike-cli`, `vike-config`; the owner's ruling of 2026-10-31: "every key lives only as a row of the SQLite settings database").** (1) The datahub recorder read `VIKE_ALERT_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, `VIKE_ALERT_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` and `VIKE_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` from the credential store and then laid its whole process environment OVER them, so a unit's `Environment=` or `EnvironmentFile=` (`<project>/.env`) won; the overlay is gone and the three are read from the store alone, set with `vike-cli secrets set NAME` (value on stdin) and a datahub restart (`docs/ops/recorder-deploy.md`, "Escalating it to a pager"; decision 0111 amended in place). the CI box's datahub unit carries no `EnvironmentFile` and its project `.env` holds no such line, so nothing changes there. (2) `databento_backfill` no longer falls back to a `DATABENTO_API_KEY` variable: the store is the only source, and the error names `vike-cli secrets set DATABENTO_API_KEY`. (3) `ctrader_authorize` writes the grant to the credential store and nowhere else: `--token-file`, the `ctrader_token.json` / `token.json` file and its writer are deleted, and it prints nothing derived from a token (it used to print the first six and last four characters of both, and the head of the one-time code); a refused store write leaves the grant nowhere, and the error says to run the browser flow again. A leftover `ctrader_token.json` is read by nothing and is the operator's to remove. `CTRADER_TOKEN_FILE` stays a refused variable, with the new wording. (4) The IBKR Client Portal login driver (`deploy/ibkr-cpapi/login.js`) no longer writes a screenshot of the filled form (`login-result-presubmit.png` is gone) and empties every input before its failure screenshot, and the second-factor code is read from the driver's STANDARD INPUT, one line, only when the gateway challenges for one, instead of the `IBKR_CP_2FA` variable (`vike-cli secrets ibkr-cp-login` now passes its stdin through; a service's stdin is `/dev/null`, so the unit sees no change). (5) The MCP agent transcript's redaction now also recognises every secret field of the venue key schemas, the hub keys and every deployment name the store accepts, by name (a funder address and a webhook URL have no credential shape), and a bare `PASSWORD=…` / `SECRET: …` in a free-text argument; a test plants one value per such name and finds none in the file.

- **The deploy helper's pre-flight no longer puts a live key on disk: its copy of the settings is built, not copied (`deploy/sbin/vike-trader-ci-deploy`, `scripts/deploy_sandbox.sh`; the 2026-10-31 key audit, row B12; the owner's ruling "all in the SQLite, not files"; offline-proved in the fake-systemd sandbox, NOT installed on any box).** Until now each of the five probes ran `cp -a` of the whole settings tree into a `mktemp -d` and booted a daemon on it: the store with every venue key and hub key, fourteen nightly copies of it under `db/backups/` and the builder's retired `strategy-builder.key` (measured on the CI box, names only), seventy-five copies of the store per deploy (five probes, fifteen files each). Now `probe_settings_copy` loads the store into `sqlite3 :memory:` (a consistent `.restore` snapshot, not a torn file copy), replaces every `credential` and `hub_key` value with a distinct `probe-<id>` placeholder, blanks the two `notes` columns, turns `secure_delete` on and compacts it before writing a file (a stale byte of a rotated or deleted key does not survive), and copies `state/` (the journal the trading daemon's probe replays) as before: nothing else of the tree is copied, and a copy it cannot clean refuses the probe. The rows stay, so the builder and the gateway still refuse a start without their key and a box that has not filed `VIKE_STRATEGY_BUILDER_KEY` fails the pre-flight by name before a byte is installed. The builder's key-file arm (`probe-key`, the throwaway file, two `confine` rows) is gone with the file it made. The helper is installed by hand and needs `sqlite3` on the box; a new gate (`deploy_layout_gate`'s `probe_copy`) holds the shape and requires every settings-store table to be cleaned or declared clean, and the sandbox's `probe-copy-no-secret` and `builder-probe-row` scenarios plant sentinel keys, residue and a retired key file and search what the probe was given.

### Fixed

- **A post-only LIMIT order priced through the book is refused at the door, by name, with both numbers, on every venue that has a post-only order (`vike-tradehub`; the post-only decision record, item 8).** A post-only order that would cross is a limit order that becomes a market order, and the node already refuses to place an order until it holds the venue's data, so the door now uses that data: a buy at or above the best ask, or a sell at or below the best bid, that the node's price tap last saw answers `post-only buy 77500 would cross the best ask 77400 (BTCUSDT on bybit): it would execute immediately as a taker; the order was NOT sent`, and nothing reaches the venue. Bybit and OKX accept such an order and cancel it within a millisecond, which the node recorded as a plain `CANCELED` with no reason; Binance, Deribit and Hyperliquid refused it themselves. One rule for all of them: a plain limit order is untouched, a `paper` book keeps its own check, a venue with no post-only order is still refused by its capability row, and with no two-sided quote or book held (only trade prints, nothing for a minute) the order goes to the venue as before. The tap now also keeps the best bid and ask each quote or book states (a pair of numbers inside the insert it already made); nothing is added to the core. Not covered: a strategy's own post-only order (it does not pass the door), and the refusal is the door's answer, not a typed `OrderRejected` cause. Proved offline against a real core and a real price tap; not live (the next release carries it).
- **An OKX mount, runtime or boot, now runs `on_bar`: the candle lane dialled a socket OKX serves no candles on (`vike-okx`).** The first live proof of the mount-works-by-candles-and-ticks rule mounted a do-nothing Rhai script at runtime on an OKX demo account: its `on_tick` ran nine times a second and its `on_bar` never ran in six one-minute closes. The core, the lane keeper and the datahub were not at fault (a runtime mount hears the closed bars of its own series, now pinned in `vike-core`'s tests); the OKX kline lane subscribed `candle<bar>` on the public socket, which answers it with a "wrong URL or channel" error and nothing else, and the shared driver retried that for ever without a journal line, so the seed arrived and no live bar ever did. The lane now dials the business socket, the one OKX serves the candle channels on (measured: the public socket errors for `candle1m` and `candle3m`, the business one sends a forming bar within a second, and the other OKX lanes answer on the public one). Proved at the venue and through the bridge's own `Feeds` by a new keyless `#[ignore]`d smoke, and offline by a pin on the lane's URL; NOT yet through a node, because it ships with the gatewayhub binary of the next release. No venue other than OKX was changed and nothing on the core's fold was touched.
- **Binance: a perpetual mount heard no bar and no real mark price, because the futures websocket path the bridge dialled no longer delivers them (`vike-binance`, `vike-aster` row; decision 0251, proposed).** Binance split its USDⓈ-M futures socket by stream class (changelog of 2026-03-05, legacy URLs decommissioned from 2026-04-23): the old `/ws/<stream>` path still accepts the connection and then delivers the public class only. Measured from the node's own address: the kline, mark-price and aggTrade streams delivered nothing on the old path and answered within a second on `/market` (the trade, book-ticker and depth streams were fine on both; the table is in the decision). The shared `UrlTable` now carries a market path and a public path with two doors (`market_ws`, `public_ws`); Binance's row is `/market` and `/public` (kline, mark price, aggTrade on the first; depth, book ticker and the trade stream on the second), aster's row leaves both empty because its own socket serves every stream on one path (measured), so aster's URLs are unchanged, and spot is untouched. The datahub lost no row: it records the BTCUSDT.P trade and depth tape only, which stayed live. The user-data stream of a live perpetual account is not changed and not measured (a known-limitations row). Offline: three lane tests against a loopback listener and the URL pins (red on the old layout); live: `crates/bridges/binance/tests/binance_perp_feed_smoke.rs` (keyless). Not deployed until the next release.
- **An account's engine refuses, by name, a symbol whose contract kind (linear or coin-margined) is not the kind of the symbol it was started on, so a Bybit demo order can no longer be filled by the venue and booked by nobody (`vike-tradehub`; decisions 0231 and 0233 amended).** The first live proof of the Bybit classes admitted the coin-margined `BTCUSD` and `BTCUSDZ26` into the linear `bybit#DEMO` engine; from then on the engine dropped the fill of every symbol with no row in its contract-value grid, so a dated linear future and a spot pair were filled at the venue and never booked, the journal said `DROPPED a fill on an instrument whose contract kind this inverse engine does not know`, and the node held reconcile rows for positions it did not know. The control door now answers the admission with the engine's kind, the symbol's kind, the consequence and the way out (a separate account mounted on that kind; one engine holding both is not built), for every venue, before any symbol slot is spent. Deribit keeps its own words. Nothing that worked is refused: a linear perpetual, a dated linear future and a spot pair on a linear engine, an inverse contract on an inverse engine, and a symbol an engine already trades (a restart restore) pass as before. A Bybit account therefore trades no coin-margined contract until a coin-margined mount or the mixed money model is built. The engine, the fold and the hot path are unchanged. Live proof needs the next deploy (the proof script is `bybitkind-refuses-the-other-kind.sh`).
- **OKX: a `demo` account's symbol facts are read from OKX's simulated-trading list, so the demo-only dated futures can be admitted (`vike-okx`, `vike-gatewayhub`; decision 0232 amended; offline-proved over a loopback server and two fixture lists, not run live).** The first live proof of v0.1.97 admitted and rested a spot pair on the demo account but refused every dated future (`QTUM-USDT-261106`, `EDGE1-USDT-261106`, `GRASS-USDT-261106`) with `no instrument ... in the venue's instrument list`: OKX serves the demo and mainnet from one host, the demo is the `x-simulated-trading: 1` header, and that header changes the list the public instruments endpoint answers (the demo lists twelve USDT-linear dated futures and far fewer swaps than mainnet, which lists no USDT-linear future today), while the node's facts had always been read from the mainnet list. Binance and Hyperliquid already followed the account's network; OKX now does the same: the asking account's tier picks the list, for the swap list and for the spot and dated one-symbol reads alike. A `live` account is read exactly as before (no header). A consequence: a demo account is no longer admitted a swap that only mainnet lists, in words that name the simulated-trading list. Nothing on the engine, the fold or the hot path changes; the fix is live with the next deploy (the proof script is `okxfactsdemo-dated-future.sh` of the next live-test kit).
- **`vike-cli trade unadmit` is refused at the door, by name, when an order of the account rests in the symbol (`vike-tradehub`; decision 0205 amended).** The first live proof of the verb (a labelled bybit demo account, one far order resting in the symbol) found the node answering "sent: the node queued the give-back" and only the engine refusing it, in its own log. The control session had never been handed any order for this verb, so the door's order check could not fire on ANY engine, labelled or not (the command line client prints no account on an order row, which read as a labelled-account mismatch; a labelled engine's published orders do name their account). The door now refuses a symbol with an order in it that has not ended (an armed conditional and a liquidated order included, as the engine counts them) with the account, the order's id and status and "cancel it first", and judges each account by its own orders: a second account holding no order in the same symbol is still queued. A bracket exit held off the venue and a core-held stop are published beside the orders, not in them, and the door still does not read them (the unfilled entry or the position they hang on refuses first; the core denies their fire for a symbol given back since). Door only: nothing in the fold or the hot hop changes. Offline-proven with tests that fail on the previous code; the live proof needs the next deploy.

## [0.1.97] - 2026-10-31

### Added

- **Binance: a TradFi perpetual and a dated USDⓈ-M future are now tradable, and a symbol the account never traded gets its first leverage (`vike-binance`, `vike-gatewayhub`, `vike-tradehub`; decision 0230, proposed; proved offline over the captured demo lists and on a lane through the real client against the demo account, not run on a deployed node).** `TSLAUSDT.P` and `XAUUSDT.P` (equity, commodity and currency perpetuals) join the picker and the symbol facts: they are linear USDT perpetuals on the same host and route as any `.P` symbol. A dated future is typed with its date and the same suffix, `BTCUSDT_261225.P`, from the command line (the door now accepts the underscore only with the suffix and says how to write a bare one); the facts refuse one that was delivered or delivers within a day, by name (the demo lists a weekly as TRADING months after its date). A `demo` account's facts now follow the demo futures host's own list, which is shorter than mainnet's. On the DEMO host only, the bridge writes the account's configured leverage (capped at the symbol's maximum) before the first order on a symbol that reads leverage 0 (the venue refused such a first order on any symbol with a low maximum, a TradFi equity above all), and signs the account's TradFi-Perps agreement at the first reject that names it (one POST; the order that met the reject is not resent); a live account is never written and its reject names the hand step. COIN-M symbols are refused by name with the contract's figures, an options symbol at the door; margin has no symbol of its own. What was measured and what is still owed (a funded COIN-M demo wallet): `docs/ops/trading-any-symbol.md`'s "Binance: TradFi perpetuals and dated futures".
- **IG: an index, a commodity, a coin and a bond future (dated or not) are admitted as a second epic on a `demo` account, not only a currency pair (`crates/bridges/ig`, decision 0227, proposed; admission and wire proved OFFLINE from 27 captured demo bodies, the price of the new classes through the node not yet run live).** A minimum deal of each was placed, read back and closed on the IG demo (Germany 40 in euros and in dollars, US 500 in two contract sizes, Wall Street, spot gold, Bitcoin and oil, and the dated Germany 40, gold, Treasury and Bund futures): the margin was `size x contractSize x level x marginFactor` and the profit `size x contractSize x the level move`, in the epic's own money, every time. The facts admit by the body (size in contracts, `contractSize` equal to `valueOfOnePip` times the scaling factor, one dealing currency, a level grid of one pip) behind a list of measured type words, because IG types Bitcoin and spot gold CURRENCIES; `lotSize` is no fence (USDJPY Mini, lot 100, is admitted). A dated contract is opened, worked and closed with its own `expiry` word. An index in euros or pounds on a USD account is rated through IG's EUR/USD or GBP/USD Mini on the converting door. A share (a measured minimum commission of 15 USD at each side, and no stream), an option and a spread-bet epic (HTTP 403 for a CFD login) stay refused, now with the measured reason. Not carried: IG's margin bands by size (the engine margins a large order at the base factor).
- **An OKX account trades a USDT-quoted SPOT pair (`ETH-USDT`) and a dated USDT-linear FUTURE (`ETH-USDT-261225`) besides its swaps (`vike-okx`, `vike-gatewayhub`, `vike-tradehub`; decision 0232, proposed; offline-proved and measured on the demo wire by hand, not yet placed through a node).** The class is read from the instrument's own id and held against the venue's row. A spot pair is admitted as a fully funded cash position, written as `cross` and, on exactly the refusal of an account level that needs it, once more as `cash`; a market order is sized in the base coin (without it the venue reads the size as the quote amount); a buy is booked net of the base-coin fee the venue takes; no spot position is reported to reconcile. A future is written like a swap and refused for an opening order inside its last day (the engine books no delivery). The private order channel and the stop channel are subscribed for every class, and a fill of a coin the operator trades by hand in the OKX app never reaches the engine. Refused by name, each with the demo measurement behind it: an inverse swap or future (it settles in the coin while the engine's ledger is USDT), an option, a USDC- or USD-settled contract and a spot pair quoted in another asset. The door spells all three shapes and refuses an option by name. The measurement smoke is `crates/bridges/okx/tests/okx_classes_measure_smoke.rs`.
- **Deribit: a dated future and a USDC-settled option can be traded from an account started on another instrument of its money model (`vike-deribit`, `vike-gatewayhub`, `vike-tradehub`; decision 0233, proposed; offline-proven, the live proof is written and not run).** An inverse account (an order is US dollars) takes the other inverse perpetuals and dated futures (`BTC-27NOV26`); a linear account (an order is the base coin) takes linear perpetuals and dated futures of its settlement coin (`BTC_USDC-27NOV26`) and USDC options (`BTC_USDC-27NOV26-80000-C`, a decimal strike keeps the venue's lower-case `d`). An option you add is held long only: its sale goes out reduce-only (the venue refuses a sale with nothing to close), because a long's premium is its whole risk and a short's margin is a multiple of it. The testnet measurement behind it (the account keeps one segregated wallet and margin per currency; what each class does on the wire) is `crates/bridges/deribit/tests/deribit_classes_testnet_smoke.rs`. A coin-settled option, a spot pair, a combo and the other money model are refused by name with the measured reason, and the record says which single change lifts each. A position the venue settles at its expiry is not folded: close it before.

### Fixed

- **Deribit: the reconcile of a LINEAR (USDC) perpetual or dated future read its position in dollars instead of coin (`vike-deribit`).** The venue's `size` of a linear contract is its quote notional (0.0001 BTC reads 7.68), and the reconcile client used it as the quantity, so a linear mount compared 7.68 with the engine's 0.0001. It now reads `size_currency` for a linear future and `size` for an inverse future and an option, as measured on the testnet.

### Not proven in the previous release (v0.1.96), stated here so it is not read as passed

- **Three live checks of v0.1.96 did not pass, and one that was open now has.** (1) The Dukascopy close in flight at a sidecar kill was INCONCLUSIVE in all four live attempts: the close filled before the killer fired, so the "the venue may have executed it" ending of that close (Dukascopy bridge only) is proven by the fake-sidecar restart test and not against the venue; a live proof needs a trigger faster than the close or a blocked venue network. (2) The the latency box latency A/B was not completed (four clean repetitions of sixty, disturbed by the release's own merge and prepare runs) and the owner skipped it for that release and the next; only the CI latency job passed. (3) A price-driven stop or take-profit fire on cTrader was not seen (the cTrader run closed through the market-exit path). The desktop client-id checklist, open in v0.1.96, PASSED live on the node on 2026-10-27: a new session's first order is no longer refused as a repeat. The same release's live proofs that did pass (the EUR latch base reading the wallet, the whole-bracket refusal on IG and Dukascopy, the FXCM, cTrader and Dukascopy demo runs) are in its own entries.
### Fixed

- **A resting Binance (and Aster) SPOT BUY limit order no longer raises a held `BalanceDrift` at the next reconcile pass (`crates/bridges/binance/src/family/recon.rs`'s `parse_spot_balance`, shared by both venues; nothing else changes).** The pass compared the node's wallet with the account's USDT `free` figure alone, but the venue moves the order's price times its quantity from `free` to `locked` while it rests, and the node's wallet is set from the user-data stream, which states `free + locked`. So every resting BUY above the cash tolerance read as unexplained cash (measured on the Binance spot demo: exactly the order's notional, for as long as it rested). The spot cash read is now the total, the same figure the stream and the perp lane's wallet balance already state; a real cash move is still reported. Proven on the venue: the order-lifecycle smoke reads the figure before, while a far BUY rests and after its cancel; it was red on the free-only parser (the figure fell by exactly the locked amount) and is green on the total (the figure did not move). Aster's spot lane gets the same figure through the same parser and the same stream mapper (it has no demo, so it was not run there). A resting SELL never touched this figure (it locks the base coin). The separate race that can hold an `OrphanLocalOrder` for a just-placed order is not part of this change.
- **IG: a reconcile pass no longer holds a `MissingFill` for every close the node sent, and the paged fills read follows IG's own next link (the IG bridge's reconcile client only; read-only measured on the demo gateway, offline-proved over captured rows, not yet proved on a deployed node).** The activity row of a CLOSE carries a new deal id that no confirm names, while the engine keys the close on the reference the close answered, so every close came back as a held divergence (booked a second time under `hybrid` or `synthesize`, which IG is kept away from): a close row is now keyed on that reference, after a restart too, and a close the book never folded (made in IG's own UI) is still held. IG writes the `from` of its own next link with the London offset of that date (`+01:00` in summer time) and then answers that link HTTP 400, written as it is and percent-encoded once, so an admitted epic's fills pass failed on any account with more than one page of activity; the link is now followed with the `from` the read opened with. A history that exactly fills its last page ends on an empty page, which the read takes as the end.
- **A reconcile pass raises no orphan row for an admitted symbol its client was not told about (`vike-exec`'s `recon::diff_scoped`, `vike-core`'s `CoreThread::unread_symbols`; the wave-two leftovers record, proposed; offline-proven, not run live).** The restore already held an order on such a symbol instead of retiring it; the same pass's diff still read the engine's local order or position there as absent at the venue and held an `OrphanLocalOrder` or `OrphanLocalPosition` row for what the client never fetched. The two local-side sweeps now skip exactly the symbols the restore holds; a pass that names no list sweeps as before. The venue-anchored legs (a fill, an order or a position the venue DOES report) are untouched, journal format unchanged, the fold untouched.
- **OKX: the reconcile client reports an admitted instrument's fill under the id the stream spells (`INSTID:tradeId`).** It reported the bare id, so every fill of a non-mounted instrument the stream had folded read as a `MissingFill` at the next pass: a held row per fill under `quarantine`, and a second booking of the fill under `hybrid` or `synthesize`. The mounted instrument keeps the bare id.
- **`vike-cli`: `trade position ls`, the REPL `positions` table, `trade doctor`'s position lines and `trade order stops` spell a size, a price, an unrealized figure and a stop's quantity and trigger without the float tail of an `n * step` product** (a Binance spot position read `0.000010000000000000026`); `--json` stays the engine's exact value.
- **Binance spot: a BNB-discounted fee on a pair quoted in USD1, USD, THB, IDR or U is valued through the BNB cross like the other quotes** (`QUOTES` lacked them; the fee stayed as stated and warned). RLUSD is listed ahead of USD so its pairs are not split as USD ones.
- **`vike-cli trade recon cancel <id>` now reaches an order resting on an admitted symbol that is not the mounted one (binance, bybit, okx; `vike-core`'s cold `cancel_recon_order` and `confirm_recon`, no bridge, `vike-exec` or `vike-model` change, hot hop untouched).** The verb sends the cancel for the client id its held `UnknownOrder` row prints, but a per-symbol router bridge learns an order's symbol only from its own submit or from `ExecutionClient::adopt_restored`, so it sent the cancel to the MOUNTED symbol, read the venue's "unknown order" there as already gone, and the node said SENT while the order kept resting and the row stayed. The core now tells the client the row's symbol first (read off the row's own identity text; the same call after an operator's confirm of a journal-recovery alert re-registers an order), only for a venue whose restore is open and whose reports echo our client id: Hyperliquid's row prints the venue's hashed id, which the call would make its bridge hash twice, and a venue whose restore is off (ibkr, oanda, aster) is left as it was. Offline-proven with a router model over a fake venue book; not yet run against a live venue.

### Added

- **The IBKR stock price lane survives a gateway drop (decision 0220, proposed; the cause is read from the journal of 2026-10-28 and from one read-only probe of the paper gateway, the fix is offline-proven and not yet proven on a node).** Two silent faults left the node pricing no stock but its own for two days after a drop of the IB Gateway: a quote stream IB ended with "no market data during a competing live session" was a refused request, not a dead connection, so its pump exited and nothing re-subscribed it; and a data connection that `ibapi` rebuilt by itself is a new gateway session whose market-data type is the real-time default, so every later subscribe ended "not subscribed" on a delayed-only account (measured: the same connection streams delayed ticks 0.3 s after it sends the delayed type). The quote pump now sends the market-data type again before every subscribe (every facts ask does too), re-opens a stream IB ends on a data refusal after 5 s, then 60 s, 2 min and 5 min, discloses the gap from the second refusal (so the order refusal says the stream is DOWN instead of "retry in a moment") and logs why in words. A competing login that stays keeps the lane down with those words, and the link dead-man treats the disclosed gap as it does any stream a venue closed.
- **An IBKR stock's grid tick is the increment of the band its price falls in, never the coarsest band (decision 0220, proposed; found live: `SAP.SMART.EUR` came back with a tick of 10.0, the band from 50000 EUR of IB's market rule, which would have rounded a 213 EUR limit to a multiple of 10).** The facts read a delayed or closing price on the ask's connection (4 s at most) and take the increment of its band (0.05 for SAP between 200 and 500; the coarsest of the contract's rules at that price when it names several), the finest increment when no price comes, and the exec refuses a limit or trigger price that is on the grid of no rule at its own price, naming IB's real increment. Offline-proven over the market rule captured from the paper gateway; a price that crosses a band edge after the ask trades on the old tick until the facts are read again.
- **A strategy can rest a REDUCE-ONLY stop: `LiveBroker::submit_stop_reduce` (live) and `SimBroker::submit_stop_reduce` (backtest), so a stop that fires after its position was closed another way opens nothing (`vike-core`, `vike-sim`, `vike-model`; Rust strategies only; journal format unchanged; offline-proven, not run on a venue).** `submit_stop` stays the core's own plain market, which opens a position when its position is already gone. The new live verb is an ORDER and goes through the operator's `--type stop --reduce-only` lane: a venue whose capability row takes a reduce-only stop rests a native one owned by the strategy, a row that refuses it (IG, Polymarket) has the node hold it as the strategy's own (a reduce-only market of at most the live position when it crosses, or nothing, `CORE-HELD STOP <id> armed: ... Armed by the strategy mount ...` on the recent events), and a refusal reaches the strategy as an `OrderRejected` in the capability words. The strategy is told nothing when the node holds its stop; it clears it with its own mass cancel. No journal key was added: the record is a strategy submit of a stop `Submit` plus the existing reduce-only arm. In the backtest the stop is refused at once in words on a flat book or the position's own side, capped to the position, and dropped (never opened) when its position was closed another way; the flag is a new defaulted field of `WorkingOrder`, absent from every fixture. The paper book still reads no flag, so a strategy's reduce-only stop on a paper account fires plain. Not built: a reduce-only trailing stop or stop-limit verb, and any call from the Rhai or plugin hosts. Decision record proposed; `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` has the new row.
- **IBKR: a forex pair (`EUR.USD.IDEALPRO`) and a dated cash-settled index future (`ES.CME.USD.FUT.20261218`) are admitted by name; an option is refused by name with its design written down (decision 0234, proposed; the venue half measured live on the paper account, the node's path offline-proved only).** The paper account answered the contract details, market rules, what-if margins and delayed quotes of EUR.USD, USD.JPY, GBP.USD, ES, MES, NQ, MNQ and CL, and filled minimum round trips of EUR.USD, USD.JPY and MES (`crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/tests/ibkr_forex_futures_probe.rs`, an `#[ignore]`d paper probe); the answers are the fixtures of `any_symbol_forex_future`'s suite. A pair is a linear instrument in units of its base currency with the IdealPro minimum the venue's own warning states; a future needs a cash-settled root, the venue's exact name and five days to its last trading day, and carries the multiplier and the what-if margin rate. The reconcile client withholds the account's cash figure while the engine holds either (the USD cash row falls by a pair's whole notional). Measured, and corrected in the docs: the paper session streams NO API forex quote (error 10089), so a pair is admitted and cannot be priced there; futures stream delayed.
- **IBKR: a commission that arrives AFTER its fill, or that IB revises, is now booked into the account once (`Event::FeeAdjustment`, a new event kind: `vike-model`, `vike-exec`, `vike-core`, `vike-ibkr`, `vike-journal`; decision 0238, proposed; offline-proven, not run on a node).** A fill booked with its fee unknown (a cancel that outran the `commissionReport`: 0.0 and no fee currency, about 1 USD short per such order) used to keep that fee for good, and a corrected commission for an execution already reported was dropped, because a second fill with another fee reads as a duplicate. The bridge now sends the total over the fill's own fee, keyed by the fill's trade id; the engine books the difference into `balance`, `fees_paid`, `fees_by_asset` and the mount's ledger exactly as a fill's fee, remembers what it booked (in the snapshot, absent until a fee is corrected), and books the same figure once: a repeat books nothing, a changed total books the change. It rides the existing journal record as a new event tag with no format step, so an older journal replays unchanged and a build older than the tag cannot read a journal that carries one (the rollback note is in `docs/ops/tradehub-the CI box.md`); the tearsheet read folds the corrections into the fills they restate. The fill ladder is unchanged. Not closed: the datahub's stored fill rows keep the fill's own fee.
- **Dukascopy now has a reconcile leg: the JForex sidecar answers what the venue lists, and the node compares its books with it at every pass (Dukascopy bridge, its Java sidecar and the wiring table; needs the jar of the release that carries it).** The sidecar understands a new `recon` command and answers ONE line: every order the venue lists (resting or filled, with its client order id, amounts, open price, stop-loss and take-profit price) and the net position per instrument, read from `engine.getOrders()` at the moment of the question. The reconcile client pulls it three times per pass (orders, fills, positions) instead of reading the last pushed `position` line, which kept the node's own belief when the venue had closed a position unheard: a position the node holds and the venue does not now reads FLAT, and the default `quarantine` holds it for the operator as a `PositionDrift` (nothing is written). The node's native stop-loss and take-profit are reported while the venue still holds their price. An answer that could not be read, never came, or came from a jar that cannot give one is an ERROR on every read and an `error` log line, never "no orders". The node is handed the client only when reconciliation is on and the jar announces `recon`; with an older jar the venue reconciles nothing, as before. The wiring class `SidecarExecNoRecon` is now `SidecarExecRecon` (the published `wiring` string in `venues.json` is `sidecar-exec-recon`). Not changed: the policy stays `quarantine` and `hybrid`/`synthesize` stay refused for this venue until its position report is live-proven complete; no balance leg; closed orders are not reported (the venue's history cannot name who closed them). The live proof is written for the demo account and cannot run before the deploy. The record is `docs/decisions/0235-dukascopy-reconciles-by-asking-the-sidecar-what-the-venue-lists.md`; the operator's page is `crates/bridges/dukascopy/CLAUDE.md`'s "The reconcile leg: the sidecar answers what the venue lists".
- **FXCM trades its metals, indices, commodities, treasuries, FX indices, share CFDs and crypto CFDs, not only forex pairs (`vike-fxcm`, the shim, `vike-gatewayhub`'s `fxcm_rate`; decision 0229, proposed; offline-proven against the venue's own table, NOT yet traded live).** The whole Offers table of the EUR demo was read live (Friday 2026-10-30, the FX week open): the class of a row is its SDK `InstrumentType`, never its name; a CFD is quoted in its `ContractCurrency`, sized in base units within the venue's own smallest and largest order, and one unit of quantity is its `ContractMultiplier` (carried on the wire's existing `contract_value`; a margin rate only when the venue states one, which the demo does not yet). The engine's spelling finds the venue's row (`USOIL` finds `USOil`, `COPPER` finds `Copper`, `NVDA.EXT` finds `NVDA.ext`) and the shim resolves the venue's own spelling at every entry point and subscribes every class. The price lane prices them all. A crypto quoted in BTC is refused by name; a CFD needs the shim of this release. The money of a contract is a hypothesis until `fxcmclasses-roundtrip.sh` (one minimum round trip per class, the venue's balance against `(close - open) * quantity * multiplier * rate`) runs at the next FX open. `docs/ops/fxcm-forexconnect.md`'s "Metals, indices and CFDs".

### Fixed

- **The FXCM shim did not compile against the staged SDK, and the next release's required shim build would have failed.** The previous wave read `getNetPL()` from a closed-trade row (`IO2GClosedTradeRow`), a method only the Table Manager's row has. The fill envelope no longer carries `net_pl`; the rollover sign check, which compared it with the gross figure, stays in the code and is inert until a net figure exists (it could only be computed from the same row's numbers, which confirm any sign). No booking changes.

### Added

- **A Bybit account trades a dated linear future, a coin-margined (inverse) perpetual or dated future and a SPOT pair, each in the V5 book the venue's own row names (decision 0231, proposed; offline-proven on rows captured from the Bybit demo host on 2026-10-30, not yet run through a deployed node).** Before, the bybit door admitted linear perpetuals only and refused every other class by name. Now a client signs in ONE `category` taken from the row's `contractType` (a cancel or a status query, which fetch no row, take it from the symbol's name or are not built: a cancel in the wrong book would be swallowed as "already gone"). A spot pair is written `DOGEUSDT.S` (the bare name is still the perpetual of that name); its market orders state the base unit (the venue reads a market buy's quantity as quote currency otherwise), a buy is booked net of the fee the venue charges in the base coin, the price lane dials the spot socket, a stop on a pair is refused whole and a pair has no leverage. A coin-margined contract carries the inverse contract value, and on a DEMO account its settlement coin is switched on as collateral before the first order (the venue answers 110101 otherwise; a live account is told which coin to switch on). A dated future is refused within a day of its delivery. Options stay refused by name (the demo takes the order; the engine has no option payoff model). Also fixes a latent trap: the private stream's `execution` topic carries every book of the account, and a spot fill of the account (an operator's, from Bybit's own app) was folded into the same-named perpetual's position; it now keeps its own symbol. Live proof of the new code needs the next deploy (the proof script is `bybitclasses-classes.sh`).
- **Every mount works by candles AND by ticks (`vike-tradehub`, `vike-script`, `vike-cli`; decision 0245, proposed; proved offline, not run live; nothing on the core's fold changed).** A strategy mounted at runtime (`vike-cli trade strategy mount`, or brought back from the topology sidecar at a start) started no feed: it heard a quote only if a boot mount happened to feed its symbol and a bar only if one fed its interval. The tradehub's lane keeper now holds the tick lane of every published mount's engine and opens every published mount's bar series from the datahub's strategy lane, within one keeper tick of the mount appearing (a `paper` engine's runtime mount, and a venue with no bar lane of its own, keep what they had; the refusal is said once). A mount on a LABELLED account (boot or runtime), whose price board was written at its bar closes only (the core hands quotes to the default account's engine), is now marked by the tap's throttled mark, which stands aside while the venue states its own, so the 30-second risk clock no longer skips it as stale. A Rhai script may define a zero-argument `fn on_tick()`, run on a live quote at most ten times a second with the reads and verbs `on_bar` has; a script without it, and every backtest on bars, are unchanged. A text gate (`mount_tick_lane_pin`) keeps any mounted venue arm from being bar-only. OANDA's stream ceiling stays the one path on which a mount runs on candles alone (said at `warn`).
### Added

- **One amend changes a resting stop or limit order, in place where the venue can and by cancel-then-new where it cannot, and a failed amend leaves the old order standing and says why (`vike-venues`' `venue_amend_mode`, `vike-exec`'s `amend`, `vike-core`'s `apply/amend.rs`, `vike-model`'s `ManagedOrder::replaces`; proposed decision on the unified amend; offline-proven, not run live).** A Binance perpetual stop (an Algo Service order), an aster, OKX or Bybit stop and a Polymarket limit order could not be changed by a modify (an advisory, nothing sent; you cancelled and placed again by hand, with a moment of no stop). The node now does it: a REDUCE-ONLY stop is placed first and the old one cancelled once the new one is acknowledged (the position is never without a stop; whichever fills first wins and the other is cancelled), a limit or an entry stop is cancelled first and placed when the venue says the old one is gone (a limit LOSES ITS PLACE IN THE QUEUE, said in the words). The new order has a new client order id linked to the old one, so `cancel` and `modify` naming the first id reach it; a bracket's stop leg stays linked to its take-profit. A refusal, a silent venue, a late cancel or a fill in the overlap leaves the old order standing and says why in the recent events (`AMEND <coid> ...`). Venues that amend in place are untouched. Also: Deribit moves a stop's trigger with `private/edit`, Hyperliquid's modify of a stop moves the trigger (it used to send the old one), a stop held for a bracket takes the new trigger, and a modify of a stop the node holds itself is refused in words instead of vanishing. The node advertises the `amend-replace` capability word; journal format unchanged; the modify is a command, the fold gains nothing (the drain loop reads one `is_empty` per pass).
- **A mounted strategy can now have a LOSS BUDGET: the settings rows `policy.max_mount_loss` and `policy.mount_loss_action` (decision 0249, proposed; offline-proven, not run live; journal format unchanged; restart to apply).** The per-mount budget latch has existed for a long time and nothing ever gave it a budget, so no node could latch a mount and the new `trade mount-unlatch` had nothing to clear. With `vike-cli config set policy.max_mount_loss <units>` every mount of the live node (the ones it starts with and the ones mounted later) is held to that loss, in its own account currency: past it the mount latches liquidate-only (its own orders cancelled, its new intents discarded) and, under the default `policy.mount_loss_action flatten`, its position is closed by a reduce-only market order that is offered again at every sweep until it is flat; `cancel_only` leaves the position (and the stops the cancel took) to the operator. The budget is judged on the existing 30-second risk clock and on every closed bar, nothing per message (`vike-core` gains one `Option` field, `CoreConfig::mount_budget_default`, read when a mount is built). **With no row written nothing changes**: no mount is watched. A `policy` row is read at start only (restart), the start logs `MOUNT LOSS BUDGET ARMED`, the change journal's boot anchor records the row, `vike-cli config show --filter mount_loss` reads it back and `config unset` removes it; removing the row and restarting lifts every latch. One figure for every mount (a per-mount figure is a store change of its own) and the gate-off paper arm carries none. A new `policy` key is unknown to an older binary: unset it before downgrading.
- **An operator can clear ONE mount's budget latch: `vike-cli trade mount-unlatch <mount>` (decision 0239, proposed; offline-proven, not run live; journal format unchanged).** A mounted strategy that breached its loss or notional budget stayed latched liquidate-only until a restart put it back or the mount was removed and mounted again. The verb is taken only while the mount is FLAT and has no live order or armed conditional: the node refuses, in words and before the acknowledgement, a mount it does not run, one that is not latched and one that still holds a position (saying whether its budget flattens it or is cancel-only), and the core refuses the rest in its recent events (a refusal for a position also offers a flattening budget's close again at once). Accepted, it clears the latch and re-arms the loss budget from the mount's CURRENT net realized PnL, a new base that the node says in a note (`MOUNT BUDGET UNLATCHED`), because clearing the flag alone would latch the mount again at the next sweep on the whole history; the notional cap is unchanged, and the account's state, every other mount, the drawdown latch and the margin call are untouched. It writes nothing at a venue. The result is not a journaled command (an older build could not read one): the core writes a checkpoint at once whose per-mount rows carry the cleared latch and the new base (an additive key, absent while zero), so a restart restores the mount unlatched. `vike-cli trade strategy ls` and `trade status` now mark a latched mount, and `trade doctor` adds a WARN `mounts` row for it. Read from the tree: no setting fills a mount's budget today, so no daemon latches a mount yet and the verb waits for a source of budgets. Needs the node's `mount-unlatch` word (a CONTROL key; one-shot only, no REPL word, no MCP tool).
- **An order has a LIFETIME and a post-only (maker-only) order exists (`vike-model`, `vike-venues`, `vike-fills`, `vike-paper`, `vike-sim`, `vike-core`, `vike-tradehub-client`, `vike-tradehub`, `vike-cli`, the binance, bybit, okx, deribit, hyperliquid and ibkr bridges; journal format unchanged, no field added to any order struct).** `vike-cli trade order submit … --tif day|gtc|ioc|fok|gtd [--expires <UTC instant or epoch ms>]` and `--post-only` (the one-shot verb and the REPL) send the lifetime the model always had and nothing could ask for; `--post-only` is a maker-only limit order that the venue, the paper book and the simulator REFUSE instead of executing when it would take liquidity (`TimeInForce::PostOnly`, a variant of the existing type; the refusal is a terminal `OrderRejected` with the cause `PostOnlyWouldCross`, or an `OrderCanceled` with a fixed reason where the venue accepts then cancels). Measured on the demo and testnet accounts (the venue codes are in the post-only decision record): Binance futures and spot, OKX (accepted, then cancelled by the venue), Deribit (it sends the flag pair that makes a crossing order refused; before, the adapter forced the flag false), Hyperliquid; Bybit is not live-proven (no demo keys on the box). A lifetime a venue cannot do is refused by name before any wire (`TIF_UNSUPPORTED`, `TIF_COERCED` for the ones an adapter used to run as another lifetime, `POST_ONLY_NEEDS_LIMIT`). The wire field rides a new `Welcome.features` word, `order-tif` (an older node is refused client-side, never run as a plain limit). IBKR: the lifetime reaches IB; with the extended-hours switch on a GTC or DAY goes out as DAY with both flags and an IOC or FOK with `outsideRth` alone (`includeOvernight` rides DAY only), and good-till-date is refused by name. Strategy API: `LiveBroker::submit_limit_tif` and `submit_limit_post_only`, `SimBroker::submit_limit_post_only`. The MCP tool, `/submit` and the desktop ticket send no lifetime.
- **An order has a LIFETIME and a post-only (maker-only) order exists (`vike-model`, `vike-venues`, `vike-fills`, `vike-paper`, `vike-sim`, `vike-core`, `vike-tradehub-client`, `vike-tradehub`, `vike-cli`, the binance, bybit, okx, deribit, hyperliquid and ibkr bridges; journal format unchanged, no field added to any order struct).** `vike-cli trade order submit … --tif day|gtc|ioc|fok|gtd [--expires <UTC instant or epoch ms>]` and `--post-only` (the one-shot verb and the REPL) send the lifetime the model always had and nothing could ask for; `--post-only` is a maker-only limit order that the venue, the paper book and the simulator REFUSE instead of executing when it would take liquidity (`TimeInForce::PostOnly`, a variant of the existing type; the refusal is a terminal `OrderRejected` with the cause `PostOnlyWouldCross`, or an `OrderCanceled` with a fixed reason where the venue accepts then cancels). Measured on the demo and testnet accounts (the venue codes are in the post-only decision record): Binance futures and spot, OKX (accepted, then cancelled by the venue), Deribit (it sends the flag pair that makes a crossing order refused; before, the adapter forced the flag false), Hyperliquid; Bybit is not live-proven (no demo keys on the box). A lifetime a venue cannot do is refused by name before any wire (`TIF_UNSUPPORTED`, `TIF_COERCED` for the ones an adapter used to run as another lifetime, `POST_ONLY_NEEDS_LIMIT`). The wire field rides a new `Welcome.features` word, `order-tif` (an older node is refused client-side, never run as a plain limit). IBKR: the lifetime reaches IB; with the extended-hours switch on a GTC or DAY goes out as DAY with both flags and an IOC or FOK with `outsideRth` alone (`includeOvernight` rides DAY only), and good-till-date is refused by name. Strategy API: `LiveBroker::submit_limit_tif` and `submit_limit_post_only`, `SimBroker::submit_limit_post_only`. The MCP tool and `/submit` send no lifetime (the desktop ticket sends the post-only one, below).
- **The Trade ticket's `Post only` button works (`vike-panels`, `vike-app-core`, `vike-desktop`, `vike-tradehub-client`; no wire or journal change).** It was greyed with "Vike cannot send post-only orders", which stopped being true when the post-only lifetime reached the order. It is now a real toggle, announced to a screen reader as pressed or not, and a Buy or Sell with it on sends a post-only LIMIT order by the same wire word as `vike-cli trade order submit --post-only`; a ladder click while it is on rests as a post-only limit order, and one through the market (which the ladder would turn into a stop that takes liquidity) is refused with its reason. It is live when the venue has a post-only order and the connected node advertises the lifetime word, and otherwise stays greyed saying which: the venue has none, the node is too old to carry one (`RemoteControlHandle::takes` asks the client's own feature gate, so no word is spelled twice), or the ticket is not on a Limit order (the compact ticket sends market orders only, so its `Post` is always greyed). Ticked, it is switched off in view the moment the order could no longer keep it (Market or Stop picked, an older node, a venue with none); with TP/SL also on the order is refused in words, because a bracket's entry has no lifetime. A post-only order refused for crossing shows on the status strip as `REJECTED` with the node's reason (every refused order now says why there). The confirm prompt names it.
- **An operator's core-held reduce-only stop (polymarket, IG) is now LISTED and FOLLOWS ITS POSITION (`vike-core`'s cold stuck-order sweep and publish overlay, `vike-exec`/`vike-tradehub-client`/`vike-tradehub`/`vike-app-core`/`vike-cli`; journal format unchanged).** `vike-cli trade order stops --node <observe addr>` lists every armed stop (id, account, side, quantity, trigger, `HELD`, `re-armed`), `trade doctor` has a `stops` row while any is armed, and `WireSnapshot::core_held_stops` carries them on the observe wire (additive, written only when non-empty; the node advertises `core-held-stops`). A stop RESTORED from the journal is HELD until its account's first reconcile pass (or the restored-tag window when none comes) instead of firing on the first tick after the restart against the snapshot's book; a stop whose position another order closed is CLEARED by the sweep (`CORE-HELD STOP <id> CLEARED`); a stop whose close was refused or filled only in part is ARMED AGAIN for what is left, a few times, then says the position is UNPROTECTED. Decision 0199's second amendment; `docs/ops/reconcile-on-restart.md`'s "A core-held reduce-only stop".
- **The control door says a closed market in ONE NOTE on the answer to an accepted order, and still sends it (`vike-venues`, `vike-catalog`, `vike-tradehub`, `vike-tradehub-client`, `vike-cli`, `vike-app-core`; nothing in the core's hot hop; decision 0236).** An order for a currency pair on oanda, ctrader, ig, fxcm or dukascopy, or for an alpaca share, placed while its market is closed is sent as ever, and the answer carries one sentence: `EURUSD: the FX market is closed until Sunday 22:00 UTC: the venue may hold, refuse or queue this order`. It is a note and never a refusal (the venue decides what it does with the order); every other symbol (an index, a metal, an oil or a share CFD, an IBKR stock, a crypto pair) gets no note, because only a class the symbol's name proves has a calendar, and holidays, pre- and post-market and futures sessions have no rows. The note is exact to New York's daylight saving (Friday close at 21:00 or 22:00 UTC, Sunday reopen likewise, by the season); the backtest keeps its union rows. The wire key is an additive `notes` list on the Ack (no feature word: an older client ignores it, an older node never writes it): `vike-cli trade order` prints `note:` lines (`notes` in `--json`, `node_notes` in the MCP write tools) and the desktop appends the sentence to the sent order's line in the Trade window, in no error colour. Decision 0020's refusal half stays deferred.
### Added

- **An account's engine can give an admitted symbol back, so one of its sixteen extra-symbol places is free again (`vike-cli trade unadmit <book> <symbol>`, decision 0205, proposed; offline-proven, not run live).** The places were never returned while an engine ran, so a trader rotating through symbols ran out after sixteen distinct ones and could only restart the account. `ExecutionEngine::unadmit_symbol` takes the symbol out with everything its admission wrote (the grid and margin rows, the contract value, the pair's place in the rate book and its marks) and refuses, with a named cause and nothing written, a symbol the engine is not quiet in: a position on any leg, a live order, an order created in the last minute (`UNADMIT_QUIET_MS`), the engine's own symbol, a declared leg. The statement is an `AdmitSymbol` record with one more key (`SymbolAdmission::release`) and NOT a new `Command` variant, so a node older than this one reads the journal without an error (it ignores the key and refuses the record as an admission with no grid: the symbol stays admitted there) and the journal format version does not move. The control door verb `WireCommand::UnadmitSymbol` (control scope, the feature word `unadmit-symbol`, audited, no notional, taken on every tier and trading state because it writes nothing at the exchange) judges the frame against the published account first (the symbol must be one the engine admitted, flat, with no live order, a conditional or held exit included) and the node then forgets what it kept for the symbol once the published account stops listing it (`LeaseFacts::settle_releases`: the cached facts, margin figure, idle stamps and price pump, which goes to the idle reaper unless another account or a mount keeps it), while the gatewayhub's reconcile client drops it from its own bounded list through a `forget` key on the facts request (`ReconClient::forget_symbol`, forwarded by every client that overrides `admit_symbol`; an older gatewayhub reads the frame as a look and the node then knows it forgot nothing). The seventeenth-symbol refusal now names the verb. Shared homes touched: `vike-exec`'s recon trait, the recon clients of the bridges that keep an admitted list, `vike-gatewayhub` and its client. The fold, `run_submit_hop` and the publish are untouched (one cold arm in `dispatch`'s command match and a `#[cold]` helper).
### Added

- **Dukascopy: a restarted JForex sidecar now takes up the orders the venue already lists, and the client sends it the stops it holds resting (the JForex sidecar jar, `crates/bridges/dukascopy/src/exec.rs` and `proto.rs`; the jar is a release asset the deploy must install).** Until now a new sidecar had no memory of the old one's orders: it could not cancel or amend an order the dead one placed, did not report its fill, did not hear its close, and the node ended a resting stop-loss `OrderCanceled` at the death while the venue kept it. At its start the new sidecar lists `engine.getOrders()`, takes up every order whose label names a client order id (an order opened in the platform is counted and left alone), subscribes their instruments, writes a `position` line per instrument and one `adopted` census. The client lifts its "restarted after this order was placed" refusal for what was adopted, keeps a resting stop-loss or take-profit on the node when an adopting sidecar dies and sends it to the next one, which takes the venue's price over (a stop whose price is gone ends `OrderCanceled` in the venue's words), and says loudly at a restart when the node holds a position in a symbol the venue lists no order on. A cancel of an id the sidecar does not know is now refused by name instead of skipped in silence. A jar that does not announce `adopt` keeps the old behaviour. Not measured on a venue: `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`'s Dukascopy restart row.
- **Dukascopy: `--type limit --price <px> --reduce-only` is now the venue's own take-profit on the open position, so a bracket on Dukascopy passes the core's atomic preflight with its take-profit resting natively beside its stop-loss (the JForex sidecar jar, the `dukascopy` row's `reduce_only_kinds`, and the client's refusal for an old jar).** The take-profit is the stop-loss's twin (`IOrder.setTakeProfitPrice` on WHOLE open orders, oldest first, the same price taken over, cancel and amend like a stop); an order closes at whichever price is reached first and the venue drops the other, which the node reports as the fired one's closing fill and the other's `OrderCanceled`. A client that reads no `take-profit` on the sidecar's `ready` line refuses a reduce-only limit by name (a jar from before would place a plain pending order that opens a position when hit). A paper account of Dukascopy no longer needs the paper relaxation for a bracket. Built from the SDK and held by the Java tests, not measured on a venue.
- **Dukascopy: gold, silver and the SDK's CFDs (indices, commodities, stocks) are admitted on the figures the VENUE states for each instrument (the JForex sidecar jar, the Dukascopy bridge and the gatewayhub's Dukascopy facts only; built offline, nothing has run against a JForex login; the jar is a release asset the deploy installs).** The sidecar now writes a `terms` line (minimum, increment, maximum, amount per contract, pip and tick scale, quote currency) at an instrument's first tick, and a `demo` account with an account-wide exposure ceiling armed is admitted `XAUUSD`, `XAGUSD` or a CFD written with the SDK's slashed name (`COPPER.CMD/USD`, `AAPL.US/USD`, `DEU.IDX/EUR`) on those figures, converted into the account's money like a euro pair; the SDK table's defaults, a CFD's placeholder pip among them, are never the grid. The fill spelling round trip that kept every CFD refused is closed: the sidecar stamps a CFD's fills and ticks with the slashed name it was sent under (it stamped the enum-style `COPPERCMDUSD`, which it cannot read back), proved for all predefined instruments against the real SDK, and the enum-style name is refused with the spelling that works. A CFD is sized from the SDK's figure per instrument, not the thousand-unit floor of a currency pair. Still refused, by name or by the venue's own terms: the two coins typed forex, the two CFDs quoted in pence, an instrument the SDK builds at run time, and any instrument whose amount per contract is not one (what a contract is worth per price point is unmeasured). Not modelled: financing, per-instrument margin, a stock CFD's exchange hours, an ETF CFD's long-only rule. The metal smoke now places the minimum the venue states (it reads the terms line first and logs the grid the node would admit) under a raised default notional cap, on a demo account only. Details: `docs/ops/trading-any-symbol.md`'s "Dukascopy: metals and CFDs".
- **Dukascopy: the sidecar sizes an order from the venue's own terms for the instrument, which opens the proof of the metal path (the JForex sidecar jar and the metal smoke only).** The sidecar held every instrument to one fixed floor of units, which is a thousand ounces of gold. It now asks the instrument (a currency pair keeps its floor, a metal takes the SDK's figure, anything else keeps the floor), refuses in words naming the figure, and judges a net-close remainder and an amend by the same terms. The door still refuses a metal by name until one demo order shows its amount: the metal smoke takes `DUKASCOPY_METAL_UNITS` (default unchanged), so the proof order is one ounce under the default notional cap.
### Added

- **FXCM: the rollover interest of a trade held overnight is now booked into the account when the trade closes (`vike-fxcm`).** The shim sends the closed row's own rollover, gross and net figures on a closing fill, and the exec drain turns the rollover into one funding event beside the fill, once per trade, in the account's currency. The sign is the SDK's word (funds added to the balance) and has never been measured, but the bridge now checks it against the row's own net P/L the first time it books and says in the journal whether the venue confirmed it or contradicted it. Install the new shim with the binary: an old shim sends none of it and books nothing.

- **cTrader: the swap a position paid is now booked into the account when the position closes (`vike-ctrader`).** A closing deal's realized swap becomes one funding event under the deal's symbol in the deposit currency, once per deal, so `funding_paid` and the cash follow the broker instead of drifting until a reconcile re-seeds them. The sign of the swap and the netting of the conversion fee have never been measured (every close read so far carried none): the first booking of a run says so in a warning, and a new read-only demo smoke, `ctrader_swap_sign_smoke`, lists five days of closing deals with the balance after each so the operator kit can settle both.

- **OANDA: overnight financing is now booked into the account (`vike-oanda`).** A `DAILY_FINANCING` row becomes one funding event per held instrument and a fill's own `financing` another, in the account's currency, so `funding_paid` and the cash follow the venue after a rollover instead of drifting until a reconcile re-seeds it; a guaranteed stop's `guaranteedExecutionFee` is added to the fill's commission. The sign of `financing` has never been measured (the practice account never held a position across a rollover): it is read as the signed balance change, the first booking of a run says so in a warning, and the operator kit has a read-only script that confirms it against the venue's `accountBalance`.

- **OANDA: the engine's cash now follows the venue's balance across a close in a pair quoted in another currency than the account's (`vike-oanda`).** OANDA converts the quote-currency result of such a close with a factor exactly one percent worse than the mid on the practice account, states the cost on the closing fill (`plHomeConversionCost`) and moves its balance by `pl`, which includes it; the engine books the close at the mid, so its cash ran about one percent of every such PnL ahead of the venue's, and the gap grew with every close (0.67 USD after four round trips of 20000 units, measured against the account's own fill records). The bridge now adds that stated cost to the fill's commission, in the transactions stream, the order reply and the reconcile report alike, so the cash agrees with the venue's balance to the rate's age (0.03 percent of the PnL on the captured USD/ZAR round trip) and the cost shows among the fees; the `realized` column is unchanged and stays gross of it. A pair quoted in the account's currency, an opening fill and a fill that states no cost book exactly as before, and nothing in the core changes. Offline-proven against the captured fills; every capture was a loss, so the sign a gain states is unmeasured and the figure is booked by its magnitude; not run on the new build.

### Fixed

- **IG: a position's CLOSE no longer cancels the order that opened it, and a fill no longer overtakes its own accept (`vike-ig`).** A raw capture of the demo gateway's trade stream showed it speaks the spec's `U,<sub>,<item>,f1|f2|f3` grammar, which the lane's parser did not: it lost the first field and read the position update as a deal confirm, so every close made an `OrderCanceled` for the entry order after its fill, and the update of an open could reach the core ahead of `OrderAccepted` (`terminal event dropped on a live order (out-of-order)`). The parser now splits the spec's way, the lane decodes only a position OPENED (a confirm of a limit order's creation reads exactly like a fill and is not decoded), stamps it with IG's own UTC `timestamp`, and holds the stream's events for an order behind the order's own answer while its submit is in flight. Offline tests on the captured lines; the live proof needs a deploy (the operator kit's igclock script).
- **IG history: the account clock rule was wrong on a winter-time day and every window failed its first row (`vike-ig`).** The rule "London plus seven hours" came from one summer-time day; on 2026-10-30 the account read an hour further (the login says 8 hours), so a fetch stopped at its first row, charged. The rule now takes the day the request is made on into account and is pinned to both measured days; `parse_ig_time_utc` refuses an account-local text (`createdDate`, `snapshotTime`) that it used to read as UTC, 8 hours late. A request made in summer time after 2027-03-28 is the next measurement; the lane still fails closed with both numbers if IG reads it another way.

- **Two tearsheet readers no longer read a euro (or any non-dollar) book as dollars (`vike-app-core` and the `tearsheet` CLI in `vike`; no change to the simulator, the paper book, the backtest or any measured crate).** The desktop's Tearsheet Summary tab checked only a fill's symbol NAME, and a euro account's `EURUSD` fills name no foreign quote, so it folded them as dollars; it now leaves out the fills of every venue the live snapshot records off the dollar and says how many in a first row. `tearsheet --journal DIR --datahub` plotted the sampler's `portfolio/TOTAL` equity series, which is one currency's (the first live engine's group) and states none; when the journal records a ledger that is not the dollar's it now plots the realized-only curve of the dollar fills instead and says why. A node of one currency is byte-identical in both. The design of the full offline valuation (a rate-aware simulator, the paper book's conversion, the rate source of a backtest) is the new design record on that subject, status proposed and not built.
