- **The risk clock (and every other fixed-cadence boundary timer) now keeps its schedule: it re-arms from the instant it was scheduled for, not from the instant it happened to run (`vike-core`'s cold boundary timers only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/timers.rs`'s `rearm_periodic`; nothing on the fold or the latency-gated hop, no journal change).** The timer wheel rounds a deadline up to its 50 ms tick, so the old rule drifted the 30 s margin-call and drawdown clock by about 43 ms per sweep on a busy core (measured on the real core and wheel, 200 sweeps) and, when nothing but the waker thread reaches the core (all feeds quiet), found the timer a fraction of a tick short on the exact millisecond and waited one more wake: the "30 s" clock ran every 45 s. Now each sweep is one interval after the scheduled instant of the last (to within the boundary's own lateness, and without drift); a stall of a whole interval or more still skips the missed sweeps rather than running them back to back. The margin call's quiet window after a release is nine tenths of an interval so the phase-locked retry is never skipped.
- **The stuck-order ladder now reaches a further account of a venue a mount drives (a second account of one exchange, or a lane twin), so an order that never gets a venue answer there is prodded and then rejected locally like the primary's, instead of staying `Submitted` for ever (`vike-core`'s cold stuck-order timer only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/watchdog/orders.rs`'s `stuck_ladder_covers`; nothing on the fold or the latency-gated hop, no journal change).** The ladder covered the primary and the accounts of price-only venues only; such an order stayed live, counted as cover by the margin call's close netting and blocked that engine's next margin call. It applies whenever the risk clock is configured, which every live node does; a core without it walks the primary alone as before.
- **A reduce-only LIMIT close priced through the market now counts as a close already in flight, so the margin call, a mount budget's flatten and a core-held stop no longer send a second close beside it (`vike-core`'s cold risk sweeps and the core-held stop's fire only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/watchdog/closes.rs`'s `closes_in_flight`; nothing on the fold or the latency-gated hop).** On a venue that puts no reduce-only flag on the wire (oanda, ig, fxcm, ibkr, ctrader, alpaca) two closes flip the position. Until now only reduce-only MARKET orders were netted; a limit sell at or below the bid (a buy at or above the ask) fills on arrival just the same. A take-profit resting far from the market is still no cover.
- **The drawdown latch now values a stale engine at the NEWEST price its board holds, not at the highest-priority one (`vike-core`'s cold 30 s risk sweep and `vike-exec`'s `PriceBoard::classify` relaxed walk only, behind a new `PriceCfg::last_known_by_recency` that defaults off and that only the risk clock sets; the fresh pricing path and the publish path are not touched, no journal change).** The latch values an engine whose price went stale (an FX weekend, a dead pump, a stopped account) at its last known price, and that used to be the first slot present at any age, so an old venue mark (a fill's or a reconcile pass's) outranked the quote that ticked a minute ago and a drawdown could be measured off the older number. A rung inside the age bound is still taken first; the SKIP line in the recent events now names the age of the price actually used.
- **A price feed that gaps for about as long as the risk clock's age bound is now ONE skip episode in the recent events and the log, not a WARN and a ring line at every other sweep (`vike-core`'s cold risk sweep only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/watchdog/risk.rs`'s `price_only_basis`; nothing on the fold or the latency-gated hop, no journal change).** An engine whose position's price went stale used to end its "skipped" episode at the first sweep that found it fresh, so a flapping feed said itself again and again and crowded fills and rejects out of the 64-line ring. The episode now ends only after the engine has stayed fresh for three clock intervals; only the saying is held, a fresh engine is priced and margin-called at once.
- **A per-mount budget latch no longer leaves a position open when its one flatten fails, and the latch survives a restart (`vike-core`'s cold risk sweeps plus one bool per live mount when a journal `Snap` is built, and `vike-journal`'s `Snap` mount row: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/watchdog/risk.rs`'s `reoffer_mount_flatten`, `vike_journal::SnapMountAttr::latched`; nothing on the fold or the latency-gated hop, an additive key and no format step).** The latch still judges and cancels once, but a latched mount whose budget says `flatten_on_breach` and that still holds a position with no reduce-only close in flight (the first flatten was denied, rejected, lost to the panic guard or sent before the trade link was ready) is now offered the missing quantity again at every sweep, said once per episode in the recent events and skipped while its engine is halted or its trade link is down. The latch also rides every `Snap`, so a restart (a clean stop writes one) puts it back on a mount that still has an active budget instead of leaving it free to trade until the next sweep re-fires it; a mount whose budget was removed from the profile comes back free.
- **`vike-cli trade order ls`, the REPL's orders table and the open-orders table of `trade venue` no longer print the float tail of a price or a quantity (`vike-cli` only: `crates/vike-cli/src/cmd/trade/describe.rs`'s `opt_num` and the three order tables now go through `verbs::fmt_num`, as the preview line does; `--json` is unchanged and carries the engine's exact value).** The engine keeps a quantized price as `round_to_step`'s `n * tick`, one last-bit off the decimal for some grid points, and the table printed every digit: a BTC-USDT-SWAP limit at 80925.93 on the OKX demo read 80925.93000000001 while the wire string (the Decimal grid multiple) and the venue's own `px` row were 80925.93 (measured on the demo, captured rows kept as test fixtures). Nothing changes in the OKX bridge or in the engine: every OKX price (submit, batch builder, amend, stop trigger) already goes through the Decimal quantizer, and a test now pins that. A number that really has more digits keeps them (the rendering is the shortest one within a part in a trillion). Quantity and filled quantity are spelled the same way. Live proof: the 0.1.98 kit's `okxmarket-price-and-live-row.sh`, after a deploy.
- **OKX: a market order's `live` row is now documented as what it is, and the submit fence's reason is corrected (comments, the OKX crate page, captured rows and tests only; no behaviour change).** The `orders` channel pushes `live` for a MARKET order too and then `filled` in the same millisecond (eight market orders on the demo, the `live` row first every time; rows kept in `crates/bridges/okx/tests/fixtures/orders_channel/`); the bridge's comments said an order that never rests gets no `live` row. That row is the pump's own bare accept: the fence does not hold it, holds the fill behind it, and the engine folds the order `Filled` once (a test per half). The fence stays for the fill that can beat the REST answer and for the history replay, which carries no `live` row.
### Added

- **FXCM: one stop-loss or take-profit may cover SEVERAL trades, its size can be amended, and a stop re-sent after a restart takes over the exit the venue still holds (`vike-fxcm` and its shim `fcshim.cpp`; needs the new `libfcshim.so`, which the deploy installs).** On the hedging account the venue's stop is bound to one whole trade, so a stop for the size of two trades was refused by name. It is now one order to the node and one venue order per trade (the oldest free trades, whole, as long as their sizes add up to the order's), placed whole or not at all, filled as one order (a partial fill until the last leg), narrowed when the venue removes a leg and cancelled with the last; `vike-cli trade order modify <coid> --qty` adds or removes whole trades' exits, exactly, and the price moves every leg. A stop or take-profit re-sent after a node restart for a trade whose exit rests at the SAME rate and size is that exit (nothing is sent, and a cancel or an amend reaches it); one at another rate is refused by name and left alone. Decision record: the FXCM exit that may span trades, proposed. Live proof: the 0.1.98 kit's FXCM exits script, after a deploy.

### Fixed

- **FXCM: a PARTIAL close no longer raises a `MissingFill` for the trade's remainder, and the exits on the trade follow it (`vike-fxcm` and its shim; needs the new `libfcshim.so`).** A partial close splits the trade and the rest returns under a new trade id; reconcile reported it under that id, which the core never folded. The shim now sends the closed row's remainder id on the closing fill and each trade's origin on the Trades read; the reconcile fill report names a remainder by the ROOT trade id (the one the opening fill carried) and the exits move to the remainder's id. A remainder of a remainder after a node restart still reads as the first remainder (held under `quarantine`).

- **A fill that comes from OUTSIDE the engine (a trade made in the venue's own screen) on the mounted symbol of a non-dollar account, in the first seconds after a start while the symbol has no conversion rate yet, is now HELD instead of being booked at the venue's own unit (US dollars into a euro ledger, wrong by the whole rate).** `vike-exec`'s fold refuses it (one `error!` line naming it `HELD`, nothing moves, the trade id is not burned), reconcile raises the venue's record, and the same fill folds at the rate once the node has rated the symbol. The node's own orders are not affected (an opening order was already refused while the rate is missing, and a closing order's fill is a fill of an order the engine holds). The fold gains one pointer test on every accepted fill; the latency A/B is owed to the integrated branch. Decision 0209.
- **The tearsheet no longer reads a euro account's fills as dollars.** The journal tearsheet (the `tearsheet` tool and the node's report verb) leaves out the fills of a venue whose engine the journal's snapshots record in a currency other than the dollar, and names what it left out in the sheet's name (a venue that runs a dollar account beside a euro one loses both accounts' fills, because a fill names no account). The drawdown alert's session peak starts over when the first live engine restarts into another currency, instead of keeping the old currency's peak until the daemon restarts. `vike-cli trade position ls` prints one total per currency instead of adding euro and dollar profit and loss, and the Residual mount row is one row per currency group. Decision 0209.
- **After a crash the boot restore now refolds the journal tail of a node that runs a labelled account (the CI box's `bybit#DEMO`) or two engines of one venue, instead of reading the last checkpoint alone for every engine on the node.** A strategy's submit, a conditional's fire and a margin call's release carry the route key of their engine and replay onto it (`Command::OrderOn`), a gateway event replays with its ring so a fill with no order id reaches the account it belongs to, and an order the checkpoint already holds keeps its engine for the tail's answers. A tail the previous build wrote (records that name no engine) is still read the old way, so the first crash across the upgrade loses nothing it did not lose before; after a clean stop nothing changes. Journal format unchanged (decision 0206, proposed). Known-limitations row retired.
- **The Binance lane twin and its parent account are bounded by ONE exposure ceiling, not one each.** The twin names its parent and the core hands each engine the other's whole book about once a second, which the engine adds to its own before judging an order, so an account that stated a ceiling can no longer hold twice of it across spot and perpetual. The partner's side is up to about a second old and a book that cannot be priced leaves the last figure standing. ⚠ An account that followed the old advice and stated half of what it meant now allows half: state the whole figure. The warning at the twin's start is an info line, and `vike-cli secrets account set-leverage` no longer tells the operator to halve the ceiling.
- **A Binance spot BUY now opens the position the wallet really holds, and a BNB-discounted spot fee is valued instead of booked as that many quote units (`crates/bridges/binance/src/family/spot_fee.rs`, shared with aster's spot lane, which is proven offline only).** Binance spot takes a BUY's fee out of the base coin it delivers, so the wallet holds the ordered quantity less the fee while the engine's long carried the whole quantity (a sell of the whole position could ask for coin the wallet lacked). The stream, the resync replay and the reconcile fill parser now all carry the net `last_qty`, and the fee stays booked in the quote (the two do not double count). A fee in BNB on a pair that is not BNB's own is priced through the public mainnet spot ticker (binance registers it; aster registers none, its fee assets being unmeasured) and is not netted from the quantity. A SELL, a quote fee and the perpetual are unchanged. Decision record: `docs/decisions/0215-a-spot-buys-quantity-is-net-of-the-base-coin-fee-and-a-third-asset-fee-is-priced-by-a-rate-the-venue-registers.md`.

- **The drawdown latch no longer judges a non-dollar demo or live account (FXCM's EUR demo, account 9) on the placeholder seed while the account is still waiting for its first wallet balance (`vike-core`'s cold 30 s risk sweep and published state only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/watchdog/risk.rs`'s `group_awaits_wallet`; nothing on the fold or the latency-gated hop, no journal change, no setting).** Measured live on the previous release (2026-10-27; the figures are in decision 0183, item 4): after a hot deactivate and activate of account 9 the EUR group's base stayed at the placeholder seed until the first reconcile balance moved it to the EUR wallet, so a small loss in that window read as a large drawdown and would have put EVERY engine of the node in `REDUCING`. Now a demo or live engine of a non-dollar group that has not adopted its wallet makes its group wait: no peak is folded, nothing trips and nothing is published for the group until the wallet is adopted, then it is judged on the wallet exactly as since v0.1.95 (a 12,000 EUR loss on 50,000 EUR still trips a 20 percent rule, once). The wait is bounded (`ADOPT_WAIT_MS`, `crates/vike-core/CLAUDE.md`) from the first sweep that found the account so; a venue that never sends a balance is then judged on the configured seed, as before, said once in the ring (`LATCH WAITS (EUR group)`, `LATCH WAIT OVER (EUR group)`; never the `DRAWDOWN LATCH` prefix, which means a trip). The dollar group, a paper engine and every group whose accounts have adopted behave exactly as before.

- **The core now refuses an explicit client order id its engine already holds answered or finished, behind the control door's own refusal (`vike-core`: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/refusals.rs`'s `answered_coid_status` and `refuse_held_coid`, called by `lower_submit`).** A second `Submit` for one id inside one publish interval passes the door (its check reads the coalesced snapshot), and the core then replaced the registry entry of an order the venue had accepted or filled with a fresh one nothing would ever answer, so the stuck-order watchdog rejected that entry locally while the original still rested at the venue. Now the command is refused with a warning and a line on the recent events (`order <id> REFUSED, nothing sent: coid <id> is already used by an order that is ACCEPTED (still live): …`), the held order is byte for byte as it was and nothing is sent. A strategy order, a fired stop, a flatten and a bracket leg carry minted ids and are never asked; a repeat whose first order the venue has not answered yet (`INITIALIZED` or `SUBMITTED`) is the in-flight retry and goes as before, which is also what keeps the latency harness's submit hop measuring what it measured. An id the core itself refused (a capability refusal registers the order `REJECTED`) is spent too: the corrected order needs a new id, as the door already told an operator. ⚠ A journal written before this change that holds a reused answered id refolds differently under the offline replay verifier. ⚠ The cost is one registry read per operator submit; its the latency box latency A/B is owed by the integrated branch.

### Added

- **`vike-cli trade venue <book> balance|open-orders --node <observe addr>` reads an account at its venue through the node: the wallet's balance (Polymarket: with the allowance each exchange holds) or the venue's OWN list of its open orders, with no reconcile flag and no order placed, moved or cancelled.** The node serves a new read request (`Request::VenueRead`, answered by `Response::VenueRead`, negotiated by the new capability word `venue-read`, so an older node is refused client-side with nothing sent and an older gatewayhub is told in words), takes the observe key alone (the argument is the new server page `venue_read.rs`), and asks the account's open trade lease, so the account must be running on that node: one that is not is told so by name. Polymarket and Hyperliquid answer; every other venue says `not offered by <venue>` and the command exits 1, never an empty list. The gatewayhub's gate holds repeat reads apart and says so in words. A held outcome-token position is in neither read. The wire is additive and the journal is untouched; the frames are pinned byte for byte in the node's and the client's tests.

- **A conversion rate that has gone stale is no longer invisible (a non-dollar account, or a dollar one that holds a symbol quoted in another currency, values its position at the last rate it has when the node stops renewing it).** `vike-cli trade equity`, Telegram `/equity` and the desktop's Account window now list every account's rates, a stale one marked `STALE` and, when a position is open in that currency, saying the position is valued at it. `vike-cli trade doctor` gains a WARN `rate` row for exactly that case (a stale rate nobody holds anything in is only listed), and a new alert rule `{"kind":"stale_rate"}` fires ONCE per episode (it needs a row in `alerts.json` like every rule). Additive: the wire's rate row gains an optional `held` key that is absent when false, and an older node or client ignores it. Decision 0209.
- **Three live-smoke tests ask a venue what price it holds for an order priced at an exact multiple of a fine tick, and run in the order-lifecycle job of the live-smoke workflow with its skip-honesty step (`crates/bridges/binance/tests/binance_perp_fine_tick_price_smoke.rs`, `crates/bridges/okx/tests/okx_fine_tick_price_smoke.rs`, `crates/bridges/deribit/tests/deribit_fine_tick_price_smoke.rs`).** Each rests one far limit BUY on the venue's demo or testnet account, compares the price its own order builder wrote and the price the venue echoes with the exact decimal (integer arithmetic in the new test-support module `crates/vike-bridge-core/src/grid_decimal.rs`), cancels it and asserts it is gone; okx and deribit became required venues of that job. Only the spot witness stays out of the lane (it declares helpers with a path attribute, which the credential guard refuses). None has run against its venue yet.
- **The gatewayhub names the symbols its reconcile client READ, and the node claims no more than that (bybit, binance, aster and every venue whose client keeps a list; additive wire, shared homes `vike-gatewayhub`, `vike-gatewayhub-client`).** Page 0 of every list reconcile reply (orders, fills, positions) now carries an optional `read`: the client's own `ReconClient::admitted_symbols`, taken under the lock the fetch held (`crates/vike-gatewayhub/src/trade/recon.rs`'s `read_symbols`), advertised by the new capability string `gw_trade_recon_read`. The lease (`crates/vike-gatewayhub-client/src/trade/told.rs`'s `Told::readable`) claims only the symbols it told AND the daemon names, matched without case and spelled as the engine spells them, so a symbol the mirror holds and the daemon's client does not (the last slot raced, or an adapter restarted inside one daemon session) is HELD by the restore instead of retired as gone, and the difference is said once at warn. The named list only narrows: it never adds a symbol, a venue outside `RECON_READS_ADMITTED` still claims nothing, a daemon that does not advertise the string (or names nothing) leaves the claim exactly as it was, an older node ignores the key, and a reply that names nothing is byte-identical to the old one. bybit, binance and aster's reconcile clients answer `admitted_symbols` now (they kept the list and did not name it). Not changed: the diff of a pass still reads the engine's local state on a symbol the client did not read. `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`, the decision record on the daemon naming what its client read (`docs/decisions/README.md`).
- **bybit, binance, aster and okx replay the history of the symbols the engine trades, not only the mounted one, after a user-data reconnect and after a command (the resync supervisor and the gap sentinel).** The reconnect-resync reads the mounted symbol first with the requests it has always made, then every symbol the reconcile client was told (the adapter hands the exec thread the SAME admitted list, as okx's funding poll shares it): `allOrders`/`userTrades` (and binance's `allAlgoOrders`) on binance and aster, `order/history`/`execution/list` on bybit, `orders-history`/`fills-history` on okx, and `orders-algo-history` for okx's ALGO socket. The gap sentinel reads the mounted symbol and the symbols the commands since its last look touched (`CoidSymbols::touch`), not all admitted ones. A foreign fill or liquidation carries the trade id the stream spells (`SYMBOL:t` on binance and aster through `fill_trade_id`, `INSTID:tradeId` on okx, `execId` on bybit), so a replayed fill the stream already folded is a known id; okx sizes it by that instrument's own contract value and skips an instrument whose value cannot be read. The walk ends at the first rate-limit answer (the mounted symbol's events are kept; the rest is the reconcile pass's, as before), a symbol of the other lane and a repeat are never read, and okx's instruments are a pace apart. With nothing admitted every request is the old one. Proved offline only; `crates/bridges/binance/CLAUDE.md`, `crates/bridges/okx/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`.
- **Polymarket: a market's slug or address can be typed as the symbol, and the control door admits each outcome token before its first order (CODE AND OFFLINE TESTS ONLY, nothing of it has run against the live CLOB; `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`'s polymarket row says what is unproven).** `slug:Outcome` or the market's polymarket.com address is resolved to the outcome's token id by the gatewayhub over the account's trade lease (Gamma is a venue socket and the node opens none), the order goes out on the id, and the facts are Gamma's point lookup by token: the market's tick, minimum size and neg-risk flag, the share lot, and a refusal by name for a market that is closed or paused (`WireSymbolFacts::symbol` is the one new wire key, additive and never written when absent). The venue's `SYMBOL_RULES` row moves from `PerOrder` to `Admits(Spelling::OutcomeToken)`, so a Polymarket account now behaves as every admitting venue does: a `live` account needs an account-wide exposure ceiling for a new token, the engine admits sixteen tokens for the life of the process, a `paper` account trades only what it was started on, an opening order needs a price the node holds (a price-only feed prices it where no mount names the venue), and an order under the market's minimum size is refused at the door. The price-only feed arms no link dead-man. `docs/decisions/0217-the-door-admits-a-polymarket-outcome-token-and-the-gatewayhub-resolves-a-market-name-to-it.md` is the record.
- **Hyperliquid: an isolated-only perpetual, a USDC spot pair (`HYPE/USDC`) and a builder-dex coin (`xyz:TSLA`) can now be ordered through the door (decision 0218; built and proved offline, no order placed yet).** The symbol admission carries the margin mode its positions open in (the engine books them in the isolated pool for an isolated-only coin and as fully funded cash for a spot pair, snapshotted and restored with the symbol), the facts verb states it to a node that says it books one and refuses the symbol by name to any other, a spot fee paid in the base token is netted out of the fill (live stream and reconcile read alike), a spot wire carries no reduce-only flag, a dex coin is folded into the exec universe with its own dex's listing alone (no universe flag), the reconcile client reads each admitted dex's book and each admitted pair's holding, and the gatewayhub's Hyperliquid feed resolves a spot pair's wire coin so the pair is priced. The delisted coin, a pair quoted in another token and the wire name `@N` stay refused by name. See the known-limitations rows for what is not measured.
- **IBKR: a stock name can pin its contract id (`AAPL.SMART.USD.STK.265598`), which resolves a ticker listed on more than one exchange without the paced symbol search, and a class share is written `BRK.B`, `BRK B` or `BRK-B` and held as `BRK_B.SMART.USD` (decision 0218; offline only, nothing run against a gateway).** The ambiguity refusal now prints the spelling to use.
- **The tradehub summary line now prints the EXACT base, peak and curve the drawdown latch folded, for every currency group including the primary's (`vike-core` publishes the base beside the curve and the primary's row: `vike_exec::GroupCurve` gains `base`, `Portfolio::group_curves` lists every judged group; cold publish only).** `other_ledgers[].base` was the curve less the group's own PnL, off by whatever the PnL moved since the last sweep; it is now the base the sweep used. The primary group gains `drawdown_peak` beside `capital_base` and `drawdown_curve`. A group still waiting for its first wallet has none of the keys (never zero). All keys are additive. The push alert is unchanged: its adapter skips the primary's new row.
- **A Dukascopy or an IG account in another currency than the pair it is mounted on (a EUR Dukascopy demo account on `EURUSD`, a pound IG demo account on the EUR/USD mini) is converted for, the way FXCM's EUR account is, instead of being refused; PROVED OFFLINE ONLY, because no non-USD demo account of either venue exists (the proof script waits in the kit for the day one does).** Both venues join the node's one list of venues whose lane rates the mounted symbol too (`MOUNT_CONVERTING_VENUES`): on a `demo` account with an account-wide exposure ceiling the ledger is the account's real money, the mount is declared quoted in its own money and booked through a rate (an opening order on it waits for the first rate, a close never), and every other symbol converts at its rate. Dukascopy's lane answers the mounted pair and every other pair into the stated money and states the ledger on each answer (a quote currency with no direct pair into it is refused; nothing is composed), and its wallet frame is labelled with the account's own money. IG's facts convert for any account currency and state it, the node's refusal that made a non-USD IG account NOT RUN once the ceiling was armed (closing orders included) is gone, an order's `currencyCode` stays the epic's own dealing currency, and a login that holds no USD CFD account is still refused at the login unless the account row's book names the pound or euro account. USD accounts, `live`, `paper` and accounts with no ceiling are unchanged; no journal change. Deploy with the account flat (the first start relabels the engine). The rates are mids: both venues convert at their own rate plus a margin. Decision 0213.

### Added

- **Dukascopy: a position the venue closed without telling the node (a stop-loss that fired after a sidecar restart, a close made in the JForex platform, a close during a session loss) now SHOWS as a held reconcile row when the next close of it is refused, and an operator can clear it with `vike-cli trade recon confirm <id>` instead of cycling the whole account.** The sidecar's refusal of a reduce-only close (`reduce-only: no open long order to reduce ... NOT sent`) now carries a typed cause (`OrderRejected::cause`, new, additive: a rejection without one is byte-for-byte what it was, an older node ignores the key), set only when the venue's own order list shows nothing facing the side, not when a close of a real position is merely already under way. The node's engine parks it and the core, on its 15-second stuck-order clock, holds one `OrphanLocalPosition` row for that account and symbol (`vike-cli trade recon ls`, the `recon` line of `vike-cli trade doctor`, the GUI). It HOLDS and writes nothing under every reconcile policy: the book keeps the position until you confirm, and the confirm drops it at its own average price with zero PnL (refused if the quantity moved). It is a witness, not a reconcile: it fires only when a close is refused, it needs the `jforex-bridge.jar` of this release (an older jar refuses in the same words and nothing is held), and the row is lost at a restart (the next refused close raises it again). Decision 0200. Any code that builds an `OrderRejected` now names `cause: None`.
### Added

- **IG: an operator's stop-loss (`submit ig <epic> sell <qty> --type stop --trigger <px> --reduce-only`) is now HELD BY THE NODE instead of refused with `REDUCE_ONLY_UNSUPPORTED: kind=stop venue=ig` (`vike-core` only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/apply/conditional.rs`'s `arm_core_held_stop`; no IG bridge change, no capability-table change, no journal format step, no CLI change).** IG's close endpoint can only close at the market now (measured on the demo host), so since v0.1.96 IG had no stop-loss at all. The node's core-held stop (decision 0199, which polymarket already used) now takes the order when the capability row refuses it either because the row has no `stop` kind or because its adapter places no reduce-only stop (IG's row: `stop` is an entry kind, `reduce_only_kinds` is `["market"]`); the capability row decides and no venue is named in code. The recent events say `CORE-HELD STOP <id> armed: ... ig has NO native reduce-only stop ... it protects only while the node runs, NOT through an outage or a restart gap`; at the trigger (a quote MID, not IG's bid or offer) the node sends a reduce-only MARKET for at most the open position, which IG closes by epic through its close endpoint, or drops itself when there is no position; `cancel <id>` takes the arm id; a restart with the journal on re-arms it. The stop is a price the node watches, NOT an order at IG. Unchanged: every other venue (a pinned matrix test of every roster venue by every order kind, reduce-only or not, holds the held set to polymarket and ig); an entry-side stop and a reduce-only limit on IG keep their way; **a BRACKET on IG is still refused whole before its entry is sent** (its stop-loss AND take-profit legs are both refused by the preflight, and the stop leg is not held by the core, so a bracket is never half protected). `docs/decisions/0199-an-operators-reduce-only-stop-on-a-venue-with-no-native-stop-is-held-by-the-core.md` has the dated amendment, `docs/ops/reconcile-on-restart.md`'s "A core-held reduce-only stop" and `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` the limits.
### Added

- **`vike-cli trade order bracket` sends a TP/SL bracket (an entry with a stop-loss and a take-profit) through the tradehub door, so the whole-bracket refusal can be seen from a terminal and not only from the desktop's TP/SL ticket (`vike-cli` only: `crates/vike-cli/src/cmd/trade/order.rs`'s `bracket_verb`, a `Verb::Bracket` that resolves to the same `WireCommand::Bracket` the desktop sends; no door, core, wire or journal change).** `vike-cli trade order bracket ig CS.D.EURUSD.CFD.IP buy 1 --stop-loss 1.05 --take-profit 1.15 --node 127.0.0.1:7879 --yes` places a market entry; `@1.10` after the quantity makes it a limit entry; the book names the account exactly as `trade order submit` does, and a node that does not advertise `bracket-account` is refused before anything is sent. It is a verb of its own rather than `submit --stop-loss` because it is another wire command with no client order id. The core mints the three legs' ids only after the node answers, so the answer reads the node's recent events once the receipt is in and prints what the core said: for a venue that cannot hold one leg (v0.1.96: IG, and Dukascopy's take-profit) the `outcome:` line carries `bracket for <venue> REFUSED WHOLE, nothing was sent: its <leg> leg is refused (...)` and three `leg:` lines carry the three rejected coids with their reasons (`node_event.legs` under `--json`); for a bracket the core accepted, the two held exits. Only lines that are new since the send count, so a second bracket on the same venue never prints the first one's refusal. Like every look it changes no exit code: a bracket the core refused whole still exits 0, and the door's own refusals (an inverted bracket, a symbol the engine does not trade, a venue with two engines and no account) are the usual `node rejected the command` before the receipt. A bracket carries no id to dedup a retry by, so after a `not yet known` answer check `trade order ls` before running the line again. Not on the REPL and not an MCP tool. `trade order submit` and every other verb are unchanged; the advisory guardrail line of the preview now sizes a bracket by its quantity and its largest priced leg instead of saying it has no size.
### Changed

- **A paper account of IG or Dukascopy now accepts a bracket and a reduce-only limit or stop, which the previous release refused there because the live adapter refuses them (`vike-venues`'s `preflight_order_at` takes the engine's stated tier and `vike-core` passes it; `vike-exec` gains `ExecutionEngine::stated_tier`; no venue adapter and no wire change).** The paper simulator holds both exits (the entry fills, the held exits are released, the take-profit fills and its stop-loss sibling is cancelled), and a paper order never reaches the adapter whose refusals the capability table's `reduce_only_kinds` lists. A demo account, a live account and an engine nobody told its tier are refused exactly as before, and every other check (order kinds, time-in-force, margin modes) still applies on paper. The cost is said, not hidden: a strategy that works on paper through this is refused on the same venue's demo and live account, so when a paper engine is let through where the venue would have refused, the recent events carry one line per venue and kind per run, `paper: the live ig adapter would refuse this (stop): ...`.
- **Dukascopy: no order stays `ACCEPTED` for ever after its JForex sidecar dies or the venue refuses its fill, and a reduce-only close the venue could only partly take no longer reads as filled (Dukascopy bridge only: `crates/bridges/dukascopy/src/exec.rs`'s `settle`, its reader drain and `submit`, plus a few lines of the sidecar's `StrategyBridge.java`; nothing in a shared crate, every other venue unchanged).** Three ends the core dropped or misread, found by the v0.1.96 agent. (1) A plain MARKET order (an entry) the sidecar had acknowledged when it died got `OrderRejected "bridge died"`, which the core folds only from `Initialized`/`Submitted`: it stayed `ACCEPTED`. It now ends `OrderCanceled`, the words saying the venue may have FILLED it and to look at the positions in the JForex platform (this venue has no reconcile pass that would find such a fill). The cancel carries no fill, so nothing is booked; an order the sidecar never answered and a resting limit keep the rejection they always had. (2) A fill the venue refused AFTER it had accepted the order (`ORDER_FILL_REJECTED` after `ORDER_SUBMIT_OK`) reached the node as `OrderRejected`, dropped the same way. The bridge now folds a refusal of an order the sidecar acknowledged as `OrderCanceled` with the venue's words, whatever jar is installed; ⚠ **the jar changes too** (the sidecar now sends that cancel itself), so the `jforex-bridge.jar` of the next release has a NEW sha256 and the deploy installs it like any jar release (the Rust half needs no new jar). (3) A reduce-only close larger than what the venue held (the venue closes what it holds and drops the rest, the v0.1.95 rule) ended `OrderFilled` short of its quantity; it now ends `OrderPartiallyFilled` then `OrderCanceled` naming the units not executed. The fills, and so the position and PnL, are exactly as before. Proven against the fake sidecar through the order FSM (`crates/bridges/dukascopy/tests/dukascopy_restart.rs`'s `an_accepted_market_entry_at_a_sidecars_death_ends_canceled_in_words_and_books_nothing`, `crates/bridges/dukascopy/tests/dukascopy_exec.rs`'s `a_fill_the_venue_rejects_after_accepting_the_order_ends_it_canceled_in_its_words`, `crates/bridges/dukascopy/tests/dukascopy_netting.rs`'s `a_reduce_only_close_larger_than_the_venues_position_ends_partly_filled_then_canceled_in_words`, each RED on the base) and, for the jar, `NetCloseAfterRestartTest.java`'s `aFillRejectedAfterTheVenueAcceptedTheOrderEndsItCanceledNotRejected`. NOT measured live: a real `ORDER_FILL_REJECTED` and a real death with an entry in flight.
- **Screen readers now read every input's name in the desktop GUI.** The order ticket's price and quantity, the settings editor's field, the execution history's pickers, the chart's two settings dialogs, the Studio's pickers and its code editor (and a few fields beside them) are each named by the label beside them; nothing on screen moves. The GUI tests check every input for a name again.
- **Polymarket: the venue's own message about an order cancelled moments ago (its cancel echo, a status update) is no longer logged as "a match that raced its own cancel — the fill is real and must fold" (the Polymarket bridge only: `crates/bridges/polymarket/src/exec_plane/registry.rs`'s `rekey_for_decode`; what is folded does not change).** Seen live on 2026-10-27 (account 16): a 5-share limit buy rested, was cancelled and filled nothing, and the cancel echo printed the match sentence at INFO. The sentence now belongs to a late TRADE frame only, which is the one that carries money; a late `order` frame is a DEBUG line naming its type (`frame_type="CANCELLATION"`) and saying it is not a fill. Both still re-key through the settling grace and fold exactly as before.
- **IBKR: a foreign-quoted stock on an account whose base currency the gateway's account summary does not state is no longer refused for want of a base; the rate is expressed in an ASSUMED USD, the owner's default, and the first statement of the venue replaces the assumption with no "changed" refusal (the ibkr bridge only: `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/src/any_symbol_socket.rs`'s `assume_base`).** A base the venue stated before is never replaced by an assumption, an assumption is never handed to the gatewayhub's start as the engine's anchor, and a dial the data lane refuses still answers unavailable. Nothing is on the wire. Offline tests of the pure pieces only; not proven against a gateway.
- **IBKR: an account whose reconcile connection has made the two account-summary requests the Gateway allows a session no longer waits for an operator to get a balance again; the reconcile client closes that connection and dials a new session itself (the ibkr bridge only: `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/src/recon/socket.rs`'s `rebuild_spent`).** The pass that finds the allowance spent still has no balance, the next one opens the new session's first request. The re-dial goes through the gateway's turn, is paced (a minute after one that worked, then 1, 2 and 5 minutes after failures) and is not made while the gateway's own rebuild schedule of a lost link is armed; a re-dial that fails leaves the client with no connection, and then its orders, fills and positions reads fail too (with the same words) until a later try works. Not proven against a gateway: the trigger is a second stream error on one connection (`docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` names which), which no drill can order.

### Changed

- **IBKR: an order that OPENS exposure off a delayed or frozen stream is refused when it is a MARKET order, or when its limit or trigger price is more than 5 percent from the delayed mid, in words, before anything reaches the gateway (the owner's standing default, E07; decision 0140's 2026-10-27 amendment; the ibkr bridge only: `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/src/delayed_order.rs`).** The owner's accounts have no real-time stock entitlement, so every stock is delayed (about 15 minutes old): until now a MARKET order's notional and the exposure checks read that stale mark and nothing judged a limit against it. A LIMIT order within the band, and any order that only closes a position (a flatten, a margin call, a protective exit), go as before; an order with no label or a real-time one is judged by nothing. The refusal is a venue `OrderRejected` (a replay folds it); the band is judged against the delayed mid the bridge's own quote pump saw in the last five minutes and is not judged when it holds none, and a price amendment is not judged. Offline tests only; not proven against a gateway.
- **The control door now sizes a qty-only modify at the price of a modify that came through ANOTHER surface and that the venue has not answered yet, not at the stale published price (`vike-exec`'s engine and read model, `vike-core`'s snapshot builder and `vike-tradehub`'s door: `OrderView::pending_price`, `ExecutionEngine::pending_modify_price`, `ControlLimits`).** The engine remembers the limit price of each modify it sends until `OrderModified` or `OrderModifyRejected` answers it (at most 30 s of engine clock, the last one sent when two are in flight; a side table, nothing in the engine snapshot, the journal or the wire), the snapshot publishes it beside the order, and the door takes the highest of the standing price, that one and the price its own surface remembers. A stop's modify (it moves the trigger) carries none. Command cadence for the write; the publish pays one `is_empty` test per order row.
- **A bracket whose STOP ends unfilled after its entry filled (the adapter refuses the released stop, the venue cancels it, the gate denies it) now says `POSITION WITHOUT STOP` at once, when no other stop covers the position; it only says it, nothing is flattened or re-armed (`vike-core` only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/recon_stops.rs`'s `note_bracket_stop_died`, called by `drive_contingency_on_terminal`; per dead bracket exit, never per event).** Before, the only trace was the "protective exit died unfilled" line, which does not say the position is bare. The line names the stop, its entry, the account, the symbol and the size, carries the venue's reason and the `vike-cli trade position flatten` command. A dying take-profit, a stop beside another covering stop and a flat book say nothing new.
- **A second launch beside a live node, or any journal that cannot be opened at start, now refuses to start in one line and exits 1, instead of panicking with a backtrace over the real sentence (`vike-core`'s start-up only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/journaling.rs`'s `refuse_start_journal_open`, called once by `assemble_core`; nothing on the fold).** The tradehub's root already refused a journal held by a live node before the core was built (`restore_for_boot` takes the same lock), so what changes is the rest: two launches reaching a fresh journal directory together, and a read-only or full disk. The line carries the interlock's own words (it names the directory and the cure).
- **A boot restore that SKIPS a journaled engine (the account's market or ledger label changed, the venue differs, two snapshots carry one key) no longer lets a halted account come up active, and says what it dropped (`vike-core`'s boot restore only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/boot_restore.rs`'s `apply_restored_engines`; once per start, before the first message, nothing on the fold).** The journaled Halted or Reducing state now reaches the engine that owns the key, as a tier refusal always did (with duplicate snapshots the engine ends at the strictest), and a skip whose book held an open position or a resting order is an ERROR naming them (a WARN as before when the book was flat; a stopped account's tombstone stays INFO).
- **Studio "Connect to Claude" (the non-default `mcp` feature) registers the `vike-cli` that is really there: the file beside the running executable when it exists, else the bare name `vike-cli` for `claude` to find on its `PATH`. It used to print the sibling path whether or not a file sat at it.**
- **The desktop's GPU toggle in the caption is visible and clickable again (issue #2320): it is drawn before the File / View / Window / Help menus, because egui's menu bar claims the rest of the row and the toggle, drawn after it, was laid out past the window's edge. A layout test pins that its rectangle is inside the caption.**
- **The FXCM shim is built against, and deployed over, the libraries the pin describes (deploy path, `scripts/release_fxcm_artifact.sh`, `crates/bridges/fxcm/scripts/package-fcsdk-runtime.sh`, `deploy/sbin/vike-trader-ci-deploy`): the release build now hash-verifies the whole ForexConnect SDK tree against `FCSDK.linux.sha256` before it compiles (it only checked that two files existed) and appends the pinned rows to the published shim as an SDK record; the deploy helper compares that record with the box's `<root>/lib` and REFUSES a shim built against other libraries (the old shim stays, `bin/.built-from` says `TOOLS-REFUSED:libfcshim.so`, `verify-tools` goes red). A shim with no record (an older release) and a box with none of the libraries install as before. Takes effect once the root-owned helper is reinstalled.**
- **The deploy helper no longer installs from a directory the CI runner can write: it copies the downloaded release assets once into a root-only directory (`/var/lib/vike-trader-deploy/staging`), verifies `SHA256SUMS` over the copy, installs from the copy, and removes it on every ending; a symlink in the download is refused by name. This closes the window between the checksum and the install in which a process of the runner's user could swap a staged file. Takes effect once the root-owned helper is reinstalled.**
- **`package-fcsdk-runtime.sh` (`just fxcm-package`) installs each library and the shim through a temporary beside the file and a rename, as the deploy helper does, instead of an in-place `cp -f`: a running gatewayhub that has the shim or a library mapped keeps the old inode and no longer risks a SIGBUS. `--verify` hashes the staged SDK against the pin and copies nothing; `--record` prints the pinned rows.**
- **`just the CI box` lanes link with mold and cap nextest at 8 threads (`LANE_MOLD`, `LANE_NEXTEST_THREADS`), `just release` refuses a candidate whose `release-prep` moved the version (set `ALLOW_COLD_CANDIDATE=1` to override) and cancels a duplicate tag run; two wrong CI statements (sccache sharing, which runner is slower) are corrected.**
- **cTrader: a net-sized `reduce_only` stop or limit over SEVERAL hedged positions now rests as one bound order per position instead of being refused, and the engine still sees ONE order (cTrader bridge only: `crates/bridges/ctrader/src/exit_legs.rs`, `exec.rs`'s `submit_split`, `positions.rs`'s `split_exit_among`; nothing in a shared crate).** One venue order binds to one position, so such an exit used to end as a terminal `OrderRejected` (`EXIT_SPANS_POSITIONS`) and every one of those positions stayed without it. It is now planned over the positions facing it (oldest first, each leg the room that position has, snapped down to the symbol's step, at least its minimum volume) and placed as one bound order per position under the leg coids `<coid>L<n>`; the legs' events are folded into the one lifecycle the engine expects (one accept, a fill per leg, `OrderFilled` only when every leg filled, one cancel when the last leg is gone, a reject only when nothing was ever accepted) at the one place every event leaves the connection (`emit_event`). The engine's cancel cancels every resting leg, all or none; an amend of the exit is refused (cancel and place again). ⚠ The engine is NOT told when one leg ends unfilled while its siblings rest (an `error` log line), the group does not survive a bridge restart (the legs are then plain exits `<coid>L<n>`), the legs cover only what the positions hold, and none of it is measured on a demo account yet. The second window of the cover count is closed too: an amend counts at the larger of the exit's size and the asked one from the request until the venue answers. Offline proof (unit, dispatcher and `tests/offline/exec_resting.rs` tests, the pinned refusals rewritten). `crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md`, "An exit that spans positions rests as one bound order per position".
- **cTrader: a symbol the broker restricts, frees or hides while the session runs is followed (cTrader bridge only: `crates/bridges/ctrader/src/conn/symbol_state.rs`, `symbols.rs`'s `SymbolMap::set_restrictions`, `trading_state.rs`'s `refreshed`).** The exec client refused an opening order from the trading state the broker reported when the session FIRST connected, and `ProtoOASymbolChangedEvent` was an unhandled frame, so a symbol re-enabled (or newly disabled) later stayed as it was until the session was rebuilt. The state is now a shared cell the actor rewrites at every reconnect and, on the event, after asking the venue for the light list and the changed symbols' records again; a refresh that fails keeps the table and says so. Only the trading state is refreshed (not digits or the volume grid). ⚠ NOT measured live: a demo account cannot be made to change a symbol, so the event's arrival is played by a scripted venue only (`tests/symbol_state.rs`); the control door still does not carry the state (a change to the shared instrument record, not made here). `crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md`, "A symbol the broker forbids is refused by name".
- **cTrader: a `reduce_only` MARKET order (`market-exit`, `flatten`, a margin-call liquidation, a mount-budget flatten) on a hedged account no longer opens a hedge when the bridge's position book is empty; it reads the venue's positions first and closes by position id, or is refused by name (cTrader bridge only: `crates/bridges/ctrader/src/exec.rs`'s `submit`, `conn/reconcile.rs`'s `read_positions_now`; nothing in a shared crate).** The book a reduce is routed by is empty and not authoritative after a connect-time seed that failed on a start that held a position (15 of 15 starts seeded in about 24 ms, so it takes a failed seed) and after a socket death, and a plain market order sent against it OPENED a position beside the one it meant to close (the locked pair the engine books as flat); the known-limitations row pinned that as expected-open. Now an order that finds nothing facing it and a book that is not authoritative sends one `ProtoOAReconcileReq` on the actor's socket (`Command::ReadPositions`, bounded by the seed's 1.5 s, the order waits at most 5 s) and closes what the venue lists by id; nothing facing it after that is a terminal `OrderRejected` by name (`NOTHING_TO_REDUCE` when the list was read, `POSITIONS_UNVERIFIED` when it could not be) and nothing is sent. An engaged HALT is exempt from the refusal and only from it: the venue is still read and what it lists is still closed by id, but with nothing facing the order, or an unreadable list, the order is admitted on its flag and goes out as before (the halt predicate and `halt_admit` are untouched), and a NETTED account is not asked and not refused. Offline proof against the in-process fake venue, red on the base (the table test that pinned the plain order flips); not yet measured on a demo account (the proof script is owed to the first deploy that carries this). `crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md`, "A hedged account closes a reduce-only market order by position id".

- **cTrader: a resting exit that outlived its position while no bridge was watching is now FOUND at connect and named in the log, never cancelled (cTrader bridge only: `crates/bridges/ctrader/src/conn/reconcile.rs`'s `flag_orphaned_exits`, `positions.rs`'s `OrphanedExit`; nothing in a shared crate).** The venue does not cancel a bound order when its position closes another way, and a stale bound stop that reaches the market OPENS a position under the reused position id (measured on the hedged demo account, 2026-10-26). The bridge cancels the exits it saw its position leave; an exit whose position closed while the daemon was down, or in the cTrader platform, is indistinguishable in a reconcile answer from a plain pending order (both name a position that is not open). The exec start now looks each such resting STOP or LIMIT up with `ProtoOAOrderListByPositionIdReq` (without bounds, then over the last week if the venue refuses that; at most 16 look-ups inside the seed's 1.5 s): a FILLED order of that position other than the exit proves the position existed and is gone, and the exit is logged at `error` (`ORPHANED EXIT`: the order, coid, position, side, size and price, "WILL OPEN a position", "cancel it by hand") and kept in `PositionBook::orphaned_exits` until its order ends. A look-up that cannot prove (unanswered, refused, truncated with no fill) leaves the order as it was and says so in a `warn`; a book the seed could not read in full, a netted account and a data-only start look at nothing. ⚠ The bridge NEVER cancels such an order (it is its owner's; the operator cancels it by hand), the held `UnknownOrder` row in `trade recon ls` still does not carry the words (that needs an optional note on the shared order report, a coordinated change: the known-limitations row says so), and the look-up is NOT measured on a demo account yet. Offline proof against the in-process fake venue (`crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/connect_orphans.rs`) and unit tests of the pure rules; red on the base, which had no look-up. `crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md`, "A bound exit that outlived its position is flagged at connect, never cancelled".
- **A keyless public GET follows a stated five redirects on purpose, and the two HTTP agents outside the venue stack state their limit instead of inheriting ureq's ten (`vike-bridge-core`'s `http::public_get_agent` and `PUBLIC_GET_MAX_REDIRECTS`, used by `get_json`, the catalog read of binance, bybit, okx and deribit; `vike-datahub`'s `UreqHttp`; `vike-backfill`'s `build_agent`; Deribit's option-chain read).** A catalog host that moves its endpoint behind a 301/302/308 used to fail the read with `HTTP 30x`; now it is followed, and a loop fails after five hops with `too many redirects`. Every venue builder (`blocking_agent` and its three siblings, so every SIGNED call) still follows none, pinned by a test over all four. Not changed, and in the `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` row: the kline and history pagers still ride the no-redirect agents, and ureq strips only `Authorization` and `Cookie` on a redirect, so a custom credential header (`X-API-KEY`, `X-Finnhub-Token`) would travel to a redirect's host if one ever named another.
- **A WebSocket dial that takes the bounded arm no longer waits for ever on a peer that accepts the TCP connection and then says nothing: the TLS + WebSocket handshake behind the dial bound has the same window as its read timeout (`vike-bridge-core`'s `ws_proxy::connect_ws` only; the Deribit order socket is the case that was open, `DeribitOrderTransport::connect` now fails with `no answer within <window>`; every other bounded dial, the market pumps and the depth driver included, gets the same bound).** The window is a READ bound, not a deadline, and is cleared again once the socket is up, so a socket leaves `connect_ws` with no read timeout exactly as before and a quiet healthy feed never times out on it. The unbounded arm (`connect_timeout: None`) and the SOCKS arm are untouched. Pinned by `crates/vike-bridge-core/src/ws_proxy_tests.rs` (a silent `ws://` and `wss://` peer, and the cleared option) and `crates/bridges/deribit/tests/offline/dial_bound.rs`; the Deribit FILL stream's own dial is still a bare `tungstenite::connect` (a row of `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`).
- **Deribit: the fill pump's dial is bounded like the order socket's, and the three start logs say what failed (`crates/bridges/deribit/src/user_data.rs`'s `open_deribit_user_data_ws`, the exec lane's `dial_timeout` row).** The pump dialed with a bare `tungstenite::connect`, so a peer that accepted the connection and said nothing pinned the pump thread in the dial with its stop flag unread (a stop of the start waited for it, with no error logged); it now fails the open as a reconnectable transport error after the dial window (`no answer within <window>`). The "order-WS auth failed" lines of the exec, resync and recon starts now read "could not be opened (dial or auth, the error names which)", because a dial failure such as the testnet's 502s of 2026-10-27 (13:11 to 13:26 UTC) was logged as an auth failure. Pinned by `crates/bridges/deribit/tests/offline/dial_bound.rs` (a silent peer for the pump, and a 502 to the upgrade for the order socket). Not changed, in the `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` row: a start made during a dial outage still runs degraded for its life.
- **Deribit: a stop the venue ends on its own now ENDS on the node, and a restart adopts or retires a Deribit stop on proof (the Deribit bridge, plus the one-line `deribit` entry of `vike-gatewayhub-client`'s `RECON_LISTS_TRIGGER_ORDERS` and its conformance row; nothing else in a shared crate changes).** Until now the fill pump subscribed `user.trades` only, so a stop cancelled by someone else, or a reduce-only stop that fired on a flat position and was refused, left the engine's order `ACCEPTED` for good (the venue keeps no trace of either in the label lookup or the order history). The pump now also subscribes `user.orders.any.any.raw` in a call of its own BEFORE the fills' (a venue refusal of it only warns; the fills' ack stays the last step of the open), and `crates/bridges/deribit/src/event_mapper.rs`'s `map_deribit_order_row` turns the rows of a stop, and of the order a fired stop placed (`trigger_order_id`), into `OrderCanceled` (cancelled, or refused: never `OrderRejected`, which the order FSM refuses after the accept) and `OrderTriggered`; every ordinary order's row maps to nothing. The A3 history replay says the same word for a stop whose child shows `rejected`. Dedup is downstream (the FSM and the gatewayhub's `OnceMemory`), pinned in `crates/bridges/deribit/tests/offline/stop_events.rs`. The Deribit reconcile client now CLAIMS to list trigger orders (decision 0192's three edits), so after a restart an operator's stop on a `demo` account is adopted and a stop the venue ended without a fill is gone after the quiet passes. ⚠ The `user.orders` row shapes are the venue's documented ones, not captures, and a restart across a stop that fired while the node was down is not yet proved on the testnet: the 0.1.97 kit's Deribit stop drill (B10) records both; the row of `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` says what is open.
- **While a market is closed, more than one resting limit or stop order now fits under the account exposure ceiling: a resting LIMIT, STOP, STOP-LIMIT or TAKE-PROFIT order whose symbol has no market price counts at its own limit or trigger, where the first one used to pass against an empty book and every later one was denied `account-exposure-unpriced` (the exposure sum of `vike-exec` only: `crates/vike-exec/src/execution_engine/valuation.rs`'s `live_order_notional` and `resting_own_price`, a per-order walk that runs only when `max_account_exposure` is armed; no fold, publish or unarmed engine is touched).** Measured on oanda and cTrader demo while FX was closed (2026-10-24). The market's price is read first, so an open market is bit-identical; a MARKET order and a position with no mark stay unpriced and still deny, and an order that does not fit is still refused `over-account-exposure`. A resting order's stated price can sit on the wrong side of a gapped reopen, so the sum may understate the book at the reopen by the gap (the known-limitations row says it). Known-limitations row and decision 0042 amended. MEASURED crate: the the latency box latency A/B is skipped by the owner's ruling for this release and OWED.

- **The price pump of a symbol no account admitted is now closed even while its venue has a gap open, and the close ENDS the gap, so the core's link dead-man window for that symbol closes with it instead of tripping after its grace (a cancel and a HALT of the venue) (the `vike-tradehub` price tap and reaper only: `crates/vike-tradehub/src/feeds/price_tap.rs`'s `PriceTap::end_gap`, called by `CexWatcher::close_ticks`, and `crates/vike-tradehub/src/remote_backend/facts.rs`'s `close_idle`; `vike-core` is untouched).** The reaper used to keep such a pump while the gap stayed open on every venue the dead-man arms, so a pair whose stream cannot connect held one of the `MAX_WATCHED` places for ever (`gap_holds_pump` is deleted; oanda and ig were the one exception and are now the rule). The `Live` goes out on the stream word and with the gap time the `GapStart` carried, after the lane is closed. A symbol an account admitted keeps its pump, as before. Known-limitations row, decision 0174 and the crate pages amended.

- **The control door says the real reason in three more places (the `vike-tradehub` door and the `vike-config` loader only: `crates/vike-tradehub/src/server/symbol_admission.rs`, `crates/vike-tradehub/src/remote_backend/facts.rs`, `crates/vike-config/src/config.rs`'s `node_ack_wait_below_hold_warning`; no core, bridge or wire change).** (1) An opening order on a new symbol whose price never came is refused with the lane's own verdict when the venue's stream for it is in a gap (`has no price on this node after 4 s: its price stream is DOWN (...) ... a retry cannot help until that stream is back`), instead of `retry in a moment`; the old words stay when the stream is simply quiet. (2) An order on the engine's own symbol typed in another spelling (dukascopy `USD/JPY` for `USDJPY`, a lower-case deribit id) is sized by the notional ceiling from the engine's grid row under the engine's own name, where the typed name found no row and fell to the default value (an inverse contract's 10 dollars was refused as 40,000). (3) A `config.node_ack_wait_ms` row shorter than the door's 4 s price hold still loads and is honoured, and now draws a loader warning at every boot and in `vike-cli config check` (a client that hangs up inside the hold never reads its refusal); the live-account hint now says `<amount in the account's currency>`. The first half of the JPY-notional proposal (a pair the door refuses is refused in the door's words, never sized in its quote money) shipped in 0.1.93.

- **One slow venue's conversion-rate read no longer delays any other venue's next rate tick: the rate timer now hands each venue's share to that venue's own long-lived worker instead of joining scoped per-tick threads (the `vike-tradehub` rate timer only: `crates/vike-tradehub/src/remote_backend/facts.rs`'s `spawn_rate_refresher` and `RatePool`; no core, bridge or wire change).** Before, a venue whose read outlasted the 60 s period (IBKR with many silent currencies, seconds per pair) held the next tick of OANDA and every other venue behind it, and an OANDA rate could cross the engine's 120 s staleness window (opening orders denied `quote-rate-stale`). Now the tick that finds a venue still reading skips it, and its worker reads once more at once when it is done; a read that panics costs that read, not the worker; a worker the OS refuses runs inline as before. `refresh_held_rates` stays as the synchronous form for callers that want the whole pass finished (tests). Known-limitations row and crate pages amended.
- **The core books every fee it is told, and a fee it cannot read is counted instead of silently zero (`vike-exec`, `vike-core`, `vike-bridge-core` and the binance, bybit and okx event mappers; FEES-AUDIT 2026-10-26 §4.8 a, b, c, e).** (a) A forced-close (liquidation) fee reached `balance` and nothing else, so every liquidation under-stated `fees_paid` (the GUI's `fees` column, the tradehub summary line) and the own-PnL the drawdown latch reads: `Account::apply_liquidation` now books it into `fees_paid` and the per-asset tally with the sign and the conversion a trade commission gets (the frozen `fixtures/r0` liquidation scenario is compared against a stated function of its bytes, the third instance of `docs/decisions/0021-python-oracle-retired-vike-is-the-reference.md`). (b) The per-mount ledger (`dispatch_applied_fills`) added the RAW commission, so on an inverse contract (deribit: the fee is ETH or BTC) the mount's net PnL, the drawdown latch and the per-mount budget saw the fee at about 1/2,000 to 1/50,000 of its dollar value; it now takes the charge the account booked (`Account::commission_in_quote`). (c) `Account::apply_account_state` adopted a LONE balance whatever it was called, so binance's ACCOUNT_UPDATE listing only `BNB` (a fee paid in BNB) wrote half a BNB into `balance`; a lone balance is now adopted only when it is the quote asset or a dollar label against a dollar label (dukascopy's one `USD` frame and a `USDC` wallet still are), and any other is reported in `balances_by_asset` and adopts nothing. The sum of several non-quote assets is unchanged (the frozen `account_state_fallbacks` fixture pins it). (e) `n` (binance), `execFee` (bybit) and `fillFee` (okx) that are present and not a number used to become a silent `0.0`; `vike_bridge_core::json::get_fee_f64` keeps the booking and adds `malformed_fee_count` and a `FEE NOT READ` warning on the 1st, 10th, 100th occurrence. Nothing on the submit hop or in the per-message fold changes: the liquidation arm runs per liquidation, the mount ledger per fill after the fold, the lone-balance guard per wallet frame.

- **The static fee schedules now match what the node measured (`vike-venues`'s `fee_schedule_for`, `vike-catalog`'s `fee_lane`; paper, simulator, backtest and display only: a LIVE fill books the venue's own figure, as before).** (1) A Deribit PERPETUAL (`...-PERPETUAL`) resolves to a new lane `deribit-perp`, flat 0 bps maker (published, unmeasured) and 5 bps taker (measured on ETH-PERPETUAL, testnet), instead of the options row (3 bps of the underlying, capped at 12.5 % of the premium) that charged a perpetual paper mount 3 bps both ways; dated futures and options keep the bare row. (2) The IBKR cap is 1 % of the trade value (it was 0.5 %, unsourced). (3) cTrader is no longer `Free`: 3.00 USD per lot (100,000 base units) per side, from the 94 fills of the hedged demo account (`PerShareWithFloor`, 0.00003 USD a unit; right for the FX majors, wrong for a spread-only account and for symbols whose lot is another size, so the backtest refuses it on a non-dollar ledger like IBKR's). (4) A Hyperliquid SPOT pair (`HYPE/USDC` or `HYPE-USDC`) resolves to a new lane `hyperliquid-spot`, 4 bps maker and 7 bps taker (published base tier, no spot fill was ever measured), instead of the perp row (1.5 and 4.5); HIP-3 builder-dex perps are not encoded. A caller that passes the bare venue string (the docs generator, `funding_carry`) still gets the bare row. Consumers checked: the tradehub paper mount and the gatewayhub arming goldens (ibkr and ctrader lines), the backtest `kind = "venue"` table and its dollar-ledger refusal, the Studio cost model, the xEMM and maker break-even floors (a per-share shape is refused as before), `venues.json`.

- **Binance, aster, bybit and okx quotes now carry their machine receive time (`QuoteTick::local_ts`), so their feed latency can be measured like hyperliquid's, deribit's, oanda's and ig's.** The three tick pumps (`crates/bridges/binance/src/family/depth.rs`, `crates/bridges/bybit/src/market_data.rs`, `crates/bridges/okx/src/market_data.rs`) left `local_ts` at the "not stamped" `0` on every quote; each now stamps `now_ms()` where the quote leaves the pump (`send_quote`), on the venue thread, one clock read per quote, nothing in the core's fold. The pure decoders still stamp nothing and keep the venue's `ts`. The TRADES those tick pumps send are not changed (the separate trade feeds, `market_feed/trades.rs`, already stamp theirs; the strategy lane reads a trade's `ts` only), and the three trade-decoder `TODO(book-recording plan)` lines now say so.

- **OKX: the funding of an admitted SWAP is folded, a batch submit carries the FD-broker tag, and the reconcile pass watches the account's position mode (`vike-okx`; FEES-AUDIT 2026-10-26 §4.7, known-limitations "okx" rows on funding and on the mode watch).** (1) The bills query named the MOUNTED `instId` only, so the funding paid on any other SWAP the engine had admitted never reached `funding_paid` or the balance until a reconcile reseeded it. The adapter now hands the reconcile client and the funding poll ONE admitted-instrument list: with nothing admitted the request is byte for byte the old one; with something admitted it reads the account's SWAP bills once and folds the mounted and the admitted instruments only (a position opened by hand on another instrument is not the ledger's), an admitted one from the poll after the one that first saw it, so a settlement that landed before the admission is not counted twice with the wallet a reconcile adopts. (2) `submit_batch` built every row with no `tag`, so a batched order was unattributed while a single one carried the broker code; it now carries it. (3) On a DEMO account the reconcile pass reads `account/config`'s `posMode` once and logs an `error!` when the account is long/short while the engine runs (the start probe only saw the mode at the start) and a `warn!` when it is back; nothing is written, a LIVE account is never read for a mode, and the line is said once per flip. Proved offline only: no demo run of the funding fold across a settlement or of a mode flip.

- **The two opt-in early-fill settings now say what they cost, and the live fee asserts check the fee (`vike-venues`, binance, bybit and okx tests; FEES-AUDIT 2026-10-26 §4.9, §4.12).** `venue.binance.trade_lite_fill` and `venue.bybit.fast_exec` (`vike-cli config venue`) book the early fill with a commission of 0 and then drop the real fee as a duplicate, so `fees_paid` stays short while either is on; the setting text says it. The binance, bybit and okx round-trip smokes asserted `fees_paid != 0.0`, which a negative figure or one a thousand times off also passed; they now require a charge between half the table row's maker rate and 1.5 times its taker rate of the notional traded. The binance and bybit captured-fill replays read the captured fee (binance: a BUY's BTC fee as quote units; bybit: `execFee` unsigned and equal to `execValue` times `feeRate`), and a captured okx taker fill (the demo capture of 2026-10-24) is pinned as a positive charge at the taker rate.
- **A bybit, okx or binance DEMO account that states a leverage while its account mode is wrong (binance hedge or isolated, bybit hedge symbol or isolated margin, okx long/short) now gets the figure at its FIRST start, and a binance hedge account is switched to one-way by the first refused order once it is flat (`vike-gatewayhub`'s trade lane, the three bridges' exec halves and `vike-bridge-core`'s `VenueAdapter`, which gains one defaulted verb `heal_modes`; nothing in `vike-core`, `vike-exec` or `vike-model`, no wire or journal change).** The lane's read-only leverage probe ran BEFORE the bridge's start-time mode switch, read the old mode and refused the figure, so the account was written the default leverage at the very start that then fixed its mode, and the figure waited for `account.active` off and on. Now the lane asks the bridge to run its own switch first (`bridge_trade.rs`'s `heal_modes_before_probe`, at a start and at a symbol's commit, only where the probe itself would run; each bridge keeps its demo-only gate, so a mainnet account is never read or written for a mode) and then probes; a switch the venue refuses (the account is not flat) is a WARN and the probe refuses the figure as before. Separately, binance's start-time switch to one-way was never retried: the venue refuses it while the account holds a position or a resting order, and every later order was rejected for the hedge mode until the next start. The first such reject now reads the position mode again (one read, a write only while it still reads hedge; demo host only; paced per process, a rejected batch is one probe, `modes.rs`'s `reject_reason`, whose pacing and error code `crates/bridges/binance/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` give). The order that met the reject stays rejected and is not resent: its reason says to send it again or what still blocks. Proved offline only (`modes_tests.rs`, `posted_leverage_tests.rs`: the heal-before-probe order and the retry's four outcomes); the hedge to one-way write itself has never run against the venue, and its demo drill is named in `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`.
- **Hyperliquid: the door's facts for a `demo` (testnet) account are now the TESTNET's universe, not mainnet's (`vike-gatewayhub` only: `BridgeTrade::symbol_facts`, `SymbolFacts::facts_on` and the composition root's testnet listing; no wire, node, core or journal change).** The gatewayhub answered every account's `symbol facts` from one mainnet `HyperliquidCatalog`, so a testnet account could be admitted a coin its network does not list (measured 2026-10-26: 19 mainnet coins, XRP and LINK among them), which spent one of the 16 extra-symbol slots before the adapter refused the order (`unknown symbol X: Hyperliquid's testnet list has no such coin`), and a coin both networks list was admitted on mainnet's grid (the adapter then re-rounds on its own network's). The lane now asks the catalog of the ASKING account's network (`Network::for_tier(tier)`; `HyperliquidCatalog::for_network(Network::Testnet)`, core markets only, kept ten minutes under its own key and failure-remembered apart from mainnet's): a coin only mainnet lists is refused at the door for a `demo` account in words that name the testnet and spends no slot, the same coin is sized on the testnet's own grid, and a `live` account is answered from mainnet's as before. Proved offline only (`symbol_facts_tests.rs`, `bridge_trade_tests.rs`); the testnet drill is `deploy/next97`'s B08 script.
- **The per-symbol leverage write (`VenueAdapter::set_symbol_leverage`: bybit, okx, binance) guards its own tier and no longer reports a POST whose answer was lost as refused (`vike-bridge-core`'s `LeverageWriteError` and `leverage_read::settle`, the three bridges' exec halves and `vike-gatewayhub`'s lane; nothing in `vike-core`, `vike-exec` or `vike-model`, no wire or journal change).** (1) The verb had no tier check of its own, so `vike_secrets::LEVERAGE_VENUES` was the only thing keeping a per-symbol write off mainnet and opening `live` for bybit or okx in that table would have opened it. bybit's and okx's `write_symbol_leverage` now refuse a `live` account before any client exists (`demo` only); binance's stays open at `demo` and the `live` lane twin, as the owner opened it (decision 0182). (2) A timeout, a 5xx or a status-unknown venue code on the POST was reported as "refused" and healed only by a later commit, although the write may have landed. The verb now says how it failed (`Refused` or `Ambiguous`, the bridge's own `error_codes::submit_outcome_unknown` rule), and `settle` reads the venue back for an ambiguous one exactly as after a clean write: a venue seen holding the figure is a success (one write, no retry), one that is not is an error worded as an UNKNOWN outcome, not as a refusal. Proved offline only (`exec_tests.rs` of the three bridges: ambiguous vs refused, the mainnet refusal; `leverage_read.rs` and `posted_leverage_tests.rs`: the read-back of a lost write).
- **The held reconcile balance of an oanda, ctrader or fxcm account whose currency the start only ASSUMED (USD, decision 0189) now lifts by itself once the venue states that very USD, and the gatewayhub's currency memory follows re-pointed keys (`vike-gatewayhub`'s trade lane, `vike-gatewayhub-client`'s `WireSymbolFacts` and `vike-tradehub`'s balance gate; one additive wire key, no journal change).** A rate stamp equal to an assumed anchor proves nothing (the lanes stamp `USD` for an assumed USD exactly as for a stated one), so a start whose currency read failed on an account that really is USD kept the balance held, with `balance held: assumed USD` standing, until `account.active` went off and on. The gatewayhub now adds the proof beside the stamp (`WireSymbolFacts::account_ccy_stated`, written only when true: the venue itself named that currency to some reader; oanda and ctrader from the currency memory, fxcm from its session), and the node raises the lift flag of an `Assumed` binding on the first facts answer that is proven and equal to the ledger's anchor (a symbol lookup, a preview or the rate timer's refresh), so the next reconcile pass adopts the venue's cash and `balance held` is withdrawn (`balance hold ended` at `info`). The gatewayhub's own belt (`balance_withheld`) lets go with it. A venue that names ANOTHER currency lifts nothing, every other binding has no flag, and ig (its facts stamp no ledger) still waits for a start. The gatewayhub's `CCY_SAID` memory is also bound to a one-way fingerprint of the account's credentials, so keys re-pointed under one label to an account in another currency drop what was stated and assumed for the old one with a `warn` (no gatewayhub restart needed any more; ctrader's rotated token pair is part of the key set, so a store re-read after a rotation drops the memory as a restart does). A node over an older gatewayhub (or the reverse) reads no proof and lifts nothing.
- **An engine whose ledger currency is only the owner's assumed USD now says so on the snapshot and in `trade equity` (`vike-exec`'s `VenueBlock::ccy_assumed` and `ExecutionEngine::set_account_ccy_assumed`, `vike-core`'s `snapshot::build`, `vike-tradehub-core`'s engine assembly, the observe frame's optional `ccy_assumed` key, `vike-app-core`'s observe bridge and one line of `vike-cli`'s `trade equity`).** The flag lived in the logs and the balance-held reason only. It is presentation (nothing folds on it, it is not journaled and not in `EngineSnapshot`; journal VERSION stays 21), absent from the frame while false, and read as false from an older node; the desktop, Telegram, `trade status` and `trade doctor` do not read it yet. ⚠ `snapshot::build` copies one more bool per engine per publish, so the the latency box latency A/B of the release owes it.
### Added

- **IG: an admitted epic is margined at IG's own `marginFactor` (the base factor of a percentage figure, as the epic's own margin rate) instead of the engine's configured rate, which for an account that set none was full notional. The figure rides a new optional `margin_rate` on the gatewayhub's symbol facts (an older node ignores it) and an account's confirmed leverage, where a venue posts one, still wins. It has not yet been compared with a booked margin (this release's live-test kit does).
