The symbol picker's IG search now runs over one kept, rate-capped login instead of a login per search; the Trade window itself still cannot pick an epic, because no wire carries a picker's query to the gatewayhub.**

### Changed

- **IG: every market-data subscription of a client (a mount's quote lane, each bar interval and each extra epic the control door admits) now rides ONE IG login and ONE Lightstreamer socket, where each was its own `POST /session` and its own socket of the same API key (IG's FAQ warns that several concurrent connections may get a key suspended; a busy key came to about six sessions or more by hand count).** A subscription IG refuses, that goes silent or that stalls costs only a `delete` and a new `add` on the shared session instead of a whole redial, so one stalled epic no longer interrupts the quotes of the others; a connection that really ends is dialed once for all its lanes with the kept login; a 41st subscription (IG allows 40 per connection) is refused in words. The lanes' redial ladders, wording and silence and stall watches are unchanged; the exec trade stream, the REST sessions and a second data client of the same account are other sessions and are not folded in. Bridge only (`crates/bridges/ig/src/ls_link.rs`, decision 0202): no journal, wire, core or setting change. The count of logins and sockets after N epics on the demo gateway is the live proof owed (the 0.1.97 kit).

### Fixed

- **IG: a fill no longer carries the time 0 (1970). An order that states no time (one from the command line or the control door) is stamped when the bridge handled it, and a streamed working-order fill or cancel is stamped when the bridge heard it (the confirm's own `date` is a zone-less text the lane read as a number, so it was always 0). An opening order on a SHARES market is refused in words, because IG charges commission on shares that nothing here reads and the fill would have booked a fee of 0; and a rejection for the market's state (`MARKET_CLOSED`, `MARKET_OFFLINE`, closings-only) or its dealing rules (`MINIMUM_ORDER_SIZE_ERROR`, market orders not allowed) now names the `marketStatus` or `dealingRules` field that answers it, after IG's own code.**
- **OANDA: a fill that happens while the node is down now names its order after the restart, instead of leaving only a position drift (OANDA bridge only: `crates/bridges/oanda/src/fill_floor.rs`, `recon_client.rs`'s `OandaReconClient::connect` and `fetch_fill_reports`, and the adapter's start handing the declared state directory; no change to the journal, a setting or a shared crate; two workspace crates, `vike-paths` and `vike-util`, become dependencies of `vike-oanda` and add no package).** The reconcile client's fill floor started at the account's latest transaction at every connect, so a stop that fired during a restart (measured 2026-10-26: 35 s into a 150 s stop) lay below it and the first pass reported only a held `PositionDrift`. The floor a pass reaches is now kept in `<state dir>/oanda-fill-floor-<hash>.json` (one file per account, written atomically, never beside `vike.db`) and the next client starts there, so the first pass after the start reads the gap and the fill arrives as a `MissingFill` carrying its client order id. A first start, a start with no state directory, a floor above the account's latest transaction and a floor more than 500 transactions behind it start where they always did. Offline fakes only; the live check is one stop of ours filling while the node is down. Keep this venue on `quarantine`.
- **OANDA: a reduce-only order on a HEDGING account now says so to the venue (`positionFill` `REDUCE_ONLY`), and a reduce-only market order is refused by name while the account's hedging setting is unknown, instead of the order going out plain and possibly opening a locked opposite position the node cannot see (OANDA bridge only: `crates/bridges/oanda/src/hedging.rs` and `exec.rs`'s `run_on`; nothing in a shared crate but one capability-row comment; no new dependency).** The exec thread reads `hedgingEnabled` from `GET /summary` once, before its first command; a netting account, which is the only account measured (practice account 14 states `hedgingEnabled=false`), sends the same bytes it always did, and a replace of a reduce-only order keeps the word. An unreadable setting is asked again by the next reduce-only order; meanwhile a reduce-only limit or stop goes out as before. The `REDUCE_ONLY` word has not met a hedging venue (offline fakes only; the live proof needs a hedging practice account).
- **FXCM: an admitted pair nobody holds anything in no longer keeps the price poll running for the life of the process (tradehub only: `crates/vike-tradehub/src/remote_backend/facts.rs`'s `LeaseFacts::reap_idle_admitted`, the table `REAPS_IDLE_ADMITTED` names fxcm alone, `readmit.rs`'s `symbol_holdings`).** Every admitted pair stayed wanted until the process ended, so one order on a second pair meant a ForexConnect refresh every two seconds on the one reconcile login for good. A check every 15 seconds now closes the pair's price pump once every account that admitted it has shown no position and no live order in it for five minutes, and opens it again when one holds something; the admission stays, so the next order on the pair is held for its first price or refused `has no price on this node yet` once. A pair a lane twin, an engine's held lane or a mount prices, and one under an open venue gap, is never closed. Offline fakes only; not run against a ForexConnect session.
- **A position held in an admitted symbol is now valued at the venue's live quotes, not at the price the admission saw (`vike-exec`'s `ExecutionEngine::seed_initial_mark`; found on an FXCM demo account, it holds for every venue that states no mark of its own).** The control door seeds the price it observed into the admission as the engine's first price, and the engine filed it in the price board's venue-MARK rung, which the node's price settings never age and which outranks every quote: an fxcm pair (and an oanda, ig, ctrader, dukascopy or ibkr one: no mark stream, no reconcile mark, fills carry none) kept the unrealized PnL of its entry spread for as long as it was held while the market moved 17 pips and the quotes were reaching the engine, and the pre-trade gate judged the next order's price collar and notional against the same stale price. The seed now sits in the board's weakest rung, so the first quote, trade or mark replaces it; until one arrives it is still the price, and a venue that states a mark (the crypto perpetuals) is unchanged. Cold paths only (one write per admission); nothing in the fold changes. Offline-proven (exec, core and tradehub tests); the live proof is the kit script `fxcmstale-held-pair-stays-fresh.sh` (kept in the kit, outside the repository), owed after the next deploy.
- **The rate timer's "valued at a conversion rate that is NOT being refreshed" line no longer counts the age from a stopped engine (`vike-tradehub`'s `readmit.rs`, `engine_rate_stamp` and `engine_holds_position`).** After an account was stopped and started in the running node the core keeps the stopped engine's block ahead of the new one under the same route key, and the timer's two readers of the raw snapshot took the first block: the line named an fxcm pair's rate 69031 s old (and another 54600 s) for a rate the running engine had refreshed that minute, and a position the stopped engine had held counted as held. Both now read the newest block of the key, as the published frame already did. Offline-proven; read from the the CI box journal of 2026-10-28 (the printed ages equal the time since the stopped engine's last admissions, to the second).
- **A position with no stop on a venue whose capability row declares none is now told in words that claim no more than the row does (`vike-core`'s `recon_stops.rs`, words only).** The reconcile line said the venue "cannot rest a protective stop for this position", untrue on an FXCM hedging account, whose trade-bound stop its order report lists and which counts as cover when it is there; it now says the row declares no reduce-only stop, what the node counts, and to check the venue. When the report lists the stop the line is not said at all, as before.
- **A bracket whose stop died unfilled no longer says the position "keeps its remaining OCO protection" when the survivor is the take-profit (`vike-core`'s `apply/contingency.rs`, words only; the sibling-cancel knob and what is kept are unchanged).** A take-profit closes a winner and leaves the loss open, so that line is now said only when a surviving sibling is a stop; with a take-profit left it says the position has NO stop from this bracket, and with no sibling left it says so.
- **FXCM: the core's own cancel of the sibling exit the venue already removed (the take-profit of a stop that fired) is answered in words instead of reading as a fault (FXCM bridge only: `crates/bridges/fxcm/src/exec.rs`'s `no_resting_order`).** The venue deletes the other exit of a trade in the fire's own batch, so the cancel finds no row; the non-terminal rejection now names the three cases it cannot tell apart (never placed here, already ended, removed by the venue as the other exit of a trade is). No event, state or order changes.
- **`vike-cli trade venue <book> positions` lists what the VENUE says a wallet holds: the third kind of the operator's venue read, Polymarket only (every other venue says `not offered by <venue>`).** It is the answer to a wallet whose older outcome-token holdings the node's engine never took (the funded account's four resolved holdings were shown nowhere): one row per holding with the market in words, the side held, the shares, the price paid, the venue's price and value now, and REDEEMABLE, the venue's own flag, which means the market has RESOLVED and which a losing outcome shows too (it pays nothing, so the table says to read the price and value). Polymarket's bridge reads the public data-api by the account's funder address, keyless (no L2 key is derived, nothing is signed), asking for holdings under one share too. It folds nothing, places and redeems nothing and is no reconcile pass, so `flags.poly_reconcile` is not needed and `trade positions` stays the engine's own list. **The kind owes its own capability word on both wires** (the lease's `gw_trade_venue_positions` in `vike-gatewayhub-client`, the node's `venue-read-positions` in `vike-tradehub-client`; the shared model is `vike_model`'s `VenueReadKind::Positions` / `VenuePosition`): a daemon of the previous build decodes the read frame but not the new kind's name, and a trade frame the daemon cannot decode ENDS the lease, so a client asks only a peer that advertises the word and is refused locally, by name, otherwise (the two older kinds still go to the same peer). Hyperliquid, which answers the other two kinds, says `not offered by hyperliquid` before it loads its key. Real data-api bodies are the fixtures (the funded wallet, and an empty one answers `[]`); the live proof needs the next deploy. The journal is untouched.

### Changed

- **The engine takes the venue's balance before the door opens: a start now waits, bounded, for the first reconcile pass over each account's leg, and an account the venue did not answer stays refused for opening orders by name and with the reason (`vike-tradehub-core`'s reconcile manager and `vike-tradehub`'s boot and account watcher; a cold path, the fold, hop and dispatch untouched; proposed decision 0246; offline-proven, not run live).** Until now an engine judged orders on its configured seed cash until that pass landed the venue's figure, which is wrong in both directions: the node's own boot did not even refuse in that window (the door opens a couple of seconds before the first pass), and a started account was reported as running while the door refused it. Now the live mount does not return, so the door does not open, until every leg's balance has reached its engine or the start's bound has passed, and the account watcher waits the same way before it reports a started account as running; the balance still lands through the reconcile pass's one authoritative write. An account the venue did not answer in time (a failed read, a leg that is not ready, a suppressed feed) is refused opening orders at the door with `account ... awaiting the venue balance ... Why it has not landed: <the leg's words>` while every other account trades; reducing orders, cancels, a flatten and a market exit are never held, and a restart cancels nothing. A strategy the run profile mounts is not behind the door, and a venue whose balance read fails for a standing reason (a cTrader account whose deposit is not in dollars) now keeps its account refused for opening orders where the boot used to trade it on the seed.

## [0.1.96] - 2026-10-27
### Added

- **The gatewayhub can be asked for a READ of an account at its venue: its balance (with the allowance each exchange contract holds, where the venue has one) or the venue's OWN list of its open orders. Polymarket and Hyperliquid answer; every other venue says `not offered by <venue>`. Nothing is placed, cancelled or folded, so a `live` account is as readable as a `demo` one, and no reconcile flag is needed (the node's control door and `vike-cli` have no verb for it yet: only the gatewayhub's trade lease carries it).** A new lease frame pair `TradeUp::VenueRead` / `TradeDown::VenueReadReply` (`vike-gatewayhub-client`, negotiated by the new feature string `gw_trade_venue_read`, so an older daemon or node is told in words and nothing is sent; `TradeSession::venue_read`), the shared vocabulary `vike_model::VenueRead` / `VenueReadKind`, and one defaulted `VenueAdapter::venue_read` (`vike-bridge-core`; no other bridge changes). Polymarket reads `/balance-allowance` and the CLOB's `/data/orders` on the account's own derived L2 key (the wallet's pUSD balance and an old position's resting orders are visible without `flags.poly_reconcile`); Hyperliquid reads the master address's `/info` (`frontendOpenOrders`, the account value). The daemon holds the reads to one in flight per venue and two seconds between the same read of one account, answers a refused one in words without touching the venue, and turns a figure that is not a number into an error before it is written. The gatewayhub-client wire goldens carry both frames; the journal is untouched (VERSION 21).

### Changed

- **The desktop GUI moves to egui 0.37 (`egui`, `eframe`, `egui-wgpu`, `egui_kittest` 0.37; `egui_plot` 0.38). Nothing a trader does changes; no server binary links egui.** The code follows the renamed calls (`Id::unique`, `Ui::scope_id`, `TextEdit::align`, accessibility roles in place of `WidgetType`, the screenshot callback behind `VIKE_SHOT` and File -> Export chart image). egui made its bundled fonts opt-in, so the root `Cargo.toml` names the same font features as before and the glyph set is unchanged. The chart tessellation goldens (18 files) are regenerated for the new tessellator. `egui_code_editor` has no 0.37 release yet, so a copy that differs from 0.4.2 only in its egui requirement lives under `third_party/egui_code_editor` until upstream releases (the root manifest's `[patch.crates-io]` row has the removal recipe).
### Fixed

- **The desktop no longer reuses a client order id: every order it places carries an id that is new to the node, so the node's door never refuses the first order of a session as a repeat (the desktop's order planner `crates/vike-app-core/src/orders/order_dispatch.rs`'s `Planner::coid` and the shell's one `App::coids` field; no node, core, bridge or journal change, and no new dependency).** Since v0.1.95 the node answers a `Submit` whose id an earlier order already carries with `coid X is already used by an order that is FILLED: pick a new client order id`. The desktop numbered its orders `ui-<windows>-0`, `dom-<windows>-0`, `poly-…` and `opt-…` from the window counter, which starts at the number of open windows at every launch, so a second launch with the same layout sent the first launch's ids again, and loading another layout in the middle of a session set the counter back to that layout's window count and did the same. Orders now take their ids from the same generator `vike-cli` and the core use: an 8-hex session drawn once per launch plus a sequence that only grows, behind the same origin prefix (`ui3fa91c070`, `dom3fa91c071`, `poly…`, `opt…`). The id is letters and digits only and 12 characters plus the digits of the sequence (21 characters after a billion orders), which fits the tightest venue budget (Binance behind the longest broker code) and, unlike the old `ui-3-0`, contains no `-` for OKX or for Binance's broker-prefix split to trip on. The window counter still advances once per order, so the symbol a new window opens with does not change. A `VIKE_SHOT` screenshot run and the offscreen/kittest harnesses keep the old deterministic `ui-3-0` spelling, so no golden moves. Proved offline only (`order_dispatch_tests/caps.rs`: a new session does not repeat the last one, a counter that goes back does not repeat an id, the id fits the tightest budget, the old spelling without a mint; `app_local_core_gate.rs` pins that the shell hands the planner its mint); the running desktop was not driven against a node.
### Fixed

- **A bracket (entry plus stop-loss plus take-profit) whose exit the venue's adapter cannot place is now refused WHOLE, in words, before the entry is sent, instead of the entry filling and the exit being refused afterwards (`vike-venues`'s capability table gains `reduce_only_kinds`, read by the capability preflight; `vike-core`'s `lower_bracket` only gains the words; no venue adapter changes behaviour).** The exits are held until the entry fills and were never checked again, so a venue whose row said `stop` but whose adapter refuses a reduce-only stop or limit by name left the position naked (or without its take-profit) with only a warning. Measured from each adapter: IG places a reduce-only MARKET only (its close endpoint cannot rest a stop or a limit), so a bracket on IG is refused; Dukascopy refuses a reduce-only LIMIT, which is a bracket's take-profit, so a bracket on Dukascopy is refused too (it used to fill its entry with the venue's stop-loss and lose the take-profit). The refusal reads `REDUCE_ONLY_UNSUPPORTED: kind=<limit|stop> venue=<venue>` on the refused leg and `BRACKET_ATOMIC_REFUSED: culprit=<coid> leg=<stop_loss|take_profit> venue=<venue>` on the others, with one line in the recent events ("bracket for <venue> REFUSED WHOLE, nothing was sent"). A plain reduce-only limit or stop on those two venues is refused at the same edge, in the same words, instead of by the adapter. Every other venue is unchanged and a bracket on it works as before (the table lists, per venue, the reduce-only kinds its adapter accepts today; what only the account or the moment decides, like FXCM's netting account, cTrader's "no open position to bind" or Deribit's option, stays the adapter's refusal). `venues.json` gains `caps.reduce_only_kinds`.
### Fixed

- **Dukascopy: a reduce-only close (a flatten, a margin call, a market exit, a liquidation) that the JForex sidecar had taken up when it died now ENDS on the node (`OrderCanceled`, in words), instead of staying `ACCEPTED` for ever and counting as a close in flight (Dukascopy bridge only: `crates/bridges/dukascopy/src/exec.rs`'s reader drain and `submit`; no jar change, nothing in a shared crate).** Found by code reading at v0.1.95, as the sibling of the stop-loss fix above: the sidecar answers a close with `OrderAccepted` (its synthetic net-accept) BEFORE it asks the venue to close, so a death between that and the venue's confirmation of the close made the bridge's EOF drain send `OrderRejected "bridge died"`, which the core folds only from `Initialized`/`Submitted` and DROPS on an `Accepted` order. The dead close stayed `ACCEPTED` on the node (the symptom of the 2026-10-26 incident: a flatten `ACCEPTED`, filled 0), and `vike-core`'s `closes_in_flight` counted it as cover, so the margin call and a mount budget's flatten sent nothing for a position that might still be open. Now the client remembers which of its stops and reduce-only market orders the sidecar acknowledged (`Shared::underway`) and the drain ends exactly those with `OrderCanceled` whose reason says the venue may have executed the close, that the node was not told, and to look at the position in the JForex platform. It changes what the NODE believes and sends nothing to the venue; a close the sidecar had not yet answered, a plain market entry and a resting limit keep the rejection they always had. Proven through the real order FSM against the fake sidecar (`crates/bridges/dukascopy/tests/dukascopy_restart.rs`: the accepted-close test is RED on the base, `got OrderRejected "bridge died"`; the unanswered-close test pins the other edge). ⚠ NOT a cure of the phantom itself: a position the node holds and the venue does not (a close the sidecar never heard, such as a stop-loss that fired after a sidecar restart) still stays in `position ls`, the totals and the risk sums until the account's engine is started afresh by hand, and a flatten of it is refused by the venue in words. Nothing in this crate can close the book without writing the node's position (decision 0043), and the sidecar's `position` line is pushed only after a reported fill, so a positions-only reconcile leg would not see it either; the cures that remove the cause need an owner decision (`docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`, the dukascopy row "the class behind the row above").
### Added

- **The tradehub summary line of a node with several currency groups now shows what the drawdown latch measures each group against, so the adopted-wallet base can be read live with no trade, no restart and no setting (the `vike-tradehub` summary line only: `crates/vike-tradehub/src/summary.rs`'s `summary_line`; nothing in `vike-core`, so nothing the latency gate measures).** Each `other_ledgers` object gains `base`, `peak` and `curve` once the latch's 30 s sweep has measured the group (absent before, never zero; `curve` and `peak` are the latch's own, `base` is the curve less the group's own PnL, exact while the group is flat), and the primary group rides as `capital_base` and `drawdown_curve` beside `ledger_ccy` (its high-water mark is not published, so no `peak`). A EUR group of a 49,986 EUR wallet reads about 49,986, a stale one-seed base would read 1,000. All keys are additive: a node of one currency prints the line it always did, and a reader of the older keys sees them unchanged.

## [0.1.95] - 2026-10-27

### Fixed

- **The drawdown latch judges a non-dollar currency group (FXCM's EUR demo, account 9) against the wallet its engine adopted, not against the configured seed_cash (`vike-core`'s risk sweep only: `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/watchdog/risk.rs`; the dollar group, every dollar engine and every `Delta` engine keep their configured seeds and fold exactly as before).** Since v0.1.93 told account 9 its currency, its engine is a group of its own, and that group's base was ONE seed_cash (default 1000) instead of the roughly 50,000 EUR demo wallet it holds: a 100,000-unit EURUSD long and a 29-pip adverse move (about 250 EUR, 0.5% of the wallet) read as 25% and would have put the WHOLE node, live accounts included, in liquidate-only (read from the code by the money review of 2026-10-26; never reached on the CI box). `CoreThread::adopt_wallet_bases` now writes the wallet into the engine's seed slot at the first sweep that finds it `Authoritative`, once, and moves the group's high-water mark by the difference; a later deposit or withdrawal moves nothing, a stopped engine and a non-positive wallet are not adopted, and the published `capital_base` reads the same slot. A 250 EUR loss on a 50,000 EUR wallet no longer latches; 12,000 EUR (24%) does against a 20% rule. Proved offline only (`drawdown_latch_ccy.rs`); the the latency box latency A/B of the `vike-core` commit is owed (a cold sweep and one `CoreThread` field, no per-event path). Decision 0183, "Amended 2026-10-27".
- **A `Submit` whose client order id an order of the node already carries is refused in words at the control door, instead of being Acked and lost (the `vike-tradehub` door only: `crates/vike-tradehub/src/server/refusal.rs`'s `coid_reuse_refusal`, `accept_command`'s step 1c' and both previews; no core, bridge or journal change).** `vike-cli trade order submit … --coid <the id of a FILLED order>` printed `accepted by the node`: the core registered the new order over the old one, the gatewayhub's per-account dedup took the repeat for a retry and never sent it, and the stuck-order watchdog rejected the half-created order about 30 s later with a reason that named nothing (measured 2026-10-26 on FXCM account 9, coid `b93fxent`, and on Dukascopy, coid `b93dsent`). The door now answers `coid b93fxent is already used by an order that is FILLED: pick a new client order id` for a FILLED, CANCELED, REJECTED or EXPIRED order, and `… is ACCEPTED (still live): pick a new client order id, or change that order by this id with modify or cancel` for one that rests, and sends nothing. A coid no order carries, a retry of a command the node never received (`NeverSent`), and an id a RiskGate veto turned away (it never entered the registry) go exactly as before. `PublisherHandle::open_orders_named_by` is now `orders_named_by` (a `Submit` is answered with the order of its id in any status; a `Modify` still gets only the OPEN one). ⚠ Residuals: the check reads the published snapshot, so two commands for one id inside one publish interval both pass (the core keeps no copy: `run_submit_hop` re-sends one coid by design), and a restart forgets the terminal ids of the previous process. ⚠ A client that mints ids from a counter that restarts, such as the desktop's `"{prefix}-{win}-{shot}"`, now reads this refusal where it used to lose the order in silence.
- **cTrader: a position the node itself holds no longer raises an `OrphanLocalPosition` plus a `PositionOnlyExternal` on every reconcile pass (the cTrader bridge only: `crates/bridges/ctrader/src/recon_client.rs`'s `net_positions`; no shared crate changes).** Measured live on 2026-10-26 on the hedged demo account (v0.1.93, tests T3 and T29): while a position was open across a pass, `trade doctor` held two extra rows on ctrader EURUSD (the book's `position:EURUSD:BOTH` "has NO venue position row" and the venue's `Long`, 1000), which cleared once the position closed; the same ids had appeared on four earlier boots. The engine's book is one signed net per `(symbol, BOTH)` and the diff matches by `(symbol, side)` exactly, while the cTrader report named each position `Long` or `Short`, so the two never met. The report is now ONE `Both` row per symbol (signed quantity, size-weighted price), IG's convention. A symbol that holds BOTH directions (a locked or partly hedged pair, which one number would hide) is still reported as a `Long` and a `Short` row and still held, a position the book does not hold, a size it disagrees with and a position the venue closed are still held, and the rows still sum to the venue's net. Offline proof against the in-process fake venue and the real diff, red before the change; not yet re-measured live.
- **Dukascopy: a native stop-loss that was resting when its JForex sidecar died now ENDS on the node (`OrderCanceled`, in words), instead of staying `ACCEPTED` for ever (Dukascopy bridge only: `crates/bridges/dukascopy/src/exec.rs`'s reader drain and `submit`; no jar change, nothing in a shared crate).** Found by code reading at the v0.1.93 tag (same code in v0.1.94): when the sidecar dies (the new supervisor's restart, a gatewayhub restart at any deploy, a JForex session loss) the bridge's EOF drain sent `OrderRejected "bridge died"` for every order in flight, and the core folds a rejection only from `Initialized`/`Submitted`, so on an `Accepted` stop it was DROPPED (`terminal event dropped on a live order`): the node kept the stop `ACCEPTED`, every cancel of it was refused as stranded, and when the venue's stop-loss later fired (the venue keeps it, measured 2026-10-26) the new sidecar's empty stop book heard nothing, so the position stayed open on the node under a stop it believed in. Now the client remembers which of its `stop` orders the sidecar accepted (`Shared::stops`) and the drain ends exactly those with `OrderCanceled` whose reason says the venue may STILL hold the stop-loss and to check the JForex platform; a stop the sidecar had not yet answered is still rejected (the core takes a cancel only from `Accepted` on). It changes what the NODE believes and nothing at the venue: no cancel is sent to anything, the stop-loss stays (a restart never cancels a resting order), and the way back is still a stop at the same price. Proven through the real order FSM against a fake sidecar whose venue keeps its stop-losses across launches and logs every cancel it receives (`crates/bridges/dukascopy/tests/dukascopy_restart.rs`: the resting-stop test is RED on the base, `got OrderRejected "bridge died"`; the unanswered-stop test pins the other edge). NOT changed: a resting LIMIT order at a death stays `Accepted` (its venue state is unknown, as before), and Dukascopy still has no reconcile leg, so a stop-loss that fires while the sidecar is down or after the restart is still not reported (`docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`'s dukascopy stop-loss row).

- **Dukascopy: a reduce-only MARKET close (flatten, margin call, market-exit, drawdown liquidation) no longer OPENS an opposite position when the venue holds less than the node thinks (the JForex sidecar jar only: `NettingPlan.java` and one line of `StrategyBridge.java`'s `handleSubmit`; nothing in the Rust crates or any shared one; it reaches a box only with the release that installs the new jar, and an older jar behaves as before).** The sidecar nets a market order against what the VENUE holds and opens a fresh order with the rest, and it never read `reduce_only`: after a stop-loss fired unheard (the restart gap in `crates/bridges/dukascopy/CLAUDE.md`) or a close made in the JForex platform, the node's flatten, sized to the node's position, closed what the venue still held and OPENED an opposite position with the remainder (or the whole quantity on a flat venue), unprotected. Found by code reading (R-STOPS, v0.1.93). Now a reduce-only market with nothing open to close is an `OrderRejected` (`reduce-only: no open long order to reduce (nothing is open, or what is open is already being closed): a reduce-only order never opens a position; this order was NOT sent`), and one larger than what is open closes what is open and drops the rest, so the order ends filled short of its quantity and never opens (the FXCM bridge's rule for the same order). The sidecar is the only place that can apply it: it reads the venue's own open orders, where the Rust side has only the last `position` line, which is stale exactly when it matters. The capability row (`supports_reduce_only` stays `false`) and the Rust client are untouched. Proven by `NettingPlanTest.java` (the pure decision, six cases) and, through `handleSubmit` over the Proxy stand-ins, two tests of `NetCloseAfterRestartTest.java` that FAIL on the sources before (an order was submitted to the venue). NOT measured on a demo account: JForex's own answer to a partial net-close of an order (the crate page lists it as not measured), and nothing here was run against a JForex login.

## [0.1.94] - 2026-10-26

### Fixed

- **FXCM: a pair whose quote currency has no pair of the account's currency is admitted, its rate composed through USD (the FXCM bridge only: the rate function of `crates/bridges/fxcm/src/home_conversion.rs` and its `hops`, and which rows `crates/bridges/fxcm/src/subscription.rs`'s `wanted` subscribes; nothing in the node's door, the engine or any shared crate).** Measured on v0.1.93 through the node on the EUR demo (account 9): `USDHKD`, `USDZAR`, `USDMXN` and `USDCNH` were refused at the door ("`cannot admit USDHKD: fxcm lists no HKD/EUR or EUR/HKD pair`") because FXCM lists no euro pair of those currencies, while pairs with a direct EUR cross (`USDSEK`, `USDNOK`, `EURHUF`, the EUR crosses) worked. The rate of one `Q` in the account's currency is now, when FXCM lists no `Q/A` and no `A/Q`, the rate of `Q` in USD times the rate of USD in the account's currency, each the mid of its listed USD pair (inverted where it is written the other way round): HKD on the EUR demo is `1 / 7.84451 x 1 / 1.118035` = 0.1140194 euro per Hong Kong dollar. Both legs must be subscription `T` (the bridge subscribes them itself), open, two-sided and under 120 s old, and the rate is stamped with the OLDEST leg's moment, so the engine's staleness rule is unchanged; a missing, view-only, closed or stale leg refuses the pair naming the leg. A listed direct pair is used exactly as before (same rate to the last bit, same stamp), a listed pair FXCM will not subscribe is never bypassed, a USD account is unchanged, and any other ledger currency (a pound or a yen account) composes the same way. The `demo` tier rule and the exposure ceiling are untouched. Proved OFFLINE on the measured Offers table of the EUR demo (`crates/bridges/fxcm/tests/fixtures/eur_demo_offers.json`); no order has been placed through it (the v0.1.93 amendment of the account-currency decision, item 8).
- **FXCM live smokes: the reconcile and currency smokes (and the exec smoke) find the demo login while the daemon's account is DEACTIVATED, like the stop, close and subscribe smokes (test code and docs only; no product code changes).** A smoke opens a second session of the demo login, which kicks the node's, so the lane run deactivates the node's FXCM account first; `fxcm_reconcile_smoke` and `fxcm_account_currency_and_conversion_rates` read only the ACTIVE row and printed `skip: no demo fxcm account credentials` in exactly that run, which left the v0.1.93 independent reads of the EUR wallet and of EUR/USD's orientation inconclusive. The lookup the other three had each spelled out now lives once in `crates/bridges/fxcm/tests/common/mod.rs`'s `demo_config` (the active default row, else THE one unlabelled demo row; several inactive ones stay a skip) and all six smokes call it; `crates/bridges/fxcm/tests/fxcm_smoke_login.rs` tests it and fails when a test file reads the credential store itself.

## [0.1.93] - 2026-10-26

### Added

- **Dukascopy: `--type stop --trigger <px> --reduce-only` is now the VENUE's own stop-loss on the open position (the JForex sidecar jar and the `dukascopy` capability row only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/dukascopy` and `crates/vike-venues` changes).** Until now `--type stop` was refused at the core edge (`TRIGGER_UNSUPPORTED: kind=stop venue=dukascopy`) because the sidecar mapped only market and limit. JForex has no reduce-only stop order (`BUYSTOP`/`SELLSTOP` are entry orders and would open a position, so they are not wired), but it has the stop-loss PRICE of an order (`IOrder.setStopLossPrice`), which Dukascopy holds and executes itself: a stop placed this way survives a tradehub outage, a sidecar crash and a gatewayhub restart. `StrategyBridge.java`'s `handleStop` sets it on the opposing open orders, oldest fill first, whole orders only (a stop-loss has no amount of its own, so a quantity that lands inside an order is refused with the sizes it can be, and more than is open is refused, not capped), all-or-nothing, and never over another stop-loss. The stop is `OrderAccepted` once every order holds it; a fired stop-loss (`ORDER_CLOSE_OK`, reason `ORDER_CLOSED_BY_SL`) is a closing fill of the STOP's coid with trade id `<order id>:c:<stop coid>`, one per order and the last terminal; `cancel` takes the stop-loss off, `modify` moves it (the new trigger is the amend's `new_price`). A `stop` that is not `--reduce-only` is refused by name (an entry stop is not wired). The row declares `stop` and `[StopLoss]`; `supports_reduce_only` stays `false` (a reduce-only market still nets and opens its remainder). A reduce-only LIMIT is now refused by name by the exec client (nothing sent): the sidecar nets only market orders, so such a limit would open an opposite position when hit, and declaring `stop` made it reachable through a bracket (before, the whole bracket was refused at the core edge for its stop): a bracket on this venue is now an entry with a native stop-loss and no take-profit (the take-profit leg dies unfilled with the reason, the core keeps the stop-loss). The sidecar puts the trigger on the instrument's grid (a tenth of a pip) because the core snaps an order's price and not its trigger. ⚠ The jar is a release asset: a jar from before this answers a stop with its own "unsupported order_type: stop", so the deploy must install this release's jar and restart the gatewayhub. ⚠ After a sidecar restart the venue keeps the stop-loss but the new sidecar has forgotten the stop: a fired stop-loss closes the position at the venue and the node is not told (no reconcile client on this venue), and the way back is to send the stop again at the SAME price, which takes the venue's stop-loss over. Measured on the demo account (USDJPY 1000, 2026-10-26, a jar built from this change; the numbers are in `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`'s Dukascopy stop-loss row): the stop-loss was accepted in 46 ms, FIRED at 157.351 for a trigger of 157.352 and arrived as the closing fill of the stop's coid; a second one outlived the sidecar (the position was closed by the venue while no client was attached); `modify` and `cancel` changed the venue's stop-loss; after a sidecar restart a stop at the same price took the venue's stop-loss over; every run ended flat.

- **FXCM: a STOP-LOSS and a TAKE-PROFIT that rest at the venue, on the hedging account (FXCM bridge, its shim and one row of the per-venue capability table; nothing in `vike-bridge-core`, `vike-exec`, `vike-core` or any other venue; it needs the new `libfcshim.so`: until a box has it, a reduce-only stop or priced limit there is refused by name).** `vike-cli trade order submit fxcm EURUSD sell 1000 --type stop --trigger 1.1175 --reduce-only` is the trade's own venue stop (`S`), a reduce-only priced limit its take-profit (`L`); a bracket's two exits bind the SAME trade. The venue holds them, so they survive a node outage and a restart, and it removes them when their trade closes any other way (no stale exit can open a trade later). Before this the core refused every FXCM stop and the plain resting form of an exit was an entry order that OPENS a second trade when hit (measured). Measured on the demo account (2026-10-26) by an SDK probe: both accepted in 0.2 s, an amend moves the stop in place, a cancel of one leaves the other, a stop and a take-profit each REALLY FIRED (the closing fill carries the exit's own order id, the sibling is deleted by the venue, the trade closes with no opposite trade), a partial close of the trade keeps both exits on the remainder under a new trade id; the venue refuses an exit for a part of a trade (`ORA-20134`), a second exit of one kind (`ORA-20114`) and a price on the wrong side (`ORA-20115`), so the bridge binds to the oldest free trade of exactly the order's size and refuses by name otherwise. A stop that is not reduce-only, a stop-limit, a mark or index trigger and a stop on a netting account are refused by name. The FXCM caps row gains `stop` and the `StopLoss` trigger type (and nothing else: `supports_reduce_only` stays `false`, because a NETTING account has no backstop for a reduce-only order, so the reconcile pass's `POSITION WITHOUT STOP` still says once that this venue "cannot rest a protective stop", which is no longer true on a hedging account). Two optional shim exports (`fc_open_exits`, `fc_place_exit`, no ABI bump). Proven through the bridge on the demo (the live smoke `crates/bridges/fxcm/tests/fxcm_stop_smoke.rs`, 2026-10-26: stop and take-profit accepted and read back, a second stop refused by name, an amend, a cancel, the exits removed with a closed trade, a stop that FIRED as a fill under its own client order id with the take-profit cancelled by the venue, a short's buy stop, flat at the end); not yet through a node's own submit path. `docs/ops/fxcm-forexconnect.md`'s "Trade-bound stop-loss and take-profit" has the table, the refusals and what is not built.

- **FXCM: a closing fill now books the commission still owed at the close, not 0 (FXCM bridge and its shim only; an installed shim that still sends 0.0 on a close books 0 for it, as before this change).** The owner ordered every venue's commissions counted correctly; the audit of 2026-10-26 found FXCM's sign unproven and the close side never booked. The SDK reference says the figure is "the amount of funds subtracted from the account balance", "expressed in the account currency" (so positive is a charge; the sign was never measured, so every figure now books as its MAGNITUDE, a cost, on the exec lane and the reconcile report alike: a charge written as a negative number would otherwise have credited the account every fee), and that a schedule pays at the open, at the close, or half at each. The demo account (EUR, spread-only) read 0.00 on every Trades and ClosedTrades row of 20 fills and its balance moved by `GrossPL` alone, so nothing here is measured on an account that charges. Through v0.1.91 only the open row's figure was booked: an account paying at the close was booked nothing and an "any deal" one half. The shim now sends the closed row's own figure, and `crates/bridges/fxcm/src/commission.rs` books it less the open fill's share (open commission times closed over open amount), never below zero, so a total figure gives exactly the close side at every stage and a close-side-only figure can understate but never charge a fee twice; a close whose opening fill this process never saw (a restart between the two, the remainder of a part-closed trade) books 0 and says so at `warn!` with the figure. The committed shim envelope no longer says `-0.08` for a charge. The one measurement that settles the rest is in `docs/ops/fxcm-forexconnect.md`'s "Commission: the sign, the currency and the close side".

- **FXCM: an order on a pair the ACCOUNT may not trade is refused by name, with nothing sent, instead of FXCM's bare `ORA-20102: Access Violation` (FXCM bridge and its shim only; nothing in `vike-bridge-core`, `vike-exec` or `vike-core`).** On the demo login USD/HKD reads subscription `T` and quotes normally, but the account's order permissions (`canCreateEntryOrder`, `canCreateMarketOpenOrder`) read Disabled for it, the one of the 48 regular forex rows; every order on it ended `FXCM native error -6: ... ORA-20102: Access Violation ...` after up to 5 s, and the live subscribe smoke of 2026-10-26 13:51 UTC picked it as a pair to trade and panicked. The shim now reads the login's permission checker (a local read, no round trip) before a placement builds or sends anything (`the account may not create entry orders on USD/HKD: FXCM's permission for it reads Disabled ... Nothing was sent`) and before it writes a subscription for a pair no order kind can use (a `V`/`D` pair is then left as it is and the door's refusal names the permission). Only a Disabled permission refuses; a Hidden or unreadable one is the venue's to judge. Measured on the demo: every other exotic tried (USD/SEK, USD/NOK, USD/ZAR, USD/MXN, USD/TRY, EUR/HUF, USD/CNH, EUR/TRY) placed and cancelled a far limit, an unpriced one and a priced one. It needs the shim of the release (the deploy installs it); an older shim keeps the raw FXCM text.

- **IBKR: a cancel held for a missing commission now asks the venue for it before the fee is booked unknown (IBKR bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr` changes).** When an order was canceled with a fill still waiting for its `commissionReport`, the bridge held the cancel for 5 s and then booked the fill with a fee of 0.0 and no fee currency (about 1 USD short per such order; the real report, if it came later, was only logged). The one mechanism that re-delivers a lost report, `reqExecutions` (the stranded-fill ladder), first asks at 15 s, so the 5 s release always preempted it. The bound that runs out now sends that ask once (`EventMapper::ask_for_held_commissions`) and the release waits 5 s more for the answer: a report the venue sends back joins the fill with its REAL fee and the cancel follows it, as on the normal path. The ask is skipped while the connection learns the venue and with the stream dead (those release at the old bound). Not measured against a gateway: no run has made IB lose a report, so this is proven over the scripted transport only, and a report IB never sends still ends as an unknown fee. The cure for that last case is a fee-adjustment event in the shared model, which does not exist and is the owner's decision (`crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/CLAUDE.md`).

- **IBKR: a new stock is priced off DELAYED data instead of refused, and the order records it (decision 0140; owner rule 2026-10-26: «I want users to be able to use ALL tickers of every venue, no hand steps»).** The any-symbol price tap refused every stream IBKR labelled delayed or frozen (`no price feed for ...: ... is delayed ...`), so on an account with no real-time stock entitlement (the owner's) EVERY new stock was refused and the one cure offered was a market-data subscription that costs money and has no API, although decision 0140 rules that an order MAY be priced off delayed data. `PriceTap::real_time_only` is now `PriceTap::labelled_quotes` (`crates/vike-tradehub/src/feeds/price_tap.rs`, the ibkr feed's only): a two-sided quote of a stream that has stated ANY label prices, a stream with no label is still "none yet", a price noted under one label is still forgotten when the label changes, and real-time is what an order records when the venue serves it. The label already travelled to the core, so the order's record (the order view's DELAYED badge) and its `PRE-TRADE <coid> <symbol>: priced off delayed data` note carry it, and the tap now says once per change in the journal `delayed data (about 15 minutes old)`. ⚠ The order is judged at that price: a MARKET order's notional, the account exposure and the buying-power check read a mark about 15 minutes old; the price collar is wired in no production path (decide its band before it is); the tap's 60 s age bound counts from a quote's arrival and the delayed feed ticks in bursts 1 to 25 s apart (measured), so a quiet stock can answer `has no price on this node yet` and an engine holding it can be skipped by the margin call. Measured on the paper gateway 2026-10-26 (pre-market; a smoke on client ids of its own, the node untouched): the lookup of MSFT, a stream labelled `delayed` with the label before the first quote, one share bought at 527.48 and sold back at 526.50, the account flat afterwards. Not run: the node's own door end to end on the paper account, a frozen label on a real stream, a stock in another currency. `docs/ops/ibkr-socket-gateway.md`, "Delayed data prices a new stock".

- **Deribit places NATIVE stop, stop-limit and take-profit orders, so `--type stop` is no longer refused on Deribit and the stop survives the node (Deribit bridge and its one capability row; `venue_trigger_by` gains its deribit row; no other venue changes) (owner ruling 2026-10-26: an operator must be able to place a stop-loss on every venue, and a venue that has a native stop uses it).** The bridge sent every order that was not a limit as a MARKET order, so a stop would have filled at once; the row therefore declared no trigger kinds and the core refused the stop. `DeribitRest` now sends `stop` as `stop_market`, `stop_limit` as `stop_limit` and `take_profit` as `take_market` (`take_limit` when it names a price), with `trigger_price` on the instrument's tick grid (floored like a limit price), `trigger` from the order's `trigger_by` (`last_price` when it names none, the workspace's default series; `mark_price` and `index_price` on request) and `reduce_only` as for any order; a trigger order with no positive trigger price, a stop-limit with no limit price, or one on an option (the venue has trigger orders for futures and perpetuals only) is refused by name before the wire. The row `crates/vike-venues/src/venue_caps.rs`'s `DERIBIT` declares `stop`, `stop_limit` and `take_profit` with both trigger types; its pin (`expanded_axes_matrix_is_pinned`), the bridge's `caps_test` and the three `vike-core` preflight tests that used Deribit as the refused venue (now Polymarket) moved with it. A consequence worth knowing: the `POSITION WITHOUT STOP` line now applies to a Deribit position (the row can rest a stop). **MEASURED on the Deribit TESTNET, `BTC-PERPETUAL`, 2026-10-26, through the production client** (`crates/bridges/deribit/tests/deribit_native_stop_testnet_smoke.rs`, by hand): a stop is held `untriggered` and listed by the label lookup and by the open-order read the restart reconcile uses; a far reduce-only stop, a stop-limit, a take-profit on the mark series and a stop on the index series were accepted, read back and cancelled (each `OrderCanceled` evented); a stop one tick under the last price TRIGGERED and closed the position within 0.3 s, and the node saw `OrderSubmitted`, `OrderAccepted`, `Fill`, `OrderFilled` (when a stop triggers, its venue id ceases to exist and a NEW market order carrying the stop's label executes, so the fill joins by coid); a stop on the wrong side of the market came back as `OrderRejected` carrying the venue's `trigger_price_too_high`; the run ended flat with nothing resting, and the node's `recon ls` showed no Deribit row. **Not done, and listed in `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`:** the node is not told when the venue ends a stop WITHOUT a fill (a stop cancelled elsewhere, or a reduce-only stop that triggers with no position: measured, it leaves no trace and the engine keeps it `Accepted`); the reconcile client does not yet CLAIM to list trigger orders (three edits and a drill, listed on that page), so after a restart an operator's `demo` stop is not adopted; a modify does not move a stop's trigger. A cancel whose venue id the venue calls gone now follows the order's label once (a stop-limit or take-limit that FIRED goes on as a NEW resting limit order under the same label, which the stale id's "not found" used to report cancelled while it still rested).

- **Polymarket: the bridge names what blocks an order, understands a market name, and can onboard the wallet itself (Polymarket bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/polymarket` changes except docs; CODE AND OFFLINE TESTS ONLY, nothing of it has run against a funded wallet).** The owner's rule of 2026-10-26 is that no ticker may need a hand step, and polymarket's hand steps were the 77-digit token id, the wallet's balance and approvals, and the API key. (1) Before each order is signed the exec thread READS the wallet (`GET /balance-allowance`: collateral for a BUY, the token for a SELL) and refuses in words, before anything is signed or sent, a positive shortfall of balance or of the allowance of that order's own exchange: the asset, both amounts, the wallet and the contract (`polymarket: this BUY was NOT sent. It needs 5 pUSD ... holds 0`), instead of the venue's bare `not enough balance / allowance` after a signed order had spent a submit token. It refuses only on a positive, parsed shortfall; a failed read or an unknown body lets the order through to the venue. (2) On an ALLOWANCE shortfall a deposit wallet whose account holds the relayer key has the four trading approvals (pUSD `approve(max)` and CTF `setApprovalForAll`, for both exchanges, nothing wider) sent once as one relayer batch, and the order is still refused, saying so; every other wallet type is told in words to press "Enable trading" in the Polymarket app. (3) The exec start CREATES the wallet's API key (`POST /auth/api-key`) when the derive says it has none, and only then: a 401, a 403, a 429, a 5xx or a transport failure creates nothing, and a derive failure now carries the venue's own sentence. The reconcile-only start stays read-only. (4) A market slug, `slug:Outcome` or a polymarket.com market address resolves to the outcome's token id through Gamma (`vike_polymarket::market_ref::canonical_polymarket_symbol`; a pasted token id works unchanged and costs no read); a bare slug, a multi-market event, a closed market, a market that takes no orders and an unlisted slug are refused with the spellings or the cause that applies (the live read of 2026-10-26 found that Gamma's `/markets` hides a resolved market unless asked with `closed=true`, so a miss is asked a second time and a resolved market is refused as closed, not as unlisted), and a slug typed as an order symbol is refused with the ids to use instead of `cannot resolve the NegRisk signing domain for token <slug>`. ⚠ The control door still passes any string for this venue (`SYMBOL_RULES` keeps `PerOrder`), so a slug cannot yet be typed into the Trade window: the translation belongs there, in a shared module, and an order submitted under a slug would book its fills under the token id (two names for one position). Unverified until a funded live run: the `/balance-allowance` body, the venue's no-key sentence, and the relayer batch (`crates/bridges/polymarket/CLAUDE.md` lists them). Tests: a loopback double of the CLOB and the relayer (`FakeServer`) for every branch above, fixtures from a live Gamma row, and a keyless read-only live smoke of the slug route.

- **Binance perpetuals: the bridge now SETS the two account modes it orders under instead of only reporting them, so a hedge-mode account or an isolated-margin symbol no longer stands between a user and a valid ticker (owner rule 2026-10-26: «the user must be able to trade ANY ticker with no hand step»; Binance bridge only, nothing shared changes).** Every order this adapter sends is one-way (`positionSide BOTH`) on cross margin, and the engine's margin math models cross. Until now a hedge-mode account had EVERY order refused by the venue (`-4061`, "Order's position side does not match user's setting.") and an isolated symbol traded on a margin the engine does not model, the bridge writing a leverage and nothing else; the modes were only READ, and only when an account stated a leverage. Now `crates/bridges/binance/src/modes.rs` reads the account's position mode at EVERY perpetual start (stated leverage or not), and the mounted symbol's margin type, and writes one-way / cross ONLY on a mismatch; any other perpetual gets the same margin probe before its FIRST order. A healthy account costs two reads and no write. The venue itself judges flatness, atomically, at write time (Binance refuses the position-mode switch while the account holds any position or resting order on any symbol, and the margin switch while that symbol does), so a mode is never switched under an open position or order: the refusal is worded (what is wrong, what blocks the fix, what to do) and nothing else is written after it; "no need to change" (`-4059`, `-4046`) is success. A hedge account that could not be switched has its orders rejected with those words (single, batch and stop paths) instead of the bare `-4061`; an isolated symbol that could not be switched is a WARN and trades as before. ⚠ **The switch happens on the DEMO host only (owner ruling 2026-10-26: no exchange write on a live account):** a mainnet client is never read and never written for a mode (`writes_modes` is true for the demo futures host alone, whatever tier the account row states), so a live account starts exactly as it did before and a hedge-mode live account's order is refused in words that name the mismatch and the hand fix (choose One-way Mode in the Binance Futures preferences); the start's leverage write is older than this change and still runs on every tier; no setting was added. ⚠ An account that states a leverage while in hedge mode or isolated margin is still refused the FIGURE at its first start: the lane's read-only probe runs before the bridge's start and still sees the old mode, so the figure applies after `account.active` off and on. Multi-Assets mode is neither read nor written. New offline tests over a scripted venue pin every branch and the start's call order; `crates/bridges/binance/tests/binance_modes_smoke.rs` is the hand-run demo drill. Drilled on the Binance demo account (2026-10-26): an isolated mounted symbol and an isolated second symbol were each switched to cross by the bridge (at the start, and by the first order on that symbol) and the order was accepted; the venue refused a position-mode switch (`-4067`, a lane twin's stop alone is enough) and a margin switch (`-4047` with an order resting, `-4048` with a position), and nothing was written after a refusal. ⚠ The hedge -> one-way write itself has NOT run against the venue: the only demo account is never flat while the lane twin trades it.

- **Bybit: a symbol the account holds in HEDGE position mode is put in one-way before its first order, an `ISOLATED_MARGIN` account in cross, and what cannot be put right is refused in words (Bybit bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/bybit` changes; owner rule 2026-10-26: any ticker tradable with no hand step, the bridge fixes the account's own mode through the API when the API allows it and says why when it does not).** Every Bybit order names `positionIdx 0`; on a symbol the account held in hedge mode the venue answered `10001 "position idx not match position mode"` and the mode had to be changed by hand in the web UI (the bridge only REPORTED a mode, and only for an account that states a leverage). Now the exec thread, before the first order of a symbol (once at the start for the mounted one, at the first order for an admitted one), reads the symbol's position rows and `account/info`: a hedge symbol that is flat with nothing resting gets `POST /v5/position/switch-mode` (one-way); an `ISOLATED_MARGIN` unified account gets `POST /v5/account/set-margin-mode` (`REGULAR_MARGIN`) only while the whole linear book (USDT and USDC) is flat and empty. A hedge symbol that cannot be switched (a position, a resting order, or the venue's own refusal) is a terminal `OrderRejected` naming the symbol, the mode and what blocks the fix, and nothing is written; the refusal is remembered for 30 s and the next order asks again. Portfolio margin, a classic account's isolated symbol and isolated margin under a position are only logged at WARN (the venue trades in them; leaving portfolio margin and the one-way upgrade to a unified account are not done without the owner's word). A read that fails changes nothing and refuses nothing. ⚠ **This happens on the DEMO host only (owner ruling 2026-10-26: no exchange write on a live account):** a live (mainnet) account is never read and never written for a mode (`Modes::writes_modes` is true for the demo host not flagged mainnet and nothing else), so it starts and orders exactly as before, and a hedge symbol's order the venue refuses for its position index is worded as the mismatch with the hand fix (switch the symbol to One-Way position mode in Bybit's settings); the start's `set-leverage` is older than this change and still runs on both tiers. Measured on the Bybit demo account on 2026-10-26: a hedge symbol was put in one-way by a client's start and by the first order of a client mounted elsewhere and the orders were accepted and cancelled; a symbol with a resting order was refused in words and left in hedge mode, and the next client after the order was gone put it right; an `ISOLATED_MARGIN` account was put back to `REGULAR_MARGIN` by a client's start; every mode was put back as found. Not proven: a classic account, portfolio margin, a mainnet account. The posted-leverage lane still reads a hedge account as a refusal before it writes a stated leverage (a shared-home change would be needed to heal there too).

- **OKX: an account in long/short position mode is switched to net mode at the engine's start when it is flat, and a restart reads the orders and positions of every admitted instrument (OKX bridge only; one row in `RECON_READS_ADMITTED`; nothing else shared changes).** (1) The bridge orders net positions and a long/short account refused every order (`Parameter posSide error`, measured on the demo account 2026-10-26); the bridge only reported the mode, and only for an account that stated a leverage. Now every OKX engine start ON THE SIMULATED (DEMO) NETWORK reads `account/config` and, for a long/short account with no open position, no resting order and no resting stop, sends ONE `set-position-mode` `net_mode` and reads it back (`crates/bridges/okx/src/account_modes.rs`). An account that is not flat, a refusal of the exchange, a failing read or a switch the read-back does not confirm leaves the account as it was and says why in words in the daemon's log, and an order refused for its `posSide` now carries the explanation. The bridge never closes a position or cancels an order to make room, never changes the account level (a Simple-mode account is named in the log), and reads the mode at the start only. ⚠ **A LIVE account is never read and never written for a mode (owner ruling 2026-10-26: no exchange write on a live account):** the gate is the sending transport itself (`OkxTransport::simulated`, true only for a transport that sends the `x-simulated-trading` header, false by default; okx has one host for both networks), so a live account starts exactly as it did before (its start's `set-leverage` is older and still runs), and an order it has refused for its `posSide` (single, stop and batch paths) carries words that name the mismatch and the hand fix (switch the account to Net mode in OKX's trading settings). Demo drill 2026-10-26: a flat net account put in long/short mode refused the net order, was refused its switch by name while an order rested, was switched and read back as net, accepted the same order, wrote nothing at the next start and ended in the mode it was found in. (2) OKX's reconcile client was built on the mounted instrument only, so after a restart a resting order on an instrument the engine had admitted later was held unregistered (it kept resting, outside HALT and cancel-all). It now reads every instrument it is told, each scaled by its own `ctVal` (orders, stops, fills, and one account-wide positions read), an instrument OKX no longer lists is read as holding nothing, and okx joins `RECON_READS_ADMITTED`. Proved offline and against the demo venue at the client level (a far ETH order under a client mounted on BTC); a whole node restart across such an order is not yet drilled. `docs/ops/trading-any-symbol.md`'s "okx: the account's position mode and the restart read", `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`.

- **A Binance spot BUY's commission is booked in the quote currency (USDT), at the fill price, instead of as that many USDT of a BTC amount.** Binance spot charges the fee in the coin a fill receives: a BUY pays in the base coin (a BTCUSDT BUY paid `0.0000001` BTC), a SELL in USDT. The core books a fill's commission as stated, so every BUY entered `fees_paid` at 1/80,000 of its value and about half of the demo spot account's true fees were missing (measured on the CI box on the release before the last one: 24 BUYs, 0.359 USDT of fees booked as 0.00000445; the audit's inflated count of BUY rows was the same trades written once per delivery by the journal before that release made one execution one record; the measurement is in `crates/bridges/binance/CLAUDE.md`). One rule, `crates/bridges/binance/src/family/spot_fee.rs`'s `spot_fee_in_quote`, now runs on all three legs that can deliver the same fill: the live executionReport, the reconnect replay and the restart reconcile (a `MissingFill` now books the figure the stream would have). A fee in the quote asset (every SELL) is unchanged; the perpetual is untouched. Aster's spot lane runs the same code and converts only a fee its own venue states in the base coin (no aster spot fill has been journaled, so its asset is unmeasured). **Not covered:** a fee paid in BNB (the BNB-discount setting) on a pair that is not BNB's own is still booked as that many quote units, because no BNB/quote price is known to a mapper; it now logs a warning on the 1st, 2nd, 4th ... such fill (`docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`). The position size of a BUY is still the ordered quantity, not net of the base-coin fee. `fees_paid` and the equity panel's fees column move up by the BUY fees from the first fill after the deploy; fills already booked keep their figure.

- **Hyperliquid: the first order on a coin the account holds in ISOLATED margin switches it to cross by itself, and a coin listed after the start no longer waits for a restart (Hyperliquid bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/hyperliquid` and its docs changes).** The owner's rule of 2026-10-26: a user must be able to trade ANY ticker with no hand step. ⚠ **The switch (1) is made on the TESTNET only (a `demo` account): a `live` (mainnet) account is never written to, by owner ruling 2026-10-26 ("what do you need live if you have demo"), and behaves exactly as v0.1.92 (nothing read, nothing written; a mode the venue refuses is the venue's own refusal text).** The reload (2) is a read and runs on every tier; it never publishes a read that moves a known coin's asset id. (1) Before the first opening order on a perp coin of a testnet account the exec thread reads the account's own `activeAssetData` for it: held cross ⇒ nothing is sent, ever; held isolated and flat ⇒ ONE signed `updateLeverage` (`isCross: true`, at the figure the account already holds, clamped into `1..=maxLeverage`: the MODE changes, the number does not; the account's stated `account.leverage` never reaches a bridge); held isolated under an open position ⇒ not sent (the venue refuses that switch), the order goes as before and one warning says so. A refused or timed-out switch refuses that order in words, a failed read lets it go and is asked again, and a reduce-only order, spot, an isolated-only coin and a builder-dex coin never wait on it. (2) An order naming a coin the start's universe lacks re-reads `meta` and `spotMeta` once (at most once a minute; the HIP-3 setting of the start is kept) and publishes the new universe to the exec thread and the user-data pump together; a re-read smaller than the start's is dropped. A coin the account's own network does not list is refused as `unknown symbol X: Hyperliquid's testnet list has no such coin (...)`, naming the network, where it said `unknown symbol X`. New `Action::UpdateLeverage` (hand-derived msgpack pins). MEASURED on the testnet account by this change's own testnet smoke (2026-10-26): the venue accepts the signed action, ETH forced to isolated 20x was switched back to cross 20x by the first order and that order was accepted, and BCH (mainnet only) was refused in the new words; nothing rests, the account is flat and the coin was restored. Amends decision 0181 item 6 and the 0174 open items (marked there, not yet ratified). **Still open:** the control door's facts for a `demo` account are the MAINNET list (the bridge's per-network catalog exists; the gatewayhub's `BridgeTrade` has to choose it per account tier), so 20 mainnet-only coins still spend one of the 16 extra-symbol slots before exec refuses them; and the venue's refusal of a switch under an open position was not provoked.

- **IG: a login now trades on its USD CFD account, not on whichever account IG made the login's default (IG bridge only; the one line each in the gatewayhub's facts read and its history lane's config only passes the account row's book on).** `POST /session` lands on the default account, so a login whose default was a spread-bet or a pound account traded on it, and the only consequence the operator saw was the node refusing to run it once an exposure ceiling was armed. After the login the session now reads `GET /accounts` and is moved, when it must be, with `PUT /session` `{accountId, defaultAccount: false}` (this session only; the login's default is never written; a switch to the account the session is already on is skipped, which IG would answer `412 error.switch.accountId-must-be-different`, measured on the demo gateway 2026-10-26). The rule: the account row's `venue_account_id` (`vike-cli secrets set-book`) wins when the login lists it enabled; else the default stays unless a STATED type, currency or status rules it out; else the one other enabled USD CFD account; else the login is refused by name, listing every account found with its type, currency and status. A spread-bet or physical account is never moved to unless the row names it. A re-login settles the same way and refuses to land on another account. Measured on the demo login: ONE account (CFD, USD, enabled), so nothing changes there (two reads at the login, no `PUT`); a switch to another account is UNPROVEN on any gateway (handled and tested over a loopback double, both with and without a fresh token in the answer). The facts source reuses the list the login read (still charged to its per-minute cap), and an epic whose `marketStatus` is stated and not `TRADEABLE` is named in a `warn` at the admission. A refused exec lane still rejects every order `venue exec thread unavailable` (the shared words); the name of the missing account is in the log.

- **cTrader trades CFDs of four measured classes: metals, indices, oil and commodities, and crypto (cTrader bridge and its facts path only; no shared module).** Until now every CFD was refused by name ("what one unit of volume means for a CFD has not been measured"). It is measured on 2026-10-26 on the Raw Trading demo account (hedged, USD) by `crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/ctrader_cfd_units_smoke.rs`, a raw-wire smoke that places a minimum-size market BUY per symbol and closes it by position id, thirteen symbols (XAUUSD, XAGUSD, XAGEUR, XTIUSD, XNGUSD, US500, DE40, JP225, AUS200, BTCUSD, ETHUSD, ADAUSD, PENGUUSD): the broker booked `grossProfit` as the price move times the filled volume (the wire counts hundredths of a unit) in the quote currency, times the closing deal's `quoteToDepositConversionRate` (deposit currency per ONE quote unit; EUR 1.1197, JPY 0.006355, AUD 0.70304) for the four foreign-quoted ones, to the cent on every row, so one unit of the engine's `qty` is one unit of the symbol's own measure (an ounce, a barrel, an index point, a coin; the wire volume is hundredths of it) and the lot size is not part of it: the engine needs no contract multiplier. `any_symbol_refusal` and `quoted_symbol_refusal` (`crates/bridges/ctrader/src/catalog.rs`, `MEASURED_CFD_CLASSES`) now admit those classes in the account's currency (a foreign quote through the rate path, as for a pair); share CFDs, bonds and the dated-futures wrappers stay refused by name, and `Futures Commodities` is now classified `Other` (a dated wrapper) instead of `Commodity`. The broker's margin runs 0.33 % to 20 % of notional by symbol and the engine's is one leverage; `GCQ26` (`Gold Futures - August26`, listed as a metal, not ticking) is admitted by class; the thirteen round trips are BUY entries (a short was round-tripped on XAUUSD and US500 only), and the bridge itself traded seven of the symbols on the same account (an off-grid quantity snapped to the grid, every close went by position id, the book was flat after each). Tests, red on the code that refused every CFD: `crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/offline/cfd_units.rs` over the recorded round trips (`crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/fixtures/ctrader_cfd_round_trips.json`), the fence tests in `crates/bridges/ctrader/src/catalog.rs` and the gatewayhub's `ctrader_answers_a_measured_cfd_class_like_a_forex_pair`. Words: `docs/ops/trading-any-symbol.md`, "cTrader: CFDs"; numbers and method: `crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md`, "A CFD's unit of volume".

- **An operator can place a stop-loss on a venue with no native stop: the node holds it.** `submit ... --type stop --trigger <px> --reduce-only` on a venue whose capability row has no `stop` (deribit, fxcm, dukascopy and polymarket today) used to end as `TRIGGER_UNSUPPORTED`; it is now armed in the core's book (no wire change, no CLI change), journaled with ONE additive key (`reduce_only` on the arm's record; no journal format step, so the previous release still reads the journal and restores such an arm as a plain stop). The node's recent events say `CORE-HELD STOP <id> armed` and that it protects ONLY while the node runs: a node outage or a restart gap is no protection, and after a restart (journal on) it fires on the first tick at whatever the price is. At the fire the quantity is capped to the arm's own account's live position and goes out `reduce_only`, or is dropped with a named note and a journaled disarm if the position is gone, so it is a covered reduce under the drawdown latch on the venues that ignore the flag. `cancel <id>` takes the arm id; the tick lane switches on by itself while such a stop rests (the profile's `guards.conditionals_on_ticks` is unchanged); a venue whose row has a native stop never takes this path. Also: the tick check of the conditional book no longer builds two `String`s per tick before it knows a book exists. `docs/ops/reconcile-on-restart.md`'s "A core-held reduce-only stop" has the limits (the mid, FXCM's 2 s prices, a Polymarket jump, no listing of armed stops), and its stale "conditional and contingency arms are not restored at all" sentence now says they come back from the journal. The fire also takes the reduce-only market closes already in flight off its cap (a flatten, a liquidation or a first crossed stop whose fill has not folded: two closes would flip a venue that sends no `reduce_only` flag), says on the ring which order carries the spent stop (`CORE-HELD STOP <id> FIRED ... as <coid>`, `UNPROTECTED` when that order is refused at once), and the tick check no longer waits behind the venue's default engine accepting the symbol, so a stop armed onto a labelled account's admitted symbol fires.

- **The control door no longer sizes a pair it refuses in the pair's own quote money (tradehub only: `crates/vike-tradehub/src/server/control.rs`'s `accept_command`, the two Preview surfaces and `crates/vike-tradehub/src/server/symbol_admission.rs`'s `foreign_contract_value`; no journal, engine, bridge or CLI change).** `vike-cli trade order submit fxcm EURJPY buy 1000 @168.490` on an FXCM EUR demo account was refused `order notional 168490.00 exceeds the node's policy ceiling max_notional_per_order 100000.00`, although 1,000 EURJPY is about 1,000 euros: the engine's grid lists no row for a pair it was never told about, the symbol door refused the pair (a ledger not in the account's currency, no account-wide exposure ceiling armed, no usable rate) so no value came out of its look-up, and the ceiling fell back to the engine's default value, `qty × price` in YEN, against a ceiling stated in the account's money (decision 0183). It hit every converting venue and every USD account whose door would not admit the pair (1,000 USDJPY at 157 read 157,000), and the door's own reason was never said. Now a pair the door refuses is refused WITH that reason (the ceiling is not applied to it, the door's refusal is said at its place in the order of the gates, and a facts source that answers differently a moment later cannot let it through unsized), a pair the door admits is counted in the account's money as before, an admitted symbol and the mounted symbol are untouched, and the Preview says the sentence the send says. A Bracket on a symbol its engine does not trade is unchanged (refused either way). Decision 0183, `docs/ops/trading-any-symbol.md` and `crates/vike-tradehub/CLAUDE.md` say it.

### Changed

- **OANDA: the practice account's instrument list is MEASURED, and it holds no CFD, metal or index (OANDA bridge, the gatewayhub's OANDA facts and docs only; no admission rule changed).** Read on 2026-10-26: `GET /instruments` returns currency pairs only (no metal, index, commodity or bond), and every one already passes the door's grid rule; an order on `XAU_USD` or `SPX500_USD` is answered `INSTRUMENT_NOT_TRADEABLE` ("The instrument specified is not tradeable by the Account") although `GET /pricing` prices them, so what one unit of a metal, an index or a commodity is worth cannot be measured on this account and their fence stays. OANDA's own pricing body values one unit of each CFD it was asked about at exactly one quoted price converted to the account currency (a valuation convention, not a fill). New: the captured list as a fixture with a test over every row, and `crates/bridges/oanda/tests/oanda_unit_semantics_smoke.rs` (a market round trip per class that prints the contract multiplier and margin, SKIPS on an account that does not list the class; its EUR/USD control measured a multiplier of 1.0000 and a margin of exactly units x price x marginRate). The refusal of an instrument the account's list lacks no longer says the list covers "FX and CFD instruments".

- **A non-USD account trades EVERY pair: the engine's mounted symbol is booked through a conversion rate (oanda, ctrader and fxcm demo accounts with the exposure ceiling; decision 0183, the mounted-symbol amendment).** Measured 2026-10-26 on v0.1.92 through the node on the FXCM EUR demo account: every pair except the mounted `EURUSD` was refused ("this account's ledger is not anchored to its currency") and the doctor said "balance held: stated EUR not anchored", because the engine booked the symbol it was started on at par in its own quote money, so a ledger could carry the account's currency only when that currency was USD (the pound account worked only through a one-row re-mount on `EURGBP`, which no euro account has: no regular pair is quoted in euros). The mounted symbol is now declared quoted in its own money with no rate and rated by the node like any other pair (a tick after the account starts, about every 40 seconds while it runs, and ahead of an order that meets an aged rate): the ledger is the account's real currency, the venue's balance is adopted, and the dollar pairs and the crosses (`EURGBP`, `EURJPY`, `EURCHF`, `EURAUD`, `EURCAD`, `GBPUSD`, `USDJPY`) pass at their rates. Until the first rate lands, and whenever a rate is older than two minutes, an OPENING order on the mounted symbol is denied `quote-rate-stale` and a closing one is never held up (nothing is booked at par). No journal format step, no change for a USD account (its snapshot and `state_hash` are byte-identical), the pound re-mount is untouched, the live tier is still closed, and dukascopy, ig and ibkr keep the mount fence. The engine commit is a MEASURED change (`vike-exec`, plus the new latency variant `fx-mount-foreign`): its the latency box A/B is owed. Deploy with the non-USD account flat: the first start relabels its engine and skips the journal restore once. A late login's EUR is not heard (switch `account.active` off and on). The operator's page is `docs/ops/trading-any-symbol.md` (the paragraph on a non-USD account).

### Fixed

- **Dukascopy: the venue's commission now reaches the books, once per side (the JForex sidecar only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/dukascopy/jforex-bridge` changes, and it takes the jar of the release that carries it).** Until now NO commission was ever booked: the node's balance and fee total did not move by the venue's charge (0.06 of the 0.08 a 1000-unit USDJPY round trip cost on the demo account).
