Measured on the demo account (2026-10-26, USDJPY 1000 and 5000 units, with the account's own base equity read beside the order's figures): `IOrder.getCommission()` is CUMULATIVE per order and NEGATIVE for a charge (0.0 at the submit, `-0.03` per 1000 units at the fill, `-0.06` at the net close), and the account's base equity moved by exactly the entry fee at the fill and by the realized profit plus the close fee at the close. The engine books a POSITIVE commission as a charge, and the sidecar's `commissionAdvance` read the figure as positive and asked for a rise, so a charge was never "above" what it had reported and every fill carried 0.0. It now reports the FALL of the venue's figure since the last fill of the order, in the engine's sign: the entry fee at the entry fill, the close fee at the close, a repeat, a rise (a reset) or a positive figure reports nothing, and the figure read is the new baseline. A closing leg after a sidecar restart no longer risks re-reporting the entry fee: an order that is already filled when the sidecar starts is seeded with the figure it carries. The sidecar also prints the account's base equity (`account[...]` on the `venue figures` lines, and a `venue account figures` line whenever the balance or base equity moves), which is what a drill compares the node's books with. Tests that fail on the old code: `OrderMapTest` and `NetCloseAfterRestartTest` (Java, `.github/workflows/jforex-bridge.yml` and the release run them; `just ci` does not). Not proven: a net-close after a restart live (the account cycle was allowed only flat), a partial net-close, a pair quoted in another currency than the account's, a `global` account. The node's equity still omits the day's realized profit (the engine's balance is the vendor's previous end-of-day figure, and a realized close never enters an adopted balance): `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`, the Dukascopy rows.

- **Dukascopy: a JForex sidecar that dies after `ready` is now started again by the client itself, with a bounded backoff (Dukascopy bridge only, plus the `DUKASCOPY` row of the venue-timings table; no jar change).** Measured on the the CI box node on v0.1.90 (2026-10-26): the sidecar died at 08:15:03 UTC (`bridge fatal reason=JForex session disconnected`; the JForex client had logged a server-initiated disconnect, then a connection problem; the reasons are in `crates/bridges/dukascopy/CLAUDE.md`'s "The sidecar is restarted by itself"), nothing started another one until the deploy's restart at 10:49:42, every order in between was refused as `bridge unavailable`, and `vike-cli trade doctor` kept saying `PASS engine dukascopy RUNNING at tier demo (the active row agrees)` for 2.5 hours while the conversion-rate refresh warned every minute. Every other venue's bridge owns its reconnect and the daemon rebuilds only IBKR's, so this bridge had none. Now one supervisor thread per client (`crates/bridges/dukascopy/src/exec.rs`'s `supervise`) kills and reaps the dead child and starts the next sidecar after 5 s, then 10, 20, 40 and 60 s (the exec `reconnect` of the `DUKASCOPY` row, which used to say "never a redial"), and never gives up while the client lives (a restarted sidecar that dies again within a minute counts as one more failed restart, so a venue that accepts the login and ends the session again is backed off like a refused login); a start that says nothing is cut at 25 s, a refused login is logged with the sidecar's own reason, and the next sidecar starts only after the dead one is reaped (one JForex session per login). The loop reads no account row: the account being deactivated or its tier changing detaches the client, and a detach ends the loop and kills a sidecar that was still logging in. While no sidecar runs the client is DOWN and says so (`SidecarState`, one `error` line, one `warn` line per wait and per failed restart): a submit is a terminal `bridge unavailable: the JForex sidecar is down (...); this order was NOT sent`, a cancel is now an `OrderCancelRejected` (it was a log line and nothing else) and an amend an `OrderModifyRejected` in the same words, and the price lane's wants are replayed to the next sidecar. An order in flight at the death is rejected exactly once (`bridge died: ...`), the netting shadow is shared by every sidecar of the client, and a cancel or amend of an order that was in flight at a death is refused by name after the restart, because the new sidecar has no memory of it (Java skips an unknown coid in silence) and would not report its fill. NOT fixed: `trade doctor` still reads RUNNING during an outage (the wire has no exec-link state for a venue; a shared home), a fill of an order that was resting across a sidecar death is not reported until the next fill's `position` line shows the size mismatch (a Java change: adopt open orders by label at `onStart`, emit a `position` line per instrument at `ready`), and a FIRST start that fails (jar missing, a login refused at boot) is still the live gate and is not retried. Proven offline over real child processes of the fake bridge (`crates/bridges/dukascopy/tests/dukascopy_restart.rs`; the production-policy test fails by assertion on the sources before the supervisor: no order is filled in 25 s after the death, 63 submits refused). Ships after 0.1.91 and is NOT yet measured on a deployed node. Live check after the deploy, under the lead's supervision (never casually on a node with a position): `pkill -f jforex-bridge` on the CI box and read the gatewayhub journal for `the JForex sidecar is DOWN`, `still DOWN: starting another` (`retry_in=5s`), `bridge ready` and `the JForex sidecar is BACK`, one new `jforex-bridge` pid, a 1000-unit USDJPY market buy sent during the 5 s window refused `bridge unavailable ... NOT sent` and the same buy after `BACK` filled; `crates/bridges/dukascopy/CLAUDE.md`'s "The sidecar is restarted by itself" has the full list and what stays unproven (a real server-shutdown window of the venue).

- **`trade doctor` no longer calls an engine whose venue path is dead healthy (Dukascopy's JForex sidecar; the node's lease worker, the gatewayhub's trade lane, one reply field on each of two wires, the doctor's engine row).** The owner's rule after 2026-10-26: a dead venue path must never look healthy. The lease to the gatewayhub stays up through a sidecar's death (its client restarts it by itself, the entry above), so nothing reached the doctor and `PASS engine dukascopy RUNNING at tier demo` stood for 2.5 hours. The exec client now writes its `SidecarState` on the process's price bus (`QuoteBus::sidecar`), the gatewayhub's trade lane states it in `TradeStatusReport::venue_link` (`TradeLane::venue_link`, a READING: it rebuilds no adapter, ends no lease, refuses no order and trips no dead-man; `TradeLane::link_watch`, which does rebuild, stays IBKR's alone because it would race a client that heals itself), the tradehub's lease worker asks that status every 5 s for the venues whose exec is an owned child process (`Wiring::SidecarExecNoRecon`: dukascopy only, every other lease is asked nothing, as before), the publisher stamps the outage on every observe frame (`WireSnapshot::venue_link_down`, written only while non-empty) and the doctor's engine row is WARN with the bridge's reason, the restarts that failed and what to expect: `RUNNING at tier demo (the active row agrees); the venue path is DOWN: <reason> (<n> restart(s) failed so far, the next try in about <s> s); orders are refused (`bridge unavailable ... NOT sent`) until its bridge has restarted it, which it does by itself`. Both wire additions are replies with serde defaults (decision 0112 verdict 3): no feature string, no protocol version, no journal record, and every old/new pairing reads (an older gatewayhub or node sends nothing and the row reads as before; an older doctor ignores the key); a rollback to v0.1.91 loses only the row. NOT covered: the loss of the lease itself (a gatewayhub restart, an IBKR session loss) still reaches only the core's `ExecLink` and `Disconnected` disclosure, not the doctor, an older node's silence cannot be told from "up", and the reading is as old as the last ask (5 s). The fold's hot path is not touched (the node-side work is on the lease worker's thread, the publisher's thread and the doctor).

### Security

- **The lock moves `crypto-bigint` to 0.7.9 (Cargo.lock only; the signing path through `elliptic-curve`, `ecdsa` and `k256` names it) and `deny.toml` triages four zstd advisories with their reasons.** Upstream yanked every 0.7.x before 0.7.9 (an unsound `NonZero` impl and timing faults), and `cargo deny` refused the yanked lock. The zstd rows are in `deny.toml` with the reason and the condition that removes them: `parquet` and `arrow-ipc` pin `zstd ^0.13`, so no update reaches the fixed releases, and both call only the one-shot bulk API the advisories do not touch. Ships in 0.1.93; nothing to check live.

## [0.1.92] - 2026-10-26

### Changed

- **cTrader: an order that would OPEN in a symbol the broker forbids is refused by name, with nothing sent (cTrader bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/ctrader` changes).** The handshake already decoded `ProtoOASymbol.tradingMode` and `ProtoOALightSymbol.enabled` and the bridge ignored both, so a listed-but-disabled symbol was admitted and then died as the broker's own bare reject. They now become a restriction on the symbol map (`crates/bridges/ctrader/src/trading_state.rs`), and `CtraderExec::submit` answers an opening order in a symbol whose `tradingMode` is `DISABLED_WITHOUT_PENDINGS_EXECUTION`, `DISABLED_WITH_PENDINGS_EXECUTION` or `CLOSE_ONLY_MODE`, or whose `enabled` is `false`, with one terminal `OrderRejected`: `ctrader: EURUSD is not tradable on this account: tradingMode CLOSE_ONLY_MODE (the broker accepts only closing trades in it); nothing was sent. ...`. A close is never refused: a `reduce_only` order of any kind, a plain opposite-side market order up to the open size and every order on a position book the venue has not answered for go to the broker as before, on a netted and a hedged account alike. A closed market, a holiday, short selling and exposure are NOT read (the proto has no "closed now" flag; they stay the broker's own `<CODE>: <description>` reject). ⚠ Measured by a read-only smoke on the default demo account (2026-10-26, no order placed): more than half of its listed symbols are restricted, among them forex pairs such as `AUDDKK`, `EURTRY` and `USDRUB` (the majors are not); the counts are on the cTrader crate page named below. An order in one of them that used to reach the broker now stops at the bridge. NOT solved: the control door still admits such a symbol (its facts carry no trading state; that is a change to the shared instrument record), the state is the one read when the exec session first connected (a symbol re-enabled later stays refused until the session is rebuilt), and what the broker answers to an order in each state was not measured. Pinned by `crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/offline/exec_symbol_state.rs` (red on `main`) and the live smoke `crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/ctrader_symbol_state_smoke.rs`; `crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` carry the rest.

### Fixed

- **FXCM: on the HEDGING demo account a reduce-only market order now CLOSES the trade facing it by trade id instead of opening an opposite one (FXCM bridge and its shim only; nothing in `vike-bridge-core`, `vike-exec`, `vike-core` or any other venue; it needs the new `libfcshim.so`: until a box has it, a reduce-only market order there is refused by name).** Measured on the demo account (2026-10-13/14 and again 2026-10-26): `MaintenanceType` reads `Y`, and an opposite `TrueMarketOpen` opens a second trade, so every close the core sends (`flatten`, `market-exit`, a reduce-only market order, a margin-call or budget liquidation) reached the shim as an open and left a locked pair (a BUY 2000 and a SELL 1000 left trades `B 2000` and `S 1000`, ClosedTrades empty), while the node read flat: the core nets fills into one position and reconcile reports each trade under an id the core already holds. Three optional shim exports (no ABI bump): `fc_account_traits` (the account's `MaintenanceType`; `"0"` is a netting account, as in the SDK's samples), `fc_open_trades` (a fresh bounded read with the open time) and `fc_close_trade` (`TrueMarketClose` + the trade's own ids + the side against it + the amount, the SDK's `ClosePosition` request). A pure planner (`crates/bridges/fxcm/src/close.rs`'s `plan_close`, cTrader's `plan_reduce` for FXCM) takes the trades facing the order oldest first and caps the quantity at what they hold. The owner's rules: ONLY a reduce-only order closes by trade; a plain opposite order still opens a hedge; a resting reduce-only LIMIT on a hedging or unreadable account is refused by name (its venue form, an entry order, was MEASURED to open a trade when hit, and the venue does not remove it when the trade closes); a netting account is unchanged; a shim without the new exports gets a NAMED refusal of a reduce-only market order, never the silent open. The close arrives as a ClosedTrades row, which the shim's listener ignored: it is reported now, under its OWN fill id `<trade id>-close-<closing order id>` (the core drops a fill whose trade id it has folded, and the opening fill carries the bare id: the class that bit Dukascopy the same day), and a close that needs several trades is one core order (partial fills, then the fill). A PARTIAL close splits the trade (MEASURED: the remainder returns under a new id with the old one as origin); the listener skips that insert, which would book the remainder twice. Measured on the demo and proven through the bridge (`tests/fxcm_close_smoke.rs`): a half close, a close of more than is held, the refusal on a flat account, a two-trade close as one order, a locked pair unwound trade by trade, and the old-shim refusal; the account ended flat. NOT fixed: a core-held stop or trailing stop that fires is a plain market order and still opens a hedge (the core would have to flag it `reduce_only`); after a partial close reconcile holds a `MissingFill` for the remainder under `quarantine` (never set `hybrid` or `synthesize` on this venue). `docs/ops/fxcm-forexconnect.md` has the measured steps, `crates/bridges/fxcm/CLAUDE.md` the rules, `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` the two rows.

- **FXCM: the bridge subscribes a symbol ITSELF instead of refusing it as "not subscribed for trading" (FXCM bridge, one shim export, and one row of the deploy helper; nothing in `vike-bridge-core`, `vike-exec` or `vike-core`).** FXCM's login lists the venue's whole Offers table (497 rows on the demo login) and holds most rows as view-only (`V`) or disabled (`D`); only a tradable (`T`) row ever traded or priced here, so the EUR demo login's EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/JPY refused with `fxcm: EUR/USD is not subscribed for trading on this login (subscription V)` until somebody subscribed them in the FXCM platform. The bridge now sends FXCM's own `SetSubscriptionStatus` (the SDK sample's request: `Command`, `OfferID`, `SubscriptionStatus`) the first time the node asks the control door for the facts of a symbol (and its conversion pair), the price lane is asked for a pair, or the exec thread is asked to trade an instrument: once per pair per session, bounded (8 s on the exec thread, 25 s on the reconcile session; an already tradable pair costs no round trip and a CLOSE never subscribes), only for a regular forex pair (enforced in the shim, so a CFD that reaches the exec thread is refused by name and never written), on the `Demo` connection only, and it only ever subscribes (rows it flips to `T` are never un-done; any cap on tradable instruments is unmeasured). A refusal is NAMED (`FXCM refused to subscribe <X> for trading; the venue said: ...`, `... is not known to have applied`, or the row's status after the wait) instead of the bare text, and an order on a listed but not tradable offer is refused with its status, not `offer not found`. MEASURED on the demo login 2026-10-26: FXCM answers in 0.2 to 0.5 s, every session of the login sees the new status at once, twelve disabled pairs in a row were never refused (31 tradable rows reached); a real account and any cap are NOT measured. An older installed shim keeps working and says in words that it is older than the binary (proof run against the shim installed on the CI box). **The shim reaches a box with the release, no hand step: `deploy/sbin/vike-trader-ci-deploy` installs `libfcshim.so` as a plain file row (`lib/libfcshim.so`, atomic, beside the SDK's libraries, backed up with the binary and put back by all three rollback paths; it was the one release tool the deploy refused to install, so a release that changed the shim left the box's old until somebody copied the new one by hand; seen at v0.1.61 and v0.1.62). The helper is root-owned and installed out of band, so the row takes effect from the first deploy after it is reinstalled, once.** Docs: `docs/ops/fxcm-forexconnect.md` ("How the shim reaches a box", "Subscribing an instrument"), `crates/bridges/fxcm/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`.

## [0.1.91] - 2026-10-26

### Fixed

- **⚠ The margin call and the drawdown latch of a MOUNTED engine run on the 30-second clock, not only on its closed bars (owner ruling 2026-10-25: «what if the candles are 4h, you will check once per 4h?? no, check once per 30 sec»).** Until now an engine a mount drives was judged only from `drive_strategy` on a closed bar (`sweep_margin_call`, `sweep_drawdown_latch`: every engine, at every closed bar of any series, never per tick), so a mount on 4-hour bars was margin-checked once per 4 hours, and a node whose every admitting venue was mounted armed NO clock at all: the timer behind `PriceOnlyConfig` ran for the engines of the price-only venues alone, and `price_only_config` built nothing when there were none. Now `price_only_config` is always built (an empty venue set is a clock and nothing else), the timer is `TimerKind::RiskClockSweep` (was `PriceOnlySweep`) and `sweep_risk_clock` (was `sweep_price_only`) sweeps EVERY live engine, and the closed-bar pass stays. What changes for an existing mount (the Bybit maker on a 1-minute series included): (1) its margin call and the account-wide drawdown latch are also evaluated on the 30 s interval, so a warning band or a breach between bars is acted on within about one interval (the real gap is the interval itself while messages flow and up to half an interval longer on an idle core, because the timer re-arms from the instant it ran and an idle core reaches the boundary on the waker's tick; derived from the code, not measured on the node: see the cadence paragraph of `docs/ops/price-only-venue-safety-plan.md`); (2) on the clock its margin call and its mount budgets price it by the price-only rules (every rung no older than the door's 60 s, no stale fallback) and SKIP it when an open position's price is older, said once per episode as `mounted-engine clock sweeps SKIP ...`, so a mounted engine whose only price is a bar close (no quote, trade or mark lane), or whose feed is silent (a restart, a deploy, an FX book over the weekend, an event-driven book), is judged by its closed bars only, as before; the drawdown latch does NOT skip it: it prices a stale mounted engine permissively, as a closed bar does, so a silent mounted feed cannot blind the node's latch to a fresh price-only leg that is down (and, since the entry below, no stale engine of any kind does); (3) a margin-call WARNING that holds is said once per episode by the clock (the closed bar still repeats it per bar), so it cannot crowd fills and rejects out of the 64-line recent ring; the per-mount budget latch (`max_loss` / `max_notional`) also runs on the clock, fire-once, its flatten journaled write-ahead as on a bar and CLAMPED (on a bar too) to what the engine's non-flat book still holds beside the reduce-only orders already in flight, so a margin call and a budget flatten in one sweep never close more than the position (the gate nets in-flight closes only against a flat book, and oanda, ig, fxcm, ibkr, ctrader and alpaca send no reduce-only flag to trim the excess), and a STOPPED account's mount is skipped by both passes (its flatten was refused and the fire-once latch spent); the open limits of the latch (not durable, a single shot right after a boot, a wick between bars) are rows of the known-limitations page; the clock sweep runs under the panic policy of a message: a panic in it (a journal append that fails at a margin call, a venue client that panics) enters the safe state instead of killing the `vt-core` thread, and the clock re-arms, each engine's margin call, the latch and the budgets under a guard of their own, so an engine that panics does not stop the margin call of the engines below it; (4) the closed-bar pass is byte-identical for a mounted engine (`config.price_cfg`); (5) NEW GUARDS: an engine that released a liquidation is quiet for one clock interval whichever pass released it (the clock would otherwise read the same breach again a few seconds after a bar did), and past that window the margin call NETS the reduce-only market closes already in flight from what it is about to send (the reduce-only orders of a manual flatten or of its own unfilled close: it sends only the quantity still missing, journals the clamped quantity, and sends nothing when the closes out already cover the breach), because the gate nets in-flight closes only against a flat book and oanda, ig, fxcm, ibkr, ctrader and alpaca send no reduce-only flag, so a second full-size close flips the position; (6) a core with no clock (`price_only` unset: the paper arm, tests, backtests) is unchanged. The liquidation is journaled write-ahead exactly like the bar's (`MarginCallLiquidate`, replay re-applies it; the drawdown latch writes no record on either path), re-application is proven by `crates/vike-core/tests/journal/margin_call_journal.rs` (a clock-swept liquidation of a mounted engine replays to the identical `state_hash`), on a clock of 3600 s whose waker never lands; ⚠ a PRODUCTION journal carries waker records (a core with `price_only` journals them), so `replay_offline` refuses it as `Unsupported` and the boot restore skips the waker records and re-applies the journaled liquidation, which is what that test shows and not an offline replay of a production journal; the clock tests are at the end of `crates/vike-core/src/runtime/tests/safe_state/drawdown_latch.rs`. The existing test `the_price_only_timer_liquidates_a_breached_engine_without_a_bar` pinned the opposite for the mounted primary and now pins this, and `price_only_config(&[], None)` is no longer `None`. Ships in 0.1.91 and is NOT yet measured on a deployed node. Live check after the deploy (read-only): the binary carries the clock's words, the doctor's `core` check reads PASS before and after four clock intervals, and the journal since the start shows the clock's traces; a healthy sweep logs nothing, so silence is the pass and not a measurement, and the one positive proof for the mounted half is the once-per-episode `mounted-engine clock sweeps SKIP ...` line naming the mounted Bybit engine, which appears only while that engine holds a position whose price is older than 60 s.

- **⚠ A stale engine no longer blinds the node-wide drawdown latch: the latch values it at its LAST KNOWN price, and the margin call still skips it (owner ruling 2026-10-25).** A price-only engine holding a position whose price was older than the 60 s bound made the whole curve "unmeasurable", so the latch acted for NO account while one pump was quiet. The two cases the owner named: an FX weekend (the book closes Friday 22:00 UTC, OANDA's EURUSD stays Friday's, and a 24% fall of a Bybit long could not trip a 20% latch), and a dead pump in an open market (2026-10-25 21:22 UTC, a 1000-unit USDJPY position of the Dukascopy engine with no tick for two minutes: `price-only risk sweeps SKIP the dukascopy engine ... the margin call and the drawdown latch do not act on it`, blinding the latch for every account). Now `drawdown_terms_in` always returns the curve and prices a stale engine permissively (the last price it had, which is what a closed bar always did for a mounted engine); the skip line, once per episode, says which engine, the age of its oldest marked price and, only when a latch is configured (`max_drawdown`), that the latch uses the last known value, with a WARN of the same words in the log (it no longer claims a latch the config does not have), so a dead pump in an open market is visible. UNCHANGED: the margin call and the mount budgets skip a stale engine (a margin call must not liquidate on a stale price), an engine on another network than its feed stays out of the curve (its seed and its PnL), and the skip is said once per episode. A STOPPED engine (mounted venue or price-only alike) is valued at its last known price without a line: its board never moves again, so the bound would read it stale for ever, and a loss is never forgiven by stopping the account (a stopped price-only engine used to make the evaluation unmeasurable for ever). Consequence: the latch can now trip on a loss priced from a frozen number, which can only repeat what that price already said while the live engines move the curve. The tests that pinned the blind spot (`a_price_only_engine_with_a_stale_mark_is_skipped_once_and_resumes_on_a_fresh_one`, the currency-group stale case, the tradehub rig's stale-mark test) pin the new rule. The cold sweep path only: nothing on the fold changed. Ships in 0.1.91 and is NOT yet measured on a deployed node. Live check after the deploy: the read-only check of the entry above; the trace is the skip line's new words (the latch uses the last known value), which a price-only engine holding a position with no new tick for over a minute prints, and the 130-second Dukascopy hold of the Dukascopy entry's live check usually makes one.

- **The margin call nets the closes already in flight, and each clock stage has its own panic guard (third review of the risk clock).** (1) A margin call asked for the whole excess whatever was already out: a manual flatten or a MarketExit (which arm no quiet window), or its own close still unfilled after one interval, was followed by a second full-size reduce-only market close, and on oanda, ig, fxcm, ibkr, ctrader and alpaca, which send no reduce-only flag, two closes flip the position. Each intent now asks for its quantity less the reduce-only MARKET closes still to fill on that symbol and side, the clamped quantity is journaled and sent, and an intent with nothing left is dropped, said once per episode as `margin-call breach COVERED ...`. A close that never gets an ack and is on an engine the stuck-order ladder does not walk (a further account of a mounted venue) therefore blocks the next margin call of that engine until it terminalizes (a row of the known-limitations page). (2) The clock walks the engines from the highest index down under one guard, so a panic at engine k stopped the margin call of engine 0 (the primary) for ever; each engine's margin call, the latch and the budgets are now stages with a guard of their own, the first panic of a stage enters the safe state and is logged once, and the walk goes on. (3) The budget latch's flatten clamp counted any live reduce-only order on the exact symbol, so a take-profit resting far from the market made the latch skip its flatten and leave the mount open; it missed an order that names no symbol (the engine's own); and on a hedge-mode book it netted the Long and Short buckets against each other. It now counts only MARKET closes, matches a blank symbol to the engine's own, and takes each side's room from its own bucket. (4) The stale-price WARN no longer says the drawdown latch values the engine when no `max_drawdown` is configured.

- **One execution, one record: a repeated fill no longer reaches the journal, `recent` or the ring (gatewayhub only).** v0.1.90 made an order's accept and terminal one record each and left the fills out: the history sentinel (five seconds after EVERY command and at every reconnect) re-lists the recent closed orders' `Fill` and `OrderFilled` and a stream plus a REST or replay path can report one execution twice, so a node's `recent` ring showed the same `Fill` line twice in a row (v0.1.88, 2026-10-25). The engine already dropped the second by its exec id (`seen_trade_ids`), so the books and positions were right; the journal and `recent` carried both. The first-wins memory at the gatewayhub account session's event door (`crates/vike-gatewayhub/src/trade/once.rs`'s `OnceMemory`) now also judges `Fill`, `OrderPartiallyFilled` and `OrderFilled`, and, because a fill is money, drops one ONLY when it is certainly the same execution already passed on that account, for an order the ring saw accepted: the same exec id AND the same order, instrument and side AND the same quantity and price (bit for bit; the fee and the time a replay restates are not part of it), in the same lane (the bare report and each wrap are three facts, each told once). Everything else passes untouched: partial fills (different exec ids), two executions of the same size and price, the same exec id with other numbers, another order, instrument or side, a fill that names no order of ours or whose order was never seen accepted, a number that is not finite (the commission included, because the engine refuses it before it burns the exec id). A wrap that overtakes its order's accept is never remembered, because the engine refuses it without burning its exec id and only the venue's redelivery after the accept completes the order. An empty exec id cannot exist (`TradeId` refuses it). The memory is bounded (first in, first out), per account, cleared where the order words are (a ring rebuild, an open without a replayable cursor) and also when the ring overruns an attached lease (a fill that fell out of the ring unread is recovered by the venue's redelivery), told of a new life of a coid (a Submit the dispatch thread admits), and the dropped repeats are counted in the session's retire line (`repeats_fill`). Venues whose replay wraps an order with another exec id or other numbers than their stream did stay noisy by design (Hyperliquid's loop wrap and its `orderUpdates` wrap). Proven offline (`crates/vike-gatewayhub/tests/trade_once.rs`). Ships in 0.1.91 and is NOT yet measured on a deployed node. Live check after the deploy: on the demo accounts, a market buy of the minimum size and its flatten, then `recent` at +1 s, +13 s and after a later command: one `FillEvent` per exec id and one `OrderFilled` per order (Hyperliquid's `OrderFilled` may still show twice, by design), the same for the fills the Dukascopy, OANDA and cTrader entries' checks make, and `repeats_fill` in a retired session's line counts what was dropped.

- **A market order the engine cannot price is now refused as `no-reference-price`, not `below-min-notional`.** Measured on the CI box v0.1.87 on 2026-10-25: the first market order of `hyperliquid#LIVE` (a labelled live engine that held nothing, so no price lane) read 0.00013 BTC (10.5 USD against a 10 USD floor) as worth nothing, because the engine had no mark yet and the lane opened 1.6 s after the order was judged, and the denial said `below-min-notional`. The risk gate now names what is missing when a priceless order (no price, no trigger) meets a mark that is not a finite positive number on a linear contract at that floor. The set of refused orders is the same as before (a limit or stop order, a marked engine, a covered reduce, an engine with no `min_notional` and an inverse contract keep their verdicts); the first market order of an unmarked labelled engine is still refused until the lane marks the symbol (about two seconds), and a limit order still goes. Decision 0198 records why the door does not wait for the lane (`docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`). Ships in 0.1.91. Live check after the deploy: the first market order of the freshly started node on the mounted Bybit demo engine (BTCUSDT, 0.001), sent before the engine has a mark, is denied `no-reference-price`, not `below-min-notional`. It reproduces only on an engine with NO mark yet and a `min_notional` in its grid, and a mounted engine usually has a mark within seconds of the boot, so the check may read NOT REPRODUCED, which proves nothing either way.

- **OANDA: the reconcile read of a fill names the order, so a stop of ours that fills while the node is up is no longer held as a `MissingFill` with `coid=None` (OANDA bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/oanda` changes).** Measured on the practice account on v0.1.90 (2026-10-26): a stop of ours, `b7oandabs`, filled while the node was up, and the reconcile pass held its fill with `coid=None`. The venue's `ORDER_FILL` transaction carries the order's client id at the TOP level (`"clientOrderID":"b7oandabs"` beside `"orderID":"82"`), and `crates/bridges/oanda/src/recon_client.rs`'s `parse_fill_reports` read only `clientExtensions.id`; the transactions stream already fell back to `clientOrderID`. The fill report now takes `clientExtensions.id`, else `clientOrderID`; an absent or empty one stays `None`, and the venue order id never stands in for it. The order report (`parse_order_reports`) is unchanged. That up-node `MissingFill` existed because a coid this process had not recorded keeps the venue's spelling `EUR_USD`, and the engine drops such a bare `Fill` (the module doc of `crates/bridges/oanda/src/symbols.rs`), so only the reconcile pass saw the fill. A `MissingFill` that now carries the coid changes origin (`Divergence::origin`, `crates/vike-exec/src/recon/types.rs`: the coid-less one read `External`, this one reads our own order's fill, materialized late): under `external-quarantine` it now folds where the coid-less one was held (that policy is the step the rollout rule allows next), under `hybrid` it folds as before, now under the real coid and without a synthetic `EXT-` accept, and under the default `quarantine` nothing changes except the origin it is reported with. Proven offline against the measured body (`crates/bridges/oanda/tests/offline/oanda_reconcile_parse.rs`). Ships in 0.1.91 and is not yet measured live after the fix. Live check after the deploy: on the practice EURUSD, a buy stop and a sell stop placed a pip or two either side of the market after an anchor round trip, one of them filling while the node is UP: the fill reads with our coid, in the ring or as a held `MissingFill` with `coid=Some(<our stop's coid>)`, never `coid=None` (it reads INCONCLUSIVE when neither stop fires within 15 minutes). NOT fixed: a fill that happens while the node is DOWN is never fetched as a fill, because the reconcile client starts its fill floor at the account's latest transaction when it connects, so the node sees a held `PositionDrift` and no order name (measured the same night, a stop fired at 00:06:25 UTC while the node was down from 00:05:50 to 00:08:20); the OANDA row of `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md` says so, and the floor needs an owner decision; the gap is the same for any reconcile client a RUNNING node rebuilds (a new client starts its floor at the account's latest transaction when it connects), not only for a node that was down.

- **Dukascopy: a flatten after a tradehub restart now reaches the node's book; a closing fill's trade id no longer repeats the entry fill's (the JForex sidecar only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/dukascopy/jforex-bridge` changes, and it takes the jar of the release that carries it).** Measured on the demo account on v0.1.90 (2026-10-26): a 1000 USDJPY long opened before a tradehub restart came back correctly, `position flatten dukascopy USDJPY` after it closed the lot at the venue (filled at 157.022, order CLOSED), and the node kept the long OPEN and the flatten order ACCEPTED with nothing filled. The sidecar named a closing fill `<order id>:<n>` from a counter that restarts with the sidecar, so the leg of the pre-restart order came out as the entry fill's own id (`<id>:1`), and the core's two fill-dedup sets, restored across the restart, dropped it as a replay (the bare fill and the `OrderFilled` alike). A closing fill (a net-close leg, a cancel that raced a fill, an external close) is now `<order id>:c:<client order id>`: unique across restarts, the same when derived again, never an entry id; entry fill ids keep their spelling, so the reconnect replay is unchanged. `NetCloseAfterRestartTest` replays the restart shape through two bridge instances (four of its five tests fail by assertion on the old sources, from the author's runs against them: the two restart-shape tests and the two tests that pin the cancel-race and external-close callers, whose old second id was `<id>:2`; the fifth, a duplicate entry fill message, passes on both), beside new `OrderMapTest` cases. The fix leaves the commission as it was: a closing leg reports the advance of `getCommission()` over what the sidecar already reported for the order, that memory restarts with the sidecar, so the first leg after a restart would re-report an entry fee once if an account charged one; the demo read 0.0 at entry and -0.06 at close on 2026-10-26, and a figure that does not rise reports nothing, so its legs carry no commission today (the known-limitations row has it). A node whose book already holds the phantom keeps it (the restored snapshot holds it and Dukascopy has no reconcile leg) until the owner clears it: the known-limitations page has the row. Ships in 0.1.91 as the `jforex-bridge.jar` release asset: the deploy installs the jar, and a box that keeps the old jar keeps the defect. Live check after the deploy: the jar's hash on the box equals the release's, and a 1000-unit USDJPY market buy on the Dukascopy demo account, held 130 s in ONE node session and then flattened, ends FILLED 1000 (not ACCEPTED with nothing filled) with the position 0, one `FillEvent` and one `OrderFilled`, and no `sidecar position line disagrees` warning. That check cannot reproduce the restart collision itself (it needs a second restart; `NetCloseAfterRestartTest` pins it offline, four of its five tests red on the old sources).

- **IBKR: after a restart the bridge no longer re-emits the fills of orders the host did not teach it (finished before the restart, or still open) (IBKR bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr` changes except comments, docs and one gatewayhub test).** Measured on the the CI box node on v0.1.90 (2026-10-26 about 00:08 UTC): every rebuild of the bridge (a tradehub restart) makes IB replay the WHOLE day's executions of our client id, and for each order that had FINISHED before the restart the bridge took the replayed execution as "recovered by its `orderRef`" with no symbol registered for it and emitted `[Fill, OrderPartiallyFilled]` again. Nothing was booked twice, but only by the SPELLING of the symbol: IB echoes the instrument of an overnight execution as `AAPL.IBEOS.USD` while the engine mounts `AAPL.SMART.USD`, so the engine dropped the repeats; an echo equal to the mounted symbol would have been booked, and a fill from the down time that should wait for the operator's `recon confirm` would have booked itself. The repeats also landed in the ring, in the gatewayhub's `recent` and in the write-ahead journal, where the owner's rule is one record per fact. The replay of an execution is now recovered only for an order whose symbol the host taught (the gatewayhub's handover); an untaught one takes the unroutable path (its commission is dropped, nothing is emitted) with one `info!` line per execution naming the coid, execution id, side, quantity, price and the echoed symbol, and a fill the engine never booked reaches the books only through the reconcile pass (`MissingFill` / `PositionDrift`) and the operator's `recon confirm`. An order the daemon DID teach behaves exactly as before. What it costs: the engine's order for a dropped fill is advanced by nothing (the wrapper that used to move it to `PartiallyFilled` by its coid is no longer sent) and stays `Accepted` at its FULL quantity, reserving margin and notional, because a confirmed `MissingFill` is a bare `Fill` and the IBKR reconcile reads open orders only. The same rule covers an order still OPEN at the venue that the daemon did not teach (partly filled or not): the learning still rebinds it (announced accepted, tracked, cancellable under IB's own id), but its fills emit no `Fill` and no wrapper, the replayed ones and the live ones alike, until the tradehub's own re-teaching names its symbol; its fill tracking still runs, so the fill that completes it is still final. Proven offline (`crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/src/exec/event_mapper_tests.rs`, `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/tests/ibkr_lifecycle.rs` through the real exec loop, `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/tests/ibkr_engine_fill.rs` into the real engine, and `crates/vike-gatewayhub/tests/ibkr_reconnect.rs` over the gatewayhub's ledger and handover) and measured LIVE on the the CI box paper gateway (2026-10-26, a lane build of this branch, not the deployed node) by the by-hand smoke `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr/tests/ibkr_untaught_replay_smoke.rs`'s `ibkr_untaught_replay_smoke`: one AAPL bought and sold back on a client id of its own, a freshly built bridge nobody taught emitted nothing for the finished buy and only an `OrderAccepted` for a far resting order it then cancelled, its taught twin emitted exactly one `Fill` and one `OrderPartiallyFilled` under the taught symbol, and main's mapper replayed the same two executions as four records under IB's echo (`AAPL.DRCTEDGE.USD` and `AAPL.BATS.USD`, pre-market); the account ended flat. NOT measured live: a PARTLY filled open order (one share cannot fill in part; the scripted tests cover it), and a deployed node after a restart (the check is one restart after a day with orders: no repeated `PartiallyFilled` in `recent`, one info line per withheld execution). Ships in 0.1.91 and is NOT yet measured on a deployed node. Live check after the deploy (read-only; the deploy's own restart is the restart): the old warning (`no submitted symbol is known for this order ... DROPS it silently`) is gone, the new info line (`replayed execution of an order nobody taught this connection`) names each replayed execution of an order nobody taught, and `recent` holds no `FillEvent` or `OrderPartiallyFilled` of an order that finished before the restart (it reads INCONCLUSIVE when IB replays nothing that day). The echo is the exchange of the execution: `AAPL.IBEOS.USD` overnight and `AAPL.DRCTEDGE.USD` or `AAPL.BATS.USD` pre-market, measured; the IBKR crate page and the gatewayhub and socket-gateway pages that named `AAPL.NASDAQ.USD` as the echo now say so.

- **cTrader: a `reduce_only` limit or stop on a hedged account is BOUND to the open position it closes (cTrader bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/ctrader` changes).** Measured on the hedged demo account: such an exit sent with no position (what the bridge sent) OPENED a position when it triggered on 2026-10-25 (a locked pair the node booked as flat); sent with the position's id it CLOSED it on 2026-10-26, and the venue does NOT cancel a bound exit when its position closes another way (a stale one opens a position). On an account the venue did not state NETTED (the account type is read at the handshake; unstated counts as hedged) a `reduce_only` limit or stop now carries the `positionId` of the oldest free open position it faces whose volume its kind (stop or limit) does not already cover, capped at the room left: a bracket's stop-loss and take-profit both bind the one position and two independent stops cannot exceed it; an exit too big for any ONE position is refused by name when several have room (one exit per position binds) and capped, with a warning, when only one has; a stop cancelled and at once re-armed binds; an amend cannot raise an exit past its position's room. With no such position it is a terminal `OrderRejected` by name and nothing is sent (never a plain exit). The bridge cancels every exit bound to a position it sees gone by any road (a market exit, `close_all`, the venue, the UI, a reconcile read in full), once (a cancel that did not arrive is re-sent after a reconnect), and holds back the engine's own cancel of the same order; the rows of exits that vanished during a reconnect are dropped, and a restart adopts the exits still resting on an open position (proved live); a market close's events fold into its order only when they carry no client order id or its own. A NETTED account, a plain limit or stop and every market order are exactly as before (a test pins the netted wire byte for byte). ⚠ Not solved: a bound exit that outlived its position while the bridge was down, or that an earlier build placed (cancel such a stop by client order id BEFORE the deploy's restart); a netted account, partial closes and an exit spanning two positions (not measured); a `reduce_only` market order against a book that tracks nothing can still open. Pinned by `crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/offline/exec_bound_wire.rs` (red on the refusal and on main) and the live smoke `crates/bridges/ctrader/tests/ctrader_bound_exit_smoke.rs`; the cTrader rows of `docs/ops/known-limitations-2026-10.md`, `crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ops/kill-switches.md` are rewritten. Ships in 0.1.91; the smoke passed on the hedged demo account twice on 2026-10-26 (04:13 and 05:20 UTC, before the release), and the node-level check is still to be made. ⚠ Before the deploy's restart, cancel every resting `reduce_only` cTrader exit that was placed with no position (`trade order cancel <coid>`): the restart does not adopt it, and a stop that triggers OPENS a position. Live check after the deploy, on the hedged demo account (EURUSD, the minimum size): a `reduce_only` stop with no position is refused by name; after an entry, a stop a pip under and a take-profit three pips over both bind and are ACCEPTED and a second stop is refused (`already has exits of this kind`); when one exit fires, or a market exit closes the position, the other leg is cancelled by the bridge within 30 s, no second position appears and no new held cTrader row is left after two reconcile passes.

### Removed

- **`vike-orderflow` no longer carries the public functions nothing called (43 of its 67; the owner said remove):** `BvcVpin` (with `VolumeClassifier`, `tick_rule_buy_fraction`, `bvc_buy_fraction` and `DEFAULT_VPIN_WINDOW`), `depth_imbalance` and `weighted_depth_imbalance`, `P2Quantile` (the whole `studies` module), `DollarBarBuilder`, `ImbalanceBarBuilder` and `RunsBarBuilder` (with `FlowUnit`), `CvdAccumulator`, `FootprintBuilder` (`FootprintBar` stays), `VolumeProfileBuilder` (`VolumeProfile::from_footprints` stays) and `bar_agg::backfill_before_id`. No crate, binary, script or fixture used any of them. The chart path is untouched: `OrderflowAgg`, `TickVolAgg`/`BarKind`, `FootprintBar`, `PriceBin`, `VolumeProfile`, the tick and volume builders (with their `from_trades` batch twins, which gate them) and `nice_orderflow_tick` all stay. About 1,800 lines gone, the crate's `vike-util` edge goes with the VPIN study, and no behaviour changes. Ships in 0.1.91; no live check (nothing behaves differently).

### Docs

- **The v0.1.90 changes are measured on the CI box (demo and paper accounts, 2026-10-25, between 11:36 and 11:50 UTC), and the pages that called them "not yet measured" now carry the readings.** (1) IBKR: with the extended-hours switch ON, a far paper stock limit order (`b9ibchk1`, buy 1 AAPL at 150) was ACCEPTED at once and the node's cancel ended it `OrderCanceled`, with exactly one `OrderSubmitted`, one `OrderAccepted` and one `OrderCanceled` in the ring and no held ibkr row and no `OrphanLocalOrder` (v0.1.88 and v0.1.89 had it rejected by IB with 10052 and held SUBMITTED for about 62 to 75 s); the overnight FILL was measured later, on 2026-10-26 (the next entry). (2) One record per order event is PROVEN LIVE: 16 far orders placed and cancelled through the node (Binance perpetual and spot, OKX, Deribit, Hyperliquid TESTNET, Bybit limits, IBKR paper) each showed exactly one `OrderAccepted` and one terminal at +1 s, +13 s and after a later command, and the registry ended CANCELED (on v0.1.88 Binance showed three terminals and two accepts, OKX three and two, Hyperliquid two and two, Bybit two); fills and re-listed `OrderFilled` lines are NOT covered by that change and still repeat. (3) Bybit's cancel word passed again on v0.1.90: a far limit and three far stops all ended `OrderCanceled`, with no `OrderExpired` line. The 0.1.90 Fixed entries below say "NOT yet measured on the deployed node" and that section is left as released. The pages are the IBKR crate page, the IBKR socket-gateway page, the gatewayhub and Bybit crate pages and the known-limitations page; `docs/ops/release.md` gains the v0.1.90 row, with the two CI notes (the first `ci` run was red on the one-authority gate, and the whole `vike-ops` suite was run in a lane before the second).

- **The measured facts of 2026-10-26 (v0.1.90; practice, demo and paper accounts) are recorded, each on the page that owns it.** (1) IBKR, the first overnight FILL: with the switch ON a limit buy of 1 AAPL was accepted with `outsideRth` and `includeOvernight`, IB's own order text for it was `OVERNIGHT + DAY`, it filled in about 1 s at 346.99, the sell-back filled at 346.92 and the account ended flat with no held row (`docs/ops/ibkr-socket-gateway.md`'s "Extended hours and the overnight session"; the three "pending" markers on the IBKR pages are replaced by it). (2) The restart leg (a clean stop of 150 s, 00:05:50 to 00:08:20 UTC): OANDA's fill during the down window is never fetched as a fill and its fill while up carried no coid, IBKR's fill that landed while nobody listened came back at the first pass as a held `MissingFill` with our coid, and the Dukascopy close after the restart was not booked; the OANDA coid, the IBKR replay and the Dukascopy close are fixed in this release (the entries above), the OANDA down-window gap is not (`docs/ops/reconcile-on-restart.md`'s "Restarting with the book left resting"). (3) cTrader, the raw-wire probe on the hedged demo account: a position-attached stop-loss and take-profit and a stop given the position's id each CLOSED the position (the first on a price-driven trigger too), and the venue does NOT cancel a bound exit when its position closes another way, a stale bound stop that fired opened a new short under the reused position id (`crates/bridges/ctrader/CLAUDE.md`, "A hedged account binds a reduce-only resting exit"). (4) FXCM: the demo login expired after about 32 days (written 2026-09-22, refused from 2026-10-24, the `User or connection doesn't exist.` of that day); the new demo login reports account currency EUR and lists EUR/USD, USD/JPY and EUR/GBP with subscription status `D`, so none of the three is priced, and nothing in the shim subscribes an instrument (a change that does is not in this release) (`docs/ops/fxcm-forexconnect.md`'s "The demo login on 2026-10-26: the cause, and the new account"). (5) The quiet-core latency reading, 24 of 24 passes at a baseline p99 of about 0.5 µs (`docs/ops/latency-gate-calibration.md`'s "The 2026-10-26 quiet-core reading").

### Internal

- **CI: the latency job's quiesce preflight finds every sibling runner on the box (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` only; no production code).** The preflight found the runners by globbing two named cgroup parents, but the build and test runners had moved into the system manager's `ci.slice`, so it watched 2 of the 5 sibling runners and a `gh-runner-test1` job burning about five cores (a dependabot CI run, 06:58 UTC on 2026-10-26) was invisible to it: a latency attempt would have been released onto it. One `find` over the whole cgroup tree (`-maxdepth 8`, under `timeout 20`) now lists every `gh-runner*.service` and `actions.runner.*.service`; the thresholds, the self-exclusion, the three clear samples and every fail-safe are unchanged, a `find` that exits non-zero is a `::warning::` and an empty result is still the `::error::` it was (`docs/ops/ci-and-lanes.md`). Ships in 0.1.91. Live check: the next `latency` job's quiesce step names the `ci.slice` runners among the cgroups it watches (`quiesce: cgroup CPU probe watching: ...`).

## [0.1.90] - 2026-10-25

### Fixed

- **IBKR: with `venue.ibkr.<tier>.extended_hours` on, a limit order on a stock is no longer refused by IBKR, and a refusal ends the order at once (IBKR bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/vike-ibkr` changes).** v0.1.87 shipped the switch with a flag IB rejects (found 2026-10-25; the 0.1.87 entry is left as released): with the switch ON (it is ON for paper on the CI box) every US-stock limit order went out with `outsideRth`, `includeOvernight` and GTC (the node's `submit` always sends GTC), and IBKR answered each within 3 ms with error 10052 "Invalid time in force:GTC" (5 of 5 on the paper gateway, v0.1.88, 2026-10-25), so on v0.1.87 to v0.1.89 no flagged order reached the market. The bridge did not know that code, so the order stayed SUBMITTED until the node's watchdog rejected it after about 62 to 75 s, the reconcile pass raised `OrphanLocalOrder` meanwhile and a second order was refused `account-exposure-unpriced`. A paper variant table showed `includeOvernight` is the flag IBKR will not take with GTC, so a GTC limit order with the switch on now goes out as DAY with both flags kept, and 10052 is an order rejection that carries IBKR's words. The notice codes (the 2100-2169 band, 10329) still reject nothing. Cost: such an order no longer rests across days, IBKR ends it with its session. The fix ships in v0.1.90: proven offline and on the paper gateway by the by-hand smoke `ibkr_flagged_tif_variant_table` (its last row: the bridge's GTC request went out as DAY with both flags, was accepted and was cancelled), NOT yet measured on the deployed node (the check after the deploy is one far paper stock limit order that must be accepted within seconds and end cancelled, with no `OrderCancelRejected` and no `OrphanLocalOrder`). NOT measured: an overnight fill (the session opens Monday 2026-10-26 at 00:00 UTC), IOC and FOK with the flags, and the paper user's overnight eligibility.
- **One order, one record: a repeated `OrderAccepted` or terminal event no longer reaches the journal, `recent` or the ring (gatewayhub only; the one other change is a knob of the hop test rig in `crates/vike-tradehub/tests`).** Measured on the v0.1.88 node (demo accounts, 2026-10-25): one far order placed and cancelled left `OrderAccepted` x2 and `OrderCanceled` x3 on Binance (perpetual limit and stop, spot), OKX and Hyperliquid, and the count grew with every later command, because the shared exec loop's answer, the venue's own stream row and the history replay (the gap-sentinel re-lists closed orders five seconds after EVERY command and at every reconnect) each reported the same fact and nothing met them in between. The engine folded the extras as no-ops, so the registry was right; the journal, `recent` and the CLI's outcome line were not. The gatewayhub's account session now keeps a bounded first-wins memory (`crates/vike-gatewayhub/src/trade/once.rs`'s `OnceMemory`, 4096 orders) in the gatewayhub account session's event sink (`crates/vike-gatewayhub/CLAUDE.md` names it), the one door every venue's order events pass before the ring stamps a `seq`: the first `OrderAccepted` that names the venue's order (the resolver's optimistic accept names none: it passes and is never remembered, so the venue's stamped cancel that resolves an UNKNOWN order is never taken for a repeat) and the first terminal (`OrderCanceled` / `OrderExpired`) of an order it saw accepted pass, a later one is dropped. A venue-stamped terminal of ANOTHER word after the loop's own synthetic cancel is a disagreement and passes once (so a venue's `OrderExpired` is never hidden behind our `OrderCanceled`), a Submit the dispatch thread admits starts a new life of its coid (the Submit dedup set is per adapter, so a coid submitted again after an adapter restart is a new order), the memory is cleared with the ring on a rebuild and on an open without a replayable cursor, and the dropped repeats are counted by class (`repeats_accepted` and `repeats_terminal` in the session's retire line). Fills, partial fills, rejects and modifies are not judged (a replay still re-lists `OrderFilled` and `Fill` wraps: the engine's trade-id dedup absorbs them). The fix ships in v0.1.90 and is proven offline (`crates/vike-gatewayhub/tests/trade_once.rs`) but NOT yet measured on the deployed node: the live check is one far order placed and cancelled through the node on each venue, counting the `OrderAccepted` and terminal lines in `recent` at +1 s, +13 s and after a later command (one of each is a pass; fills and re-listed `OrderFilled` still repeat). Bybit's second terminal of ANOTHER word (a cancelled stop's `Deactivated` read as `OrderExpired`) stays the Bybit bridge's cure.

### Docs

- **The measured facts of 2026-10-25 on the CI box (v0.1.88 and v0.1.89; demo and paper accounts, Hyperliquid on mainnet) are recorded.** (1) Bybit's cancel word is PROVEN LIVE on v0.1.89: a far limit and three far stops cancelled through the node all ended `OrderCanceled`, no `OrderExpired` in the ring at t+1 s, t+13 s or after another command, the registry CANCELED for all five (the 0.1.89 Fixed entry says "not yet measured live"; the 0.1.89 section is left as released). (2) A second `hyperliquid#LIVE` run (09:08 UTC, leverage 10x): a marketable limit buy of 0.00037 BTC (about 30 USD) filled at 80400 and was flattened at 80385, the lane held 1 s after the command, cost about 0.03 USD by estimate; decision 0198's "What it costs" and the tradehub page carry it, and the advice to use a limit order for the first order stays. (3) The duplicate-events row of the known-limitations page now counts the doubled `OrderAccepted` of three venues and the Hyperliquid testnet reading, and records the owner's ruling that a duplicate is an ERROR (one record per fact; it replaces the 0.1.89 Docs entry's "noise ... not a failure"); the shared fix ships in v0.1.90 (the Fixed entry "One order, one record" above), not yet measured on the deployed node. (4) The IBKR extended-hours bug above, with its variant table, on the IBKR socket-gateway page, the IBKR crate page and the known-limitations page. (5) `docs/ops/release.md` gains the v0.1.89 row, and says it has none for v0.1.82 to v0.1.87.

## [0.1.89] - 2026-10-25

### Fixed

- **Bybit: a cancelled stop ends Canceled, never Expired, and a stream row that beats the REST answer no longer leaves the order Expired (Bybit bridge only; nothing outside `crates/bridges/bybit` changes).** Bybit sends a cancelled stop only a `Deactivated` row, which the mapper read as `OrderExpired`; the node's own cancel answer says `OrderCanceled`, so one cancel put both words in the journal and the CLI printed `outcome: OrderExpired`, and when the stream's row beat the REST answer the order ended `EXPIRED` in the registry (measured on the CI box v0.1.88, demo, 2026-10-25). `BybitExecutionClient::cancel` now notes the client order id of every cancel it issues in `CancelNotes`, a small bounded memory shared with the private-WS decoder and the history replay (the gap-sentinel and the reconnect resync): a `Deactivated` for a coid WE cancelled reads `OrderCanceled`, a `Deactivated` for an order nobody cancelled stays `OrderExpired`, and a cancel the venue refuses is struck from the memory. Same-word duplicates (`OrderCanceled` twice, every REST venue's) are not touched: the engine drops them without a counter. Proven offline (`crates/bridges/bybit/tests/offline/single_terminal.rs`: the exec loop, the stream decoder and the history replay together over a stubbed REST transport); NOT yet measured live (the check is a far limit order and three far stops cancelled through the node on the demo account, run after the deploy).

### Docs

- **The Bybit double terminal is explained and the other venues' readings are recorded.** The second terminal of a cancel has three producers: the shared exec loop's own answer to the REST cancel, the venue's private stream and the history replay; Bybit alone gets only `Deactivated` for a cancelled stop. The known-limitations page gains a row with the terminal-word lines counted in the `recent` ring after a far order was placed and cancelled through the v0.1.88 node (demo, 2026-10-25 about 08:00 UTC; the registry ended CANCELED everywhere): Binance perpetual limit 3 x `OrderCanceled`, Binance perpetual stop 3, Binance spot limit 3, OKX limit 3, OKX stop 2, Deribit limit 1 (clean), Bybit stop `OrderCanceled` + `OrderExpired`, Bybit limit 2 x `OrderCanceled` (Aster not measured: its demo is mainnet). Same-word duplicates are noise the engine drops without a counter; they are not fixed and not a failure.
- **Correction to the 0.1.88 Bybit bullet ("a cancelled conditional order now ends in ONE terminal event"): the live read showed no change.** Measured on the CI box v0.1.88 (demo, 2026-10-25, 06:38 UTC): the node cancel of a Bybit conditional stop still produced `OrderCanceled` and then `OrderExpired` (three stops, and the CLI printed `outcome: OrderExpired`), and a plain far limit order showed the same duplication (cancelling `b8bybe1` printed `OrderCanceled` twice in `recent`, invisible before because both words are `OrderCanceled`). The registry ends right (CANCELED); only the journal line and the CLI's outcome word are wrong. So the decoder dedup of 0.1.88 (`perp_frame_decoder`) alone is not where the second terminal comes from: it has three producers (the shared exec loop's own cancel answer, the private-WS rows and the history replay), and Bybit alone gets only a `Deactivated` row for a cancelled stop, read as `OrderExpired`; 0.1.89 ships the Bybit-only cure (the Fixed entry above), not yet measured live. The Bybit crate page (`crates/bridges/bybit/CLAUDE.md`) and the known-limitations row say so; the 0.1.88 section itself is left as released.
- **Two live proofs of v0.1.88 on the CI box (demo accounts, 2026-10-25) are recorded.** (1) Binance names the fill of a plain order: in a clean tradehub stop of 150 s (06:41:53 to 06:44:23 UTC), two plain limit buys on the perpetual that filled while the node was down, `b8binpl1` (filled at 80508.2) and `b8binpl2` (filled at 80505), came back as held `MissingFill` rows that carry OUR coid (on v0.1.87 they carried `coid=None`), beside a `PositionDrift` (venue 0.003, book 0.001); the three unfilled ladder buys came back as held `UnknownOrder` rows, by design. (2) A far REDUCE-ONLY stop behind a tiny long (`b8okxfar3` on OKX, `b8bybfar3` on Bybit) is adopted silently at the restart and stays ACCEPTED, with no held row; a far stop that is NOT reduce-only is not a protective stop, and comes back as a held `UnknownOrder` (cleared by `recon cancel`): that is the design, and the page that documents the adoption rule now says so. The rows are in `docs/ops/reconcile-on-restart.md`'s "Restarting with the book left resting".

## [0.1.88] - 2026-10-25

### Fixed

- **Binance: the node names the fill of a PLAIN order (not a stop) with the order's own client id, on the perpetual and on spot.** `userTrades` and spot `myTrades` carry the venue's order id and no client order id, so a plain order that filled while the node was down came back from the reconcile read as a held `MissingFill` with `coid=None` (measured on the Binance demo perpetual on 2026-10-24: four held rows told apart only by price, where Bybit's carried the coid). The step that already names a triggered stop's child by id now also answers for a plain order of ours: on the perpetual the algo read answering "unknown order" means no stop shares the id, so the order's stored `clientOrderId` names the fill; spot has no Algo Service, so `GET /api/v3/order` by `orderId` gives it, and the spot recon client now gets the broker link id too. Only an id this node minted names a fill: a `web_…` id, another broker's `x-…`, a link id this node was not told and an order the venue no longer finds stay `coid=None`, and a fill that already has a coid is untouched. The per-pass budget (25 lookups), the remembered answers and the strict-then-unnamed failure rule are the stop path's. Proven offline against a scripted venue on both lanes (`crates/bridges/binance/tests/offline/plain_fill_naming.rs`); not yet measured on the live venue, and spot's `GET /api/v3/order` weight (published as four) is not measured.
- **Bybit: a cancelled conditional order now ends in ONE terminal event.** Bybit's `order` topic answers a cancelled conditional order with a `Cancelled` row and then a `Deactivated` row (measured on the Bybit demo host, 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-25, the last time by the CI box v0.1.87), which the node read as `OrderCanceled` and then `OrderExpired`: one cancel reached the journal as two terminals and the CLI printed the outcome `OrderExpired`. The decoder both pumps use (`perp_frame_decoder`) now keeps a bounded memory of the order ids it already reported a cancel or expiry for and drops a second one; the first terminal wins, so a lone `Deactivated` is still `OrderExpired`. The engine's order state was never wrong (its fold drops a terminal on an ended order), only the journal and the CLI's outcome line; the resync replay after a reconnect bypasses the decoder, so a terminal it repeats is still the engine's to drop. Proven offline (`crates/bridges/bybit/tests/offline/single_terminal.rs`); not yet seen on the live demo after the fix.
- **IG history no longer asks a chunk on the other side of a UK clock change an hour wider.** Each request now covers exactly its own window in the clock valid at it, so an hourly chunk costs one or two fewer points (the extra bars were charged and then thrown away). The 359 hourly bars stored on 2026-10-24 line up hour for hour with FXCM's on both sides of the 2026-03-29 change. Not yet seen: the change of 2026-10-25 (summer to winter); if the first chunk across it shows a hole, the extra hour comes back.

### Docs

- **The measured facts of the night of 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-25 on the CI box v0.1.87 are recorded, and decision 0198 is accepted (the owner agreed on 2026-10-25).** Crate pages and ops pages only, no code change: what a clean tradehub stop does to a resting order's fill by venue (a limit order is held and its fill comes back as a held `MissingFill`, Bybit's carrying our coid and Binance's none), operator stops adopted silently on Binance, OKX and the Bybit demo, the OKX stop that fires live ending Triggered then Filled under its own coid, the IBKR logoff at 84 s against the 120 s dead-man, the IG clock evidence behind the dropped widening, and decision 0198's first run on Hyperliquid mainnet with one finding not fixed (a market order as the first order of a labelled engine with no mark is denied below-minimum-notional before the lane delivers a price).

## [0.1.87] - 2026-10-24

### Changed

- **OKX stops are now restart-safe like Binance's perpetual stops (decision 0192: okx is the second venue whose client claims it lists its trigger orders).** After a restart the node judges a restored OKX stop by what OKX's reconcile reads. A stop OKX still lists is adopted (an operator's own stop only on a demo account, never on a live one), a stop that fired while the node was down comes back FILLED under its own client id (its child order's fills are named from `orders-algo-history`, and that read is strict: three failing passes in a row fail the fill read, then the pass goes ahead with the fills unnamed and one warning an hour, as Binance's does), and a stop that was cancelled while down is declared cancelled only after the three quiet passes. Before, an OKX stop the report did not list was held for good, and an operator's OKX stop was never adopted. The restart drill on the OKX demo account is owed after the first deploy of this build (its steps are on the okx crate page).
- **The desktop's Account window now says which account and which tier each row is.** Two rows named `bybit` (one demo, one LIVE) used to look the same; each row now shows its account and a tier chip (LIVE filled, DEMO outlined blue), the numbers are no longer cut off (`100000.…`) because the columns are sized from their text, and every order row names its venue, symbol and order id. The table uses the window's width up to a 960-point cap instead of the left quarter. Nothing on the wire changed: the account and tier were already in the node's snapshot.

### Fixed

- **A chart's crosshair price tag is no longer painted in the price pane's right margin when the pointer is in another pane** (Volume, an indicator pane or off the window). It used to land on the price axis at the pointer's height, on top of a tick label. A pointer inside the price pane draws exactly as before.
- **Chart axis labels no longer collide (the owner's rule: a price or last-value chip wins over the tick label under it).** A tick label under a chip is not drawn, a tick label that would stick out of its pane is not drawn, a time tag is kept inside the window, a last-price chip is pinned to the pane edge when the close is off the pane, a chip wider than the price gutter loses decimals until it fits, a window too short for the minimum pane heights drops the lowest panes instead of overflowing, and a narrow price range gets enough decimals that two ticks never read the same. Chart pictures with no collision are unchanged; only the label that used to sit under a chip is gone (12 golden files lose a bottom `0` tick, 11 lose a tick under a chip, one Renko picture now shows its last-price chip). The eight ignored size-matrix checks are now enforced tests, and new tests cover four and six indicator panes, a 1-bar, a 2-bar and a 100,000-bar series, and a window resized between frames.
- **The Trade window's reason lines are covered by tests** (no datahub, a refusing datahub, a datahub that serves other venues, and the read-only line when the desktop holds no control key) at three widths and two display scales, and the `07-trade` capture pose describes what the app really shows.
- **OKX: a stop that fires, and a stop the venue cancels, now end in the node.** Until now a stop that fired live stayed `ACCEPTED` forever (a held `OrphanLocalOrder` named it) because the bridge never listened to OKX's algo-orders channel; the bridge now opens a second socket on OKX's business URL (`orders-algo`), books the stop as triggered and its child order under the stop's own client id, and books a venue-side cancel (OKX cancels a reduce-only stop 1 s after its position is closed) as `OrderCanceled`. A stop that fired while the node was down is named by the stop's id in reconcile (the child's fills are joined by `algoClOrdId`) instead of by OKX's own child id. **OKX now claims that its open-order read lists trigger orders** (decision 0192, the owner's yes on 2026-10-24, before its live proof): after a restart an operator's stop on a `demo` OKX engine is adopted silently instead of held, a stop that fired while the node was down is booked filled under its own id, and a stop missing from the list is declared gone only after three quiet checks; a LIVE engine never adopts an operator's stop. If three `orders-algo-history` reads in a row fail, OKX's whole fill, position and balance leg is skipped for that pass (as Binance's is).
- **Bybit: restart restore is switched on and Bybit claims that its open-order read lists stops.** After a restart the node takes back the orders it left resting on Bybit: an order Bybit still lists is put back into the engine at the first reconcile pass, so the strategy that owned it can cancel or modify it; an order it no longer lists is declared gone only after three quiet passes (about an hour at the default lookback), never on one empty answer; an operator's stop on a demo Bybit account is adopted too, never on a live one. The restore smoke was green twice on the Bybit demo account on 2026-10-24.
- **A labelled account's position now keeps its symbol's price flowing (decision 0198, amending 0197).** 0197 kept a price lane open only for a venue's default account; a position on a labelled engine (`hyperliquid#LIVE`, the Binance lane twin) had no price source of its own. The lane is now held for any non-Alpaca, unmounted engine that holds a position or an order in its own symbol, the engine's mark is fed to the core while it is held, two accounts of one venue share ONE public quote subscription, and the lane is handed back about a minute after the engine is flat. `bybit#LIVE` gains nothing today: its own symbol is the primary mount's, which the mount already prices.
- **Binance: the node names the fill of a stop that rested more than 7 days, with no code change needed, and tests now hold it.** `allAlgoOrders` filters on `updateTime` and refuses a window over 7 days (`-4165`, measured on the demo host); the node never sends a window and falls back to a by-id read of the child order (`order?orderId=`, then `algoOrder?clientAlgoId=`; the child's `clientOrderId` equals the stop's `clientAlgoId`, measured). Four offline tests against a scripted venue that models those rules cover stops created 8-30 days ago, a refused history and the restore planner's reading. One warning string no longer says the REST spelling is unmeasured.
- **Hyperliquid: an order the venue fills in its own answer no longer stays `SUBMITTED`.** The bridge said `OrderSubmitted` and then `OrderFilled`, the engine has no such step, and the order stranded (`terminal event dropped on a live order ... SUBMITTED`, a held `OrphanLocalOrder`). The bridge now says `OrderAccepted` before the fill when the place answer is `filled`; a resting order is unchanged.
- **Binance perp lane twin: its price no longer reads as 55 years old.** Binance's best bid/ask carry no time, the bridge stamped them 0, and the price-only risk sweep judged a mark stamped 1970 stale however live it was, so the twin was skipped by the margin call, and the drawdown latch was blind for the whole node while the twin held a position. The tap now stamps the arrival time when a tick has none and keeps a real venue time.
- **A REST failure line now names what failed:** the warning for a failed venue request carries the method, the path (never the query, which holds the signature) and the venue's code and message, instead of only `venue` and `status`. The three `400` lines a restart prints for Binance are the venue's `-2013` answer to "is this plain order a stop's child?" and are expected once per own fill in the look-back.

### Removed

- **The chart's dead microstructure "studies" path is gone** (`studies.rs`, `ActiveStudy`, `ChartInputs::studies`, the study registry and 28 tests that only covered it): the desktop always passed an empty list, so no picture changes. `vike-orderflow`'s `Vpin`, `ImbalanceTracker` and `OtrTracker` now have no consumer in the GUI.
- **`vike-orderflow` no longer carries `Vpin` (with `VpinBucket`), `ImbalanceTracker` and `OtrTracker` (with `OtrConfig` and `OtrSample`):** no crate, binary, script or fixture used them (the owner said remove). The depth-imbalance functions, `BvcVpin` (which now owns `DEFAULT_VPIN_WINDOW`) and `P2Quantile` stay. About 680 lines gone, no behaviour changes.
- **The desktop's `VIKE_TRADE_SEED` capture knob is gone** (the env read, `plan_trade_seed` and its 9 tests, the settings-registry row and the hidden capture-fill-clock chart window): it could never seed, because its only call site passed a flag that is true exactly when the guard refuses. `scripts/marketing_shots.sh` no longer sets it; an exported `VIKE_TRADE_SEED` is now silently ignored. The `pipeline-3-golive` marketing shot now captures with empty order and position tables.
- **Dead GUI code and the tests that only covered it:** the feed-plane teardown that nothing calls, the Polymarket market short-name helper, three data-manager filter arms nothing ever sets, an unused order-id formatter, `WinState::move_series`, and the `2 + 2` smoke test (14 tests deleted, about 260 lines of production code). Nothing a user can reach changes.

### Added

- **IBKR limit orders on stocks can trade in extended hours and the overnight session (a setting, off by default).** The row `venue.ibkr.<tier>.extended_hours` set to `1` makes the socket backend send `outsideRth` and `includeOvernight` on LIMIT orders for stocks (market, stop, forex and futures orders and every order with the row off are sent exactly as before; the cpapi backend refuses to start while it is `1`). Turn it on for the paper account with `vike-cli config set venue.ibkr.demo.extended_hours 1` (applies at the next tradehub start; the gatewayhub journal says `ibkr: EXTENDED HOURS is ON for this account`). The overnight session is Sunday 20:00 to Friday 03:50 ET; whether the paper user may trade it and whether it fills there is not yet measured.
- **The chart is now tested at nine window sizes (640x360 to 3840x2160, ultrawide and tall-narrow) and four display scales (1.0 to 2.0)**: 246 headless layout cells with checks for overlapping axis labels, labels outside their pane, a tag outside the window and a stack that does not fit. Eight checks that fail on today's chart (a chip over a tick label in 142 cells, a tick half outside its pane, duplicate tick text and others) are kept as ignored tests carrying their measured numbers (`cargo nextest run -p vike-chart --run-ignored only`) until the owner rules on how a tag and a tick should share space. `scripts/qa_shots.sh` and the `export_png` example take a size and scale for dev-box screenshots.

## [0.1.86] - 2026-10-24

### Added

- **`vike-cli trade recon cancel <id>` sends one cancel to the venue for one held unknown order (decision 0196, rule (b), ordered by the owner on 2026-10-24).** Demo accounts only, operator only (no REPL word, no MCP tool), through the usual preview and confirm of `recon confirm`; it refuses a row with no id the venue can cancel by (a Hyperliquid order placed in the venue's own screen carries no client id), a live or paper account, and an id a registry holds. Success says "cancel SENT": it folds nothing and removes no row, the row clears at the next reconcile pass if the venue really cancelled the order. An older node refuses the verb client-side. On Hyperliquid testnet the bridge finds the order in the account's open orders by the id the row prints and cancels it by that client id; "not listed", "list unreadable" and "unknown coin" are answered as a rejection with nothing sent.
- **The `vike-cli trade` prompt's `submit`, `buy` and `sell` take stop, stop-limit and take-profit orders (`--type ... --trigger <price>`) and a named account (`hyperliquid/LIVE`),** with the same refusals as `trade order submit`; a bare venue still names no account.
- **`trade order submit`, `cancel`, `mass-cancel` and `position close-all` wait up to two seconds after the node accepts the command and print what the node did with it** (`outcome: OrderCancelRejected (...)`, or "not seen within 2 s"); `--json` carries it as `node_event` and `waited_ms`, and `--no-wait` skips it.

### Changed

- **`mass-cancel <venue> <symbol>` cancels only that symbol's resting orders instead of every order on the venue.** Without a symbol it still cancels the whole venue, and a strategy's own "pull all my quotes" is unchanged.
